proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group addressing governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance considerations across agentic AI systems[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group establishes standard operational procedures for recording topics, decisions, deliverables, and action items in structured meeting notes[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

# Lifecycle History

- Meeting note templates and agent recording workflows established[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-6fa126354b0b-2d7e8a4a][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-eb9c68e792e7-c6422732].

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group focusing on governance frameworks, risk assessment, and regulatory alignment for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk and Regulatory Working Group is an AAIF collaboration forum focused on mapping regulatory requirements, developing risk-assessment frameworks, and producing governance guidance for agentic AI deployments [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group provides pre-competitive analysis of existing standards and emerging regulatory regimes [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].

# Working Model & Deliverables

The working group operates on a biweekly meeting cadence and executes across a three-step deliverable pipeline [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77]:

1. **Landscape Analysis:** Compiling and reviewing existing standards, frameworks, and regulations across jurisdictions (including EU AI Act, eIDAS 2, GDPR/PII controls, and Singapore co-creation frameworks) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
2. **Gap Analysis:** Identifying specific areas where existing governance frameworks do not sufficiently address agentic AI capabilities and oversight risks [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].
3. **Distilled Guidance & Principles:** Formulating actionable principles and risk assessment protocols (such as probabilistic risk assessment) for human-agent interactions and organizational governance [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f] [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-19:** Inaugural kickoff meeting covering governance, antitrust rules, and chair nomination procedures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-a20272325759-501fd75f].
- **2026-03-05:** Formally adopted the three-step deliverable model and established initial workstreams for landscape collection [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-e39762d8063f-bb347f77].

proposed_concept.title: Technical Committee
proposed_concept.description: The technical leadership body of AAIF responsible for project lifecycle management, working group oversight, and community technical direction.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Technical Committee (TC) is the primary technical governance body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), established to assist the Governing Board (GB) with evaluating project proposals, managing the project lifecycle, and facilitating open-source technical collaboration [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Composition and Responsibilities

Each Platinum Member of AAIF is entitled to appoint one representative to the Technical Committee [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]. The committee is empowered to elect an annual Chair and Co-Chair [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

Key responsibilities defined under its charter include [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- Establishing, managing, and archiving AAIF working groups.
- Coordinating cross-project technical priorities and community vision.
- Recommending new project proposals to the Governing Board for acceptance.
- Managing project progression and status under the Project Lifecycle Policy.
- Recommending resource allocations for supported Technical Projects to the Governing Board.

# Decision Making and Voting

The TC operates primarily through consensus-driven deliberation and lazy consensus [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941]:
- **Lazy Consensus:** Proposals are deemed approved under a "silence-as-agreement" policy if no formal objection is registered by a voting member within 72 hours [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Formal Voting:** When consensus cannot be reached, decisions proceed on a one-vote-per-representative basis with a 50% quorum requirement for meetings. If an objection is raised against an electronic vote, a majority of all TC voting members is required [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].
- **Amendments:** Charter amendments require a two-thirds TC majority approval followed by Governing Board confirmation [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-03:** Formal Technical Committee Charter adopted [^evt-technical-committee-file-29954f63e09f-d9521941].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent observability, workflow-level tracing, and auditability across open standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) convenes practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to advance shared understanding and conventions for agent observability across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. It functions primarily as a coordination forum collaborating with existing bodies like the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context rather than establishing a competing specification organization[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on closing the gap between individual model call tracing and multi-turn, multi-tool agentic workflow behavior[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88]. Key mandate areas include:
- Developing the Agent Behavior Trace Model as a founding focus area[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- Establishing lineage, fidelity, and grounding conventions for multi-modal workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].
- Enabling vendor-neutral auditability, evaluation, and cross-framework observability interoperability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was initiated under lead Pavan Sudheendra[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-5cfc9888dc02-166f2d88].

proposed_concept.title: Case Study Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Submission guidelines for AAIF member case studies highlighting tangible business impact from open agentic AI standards.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation publishes member-driven case studies highlighting the adoption and measurable impact of open agentic AI standards such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose, and AGENTS.md[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

# Architecture / Specification
Submissions are accepted in two formats[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70]:
- **Written Case Study**: Authored by member organizations or featuring customer implementations, detailing technical challenges, solutions, and measurable impact.
- **Webinar Case Study**: Recorded 20–30 minute presentations with Q&A hosted across AAIF distribution channels.

Case studies are prioritized based on demonstrations of agentic maturity, open interoperability, or quantitative operational acceleration[^evt-foundation-file-d803a4dfa3ec-79586e70].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Landscape
proposed_concept.description: Visual directory and categorization of open source software, open standards, and member projects across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Landscape is an open-source visual map and taxonomy hosted at landscape.aaif.io that catalogues prominent open source software and open standards across the agentic AI ecosystem, including AAIF members and projects[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

# Architecture / Specification
The landscape is maintained in the `aaif/aaif-landscape` repository and generated daily using the `cncf/landscape2` compilation tool[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]. Ecosystem entries and category classifications are declared in `landscape.yml` and paired with SVG logos hosted in the repository[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

## Inclusion Guidelines
Entries submitted to the landscape must satisfy explicit community rules[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1]:
- **Open Source and Standards**: Listed software must be open source with at least 1,000 GitHub stars fitting an existing category, or represent open standards[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Exclusions**: Closed-source products and services, proprietary standards, and commercial packaging of open-source projects are excluded[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Placement Limits**: Organizations are generally restricted to a single entry representing their primary offering[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].
- **Asset Standards**: Project logos must be in SVG format with English text on non-reversed backgrounds[^evt-aaif-landscape-file-b33563055168-4c8ec9d1].

proposed_concept.title: Code of Conduct
proposed_concept.description: Community standards, expected behaviors, and enforcement scope for participants across Agentic AI Foundation activities and committee meetings.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) Code of Conduct defines the standards of behavior, inclusivity commitments, and enforcement scope for participants across Foundation activities[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

# Architecture / Specification
## Scope
The Code of Conduct applies directly to Governing Board meetings, Technical Committee meetings, Working Group meetings, Outreach Committee meetings, and other Foundation-wide activities[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

- **Foundation Events**: In-person and virtual events managed by professional events staff are governed by the Linux Foundation Events Code of Conduct in conjunction with this policy[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].
- **Technical Projects**: Technical projects operating under the AAIF umbrella maintain their own project-specific codes of conduct[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

## Behavioral Standards
The policy mandates respectful, welcoming, and collaborative conduct while strictly prohibiting harassment, discrimination, sustained disruption, personal attacks, and non-consensual disclosure of private information[^evt-foundation-file-ffdbe3a1e7ee-0ec44588].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Brand Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, stylistic, and messaging standards establishing a neutral, collaborative, and trustworthy identity for Agentic AI Foundation assets.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Brand Guidelines establish the foundational design principles, visual specifications, and editorial tone for all Agentic AI Foundation content, presentations, and marketing assets[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

# Architecture / Specification
## Brand Pillars
The AAIF brand identity is anchored by three principles[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b]:
- **Neutral**: Transparent governance avoiding single-vendor dominance or winner-takes-all framing[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Collaborative**: Cross-industry participation emphasizing open standards, shared ecosystems, and inclusive community language[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].
- **Trustworthy**: Credibility inherited from Linux Foundation governance, emphasizing precise claims over speculative AI hype[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

## Visual and Copy Direction
Visual assets prioritize a primary palette of high-contrast black (`#000000`) and white (`#ffffff`), supported by clear typography, balanced layouts, and grounded technical copy[^evt-public-agents-file-3a3a326b4277-185cd03b].

proposed_concept.description: Repository of modular, portable agent skill bundles conforming to the Agent Skills specification for AI agent workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Public Agent Skills repository provides portable, modular packages containing instructions, references, scripts, and static assets to equip AI agents with reusable domain expertise[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

# Architecture / Specification
## Skill Packaging
Each skill is organized in a dedicated directory containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter metadata and instruction prompts[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808]. Skills optionally include supplementary subdirectories:
- `assets/`: Static resources such as templates and logos[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `references/`: Extended technical documentation[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].
- `scripts/`: Executable helper utilities[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

## Interoperability
Skills adhere to the Agent Skills specification and can be installed via CLI tooling for use across supported AI agent environments[^evt-public-agents-file-4d647326e823-2a94f808].

proposed_concept.description: Public repository of modular agent skills, recipes, prompts, and testing workflows for the AAIF ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `public-agents` repository provides public, reusable agent resources for the Agentic AI Foundation, including modular skills, recipes, prompts, and agent-facing workflows [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7]. These resources support installable capabilities, repeatable execution patterns, and consistent operational guidelines such as the [Brand Guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md) skill [^evt-public-agents-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification
The repository is structured into modular resource categories and automated workflow test harnesses:
- `skills/`: Agent skills encapsulating domain expertise, workflows, and tool instructions [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `recipes/`: Repeatable multi-step agent workflows and task definitions [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `prompts/`: Reusable prompt templates and instruction sets [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- `docs/`: Supporting documentation for contributors and users [^evt-public-agents-file-b33563055168-20a6dfb7].
- Workflow automation: GitHub Actions workflows providing manual test harnesses for LLM endpoints, including `copilot-test-action` for GitHub Models [^evt-public-agents-file-b248ae41d1f0-0667ce2f] and `gemini-test-action` for Google Gemini models [^evt-public-agents-file-ae1d68d00103-0e76c626].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing security and privacy threat models, shared taxonomies, design patterns, and protocol integration guidance.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group focuses on security threat models, privacy-preserving patterns, and shared terminology across agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. The group collaborates across working groups and coordinates on protocol touchpoints including Model Context Protocol (MCP) security extensions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
Key deliverable tracks and areas of engagement include:
- **Cross-WG Taxonomy**: Leading the foundational taxonomy deliverable across AAIF working groups using an initial SP WG draft [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Protocol Security Touchpoints**: Monitoring and contributing to protocol extensions with security and privacy implications, including MCP Interceptors (hooks for data privacy and redaction) and MCP Apps (UI integration across browser boundaries) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Async Workstream Structure**: Organizing deliverables into self-directed workstreams with dedicated leads, transitioning general meetings into concise checkpoints [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Lifecycle History
The working group charter was submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) in April 2026, proceeding with workstream formation and taxonomy deliverables following informal and async approvals [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical oversight body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5]. It is responsible for reviewing and formally approving working group charters before groups are integrated into the foundation, as well as overseeing technical direction [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

# Architecture / Specification
The committee's responsibilities include:
- **Working Group Oversight**: Formal voting and review of newly proposed working group charters [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].
- **Cross-Group Harmonization**: Encouraging unified deliverables across working groups, such as cross-working group taxonomy alignment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0bd81720ed50-b38134d5].

proposed_concept.title: Identity & Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group advancing vendor-neutral standards and patterns for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and cross-organizational trust.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity & Trust Working Group (I&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) initiative focused on identifying and promoting vendor-neutral, interoperable standards and viewpoints for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Its purpose is to enable agents to discover one another, prove identity and context, demonstrate authority delegation, and establish trusted interactions across enterprise and organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group's charter addresses key focus areas across agent lifecycle and interaction models[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- **Agent Identity, Authentication, and Provenance**: Frameworks for how agents identify themselves, authenticate endpoints, and express provenance, operating context, and system software context.
- **Delegation and Authority Chains**: Mechanisms for representing agents acting on behalf of humans, teams, or services, including delegated scope boundaries and chain-of-authority validation.
- **Authorization and Consent Models**: Short-lived, fine-grained authorization patterns, policy constraints, and human consent or governance controls.
- **Trust Evaluation and Cross-Organizational Trust**: Approaches for evaluating agent trustworthiness and permission sets across independent organizational domains.
- **Agent Discovery and Metadata**: Standard metadata descriptions supporting discovery, interoperability, observability, and traceability.

## Out of Scope
The working group explicitly limits its scope to avoid overlap with other foundation initiatives[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]:
- Ratifying formal standards as a Standards Development Organization (SDO), though it may submit recommendations to external SDOs.
- Defining execution architectures or comprehensive security controls, which are coordinated through the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).
- Defining normative Responsible AI policies or general ethics frameworks, which coordinate with the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md).
- Building production identity infrastructure or operating certification authorities.

# Governance and Coordination
The working group operates under the governance of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and collaborates with the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c]. Leadership and primary coordination is chaired by Grant Miller[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-d22b3d6550c3-1096ec0c].

proposed_concept.title: Observability & Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent observability, workflow-level tracing conventions, and cross-framework auditability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability & Traceability Working Group (OT-WG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by convening practitioners, vendors, and standards bodies to establish shared conventions for agent observability, debugging, evaluation, and accountability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

Rather than operating as a competing standards body, the working group functions primarily as a coordination forum that aligns existing specifications (such as the OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, and W3C Trace Context) and produces new guidance or specifications only when an unaddressed gap exists[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

# Architecture / Specification

## Purpose and Problem Space
The working group addresses three primary industry challenges[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d]:
- **Fragmented observability landscape:** Incompatible trace formats and schemas across proprietary platforms risk vendor lock-in and prevent cross-framework observability.
- **Gap between LLM call tracing and agent-level understanding:** Tracing individual model calls does not provide visibility into multi-turn, multi-tool, workflow-level agent behaviors.
- **Agent accountability:** Enterprises require reliable auditing, evaluation, and lineage tracing for autonomous and multi-modal agent workflows.

## Core Principles
- **Coordinate first, specify only when necessary:** Prioritize extending existing standards and upstreaming contributions.
- **Interoperability over innovation:** Ensure solutions compose with existing industry telemetry.
- **Observable by default:** Enable out-of-the-box visibility across agentic architectures.
- **Vendor and framework neutrality:** Ensure outputs do not favor specific commercial vendors or frameworks.

# Governance and Leadership
- **Short Name / Acronym:** OT-WG
- **Primary Contact / Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra
- **Charter Ratification:** Ratified by WG on April 15, 2026; approved on May 13, 2026[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-eee95d3f1c5a-c232597d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security & Privacy Working Group (SPAA) establishes security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem by producing open threat models, taxonomies, and reference architecture design patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

SPAA serves as an intersecting foundational layer across all AAIF working groups, helping providers and consumers address risks unique to autonomous systems—such as prompt injection, confused deputy attacks, authorization boundary violations, tool invocation risks, and memory vulnerabilities[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope
- **In Scope:** Threat modeling and attack analysis, security architecture and design patterns, agent control and containment, data protection and privacy, and cross-working-group collaboration[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].
- **Out of Scope:** Ethics, bias, and normative value judgments (handled by [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)); prescriptive regulatory compliance; and direct product certification programs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

## Assumptions and Dependencies
- Operates under the assumption that safety and risk management is a shared responsibility across the entire agentic AI software stack.
- Relies on peer AAIF working groups for shared foundation glossaries and co-authored cross-domain specifications.

# Governance and Leadership
- **Short Name / Acronym:** SPAA (Security & Privacy for Agentic AI)
- **Primary Contact / Chair:** Alex Frazer
- **Charter Approval:** Approved on May 13, 2026[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ef737899].

proposed_concept.title: AAIF Blog Content Intake Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Editorial standards, eligibility rules, and intake submission workflows for the Agentic AI Foundation blog.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Blog Guidelines establish the editorial standards, contributor eligibility, topic scope, and submission procedures for publishing articles, project releases, and thought leadership on aaif.io[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

The Linux Foundation and AAIF teams manage end-to-end editorial triage, review, scheduling, and publication to ensure content is educational, timely, and vendor-neutral[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Permitted Topics
AAIF prioritizes narrative-driven content covering[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c]:
- Release announcements and updates for AAIF-hosted projects (e.g., MCP, goose, AGENTS.md).
- Technical guides, tutorials, and integration architectures involving agentic AI tooling.
- Production case studies and real-world deployment lessons.
- Thought leadership on agent interoperability, standards, and community milestones.

## Contributor Eligibility
- **Member Companies:** Submissions must remain vendor-neutral, with commercial mentions restricted to one or two closing sentences with a single external link[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Project Maintainers & Working Groups:** Direct updates, roadmaps, and technical deep-dives authored by AAIF working groups or the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].
- **Community Contributors:** Educational articles and tutorials, limited to two submissions per month per author[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

## Submission and Lead Times
- Articles must be original, previously unpublished, and approved by stakeholder reviewers prior to intake[^evt-foundation-file-d56154a3412d-c180d87c].

- Contributors can utilize the `aaif-blog-guidelines` skill from [Public Agent Skills](../resources/public-agent-skills.md) to draft, review, and format submissions[^evt-public-agents-file-2aebb9feb4df-f97f79ed][^evt-foundation-pr-2].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security taxonomies, hook standardization, and privacy design patterns for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (S&P WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group establishing shared threat models, security architectures, agent containment patterns, and privacy best practices across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. The group addresses risks unique to agentic workflows, including multi-agent persuasion, autonomous tool invocation, delegated authentication, agent memory protection, goal drift, cascading failures, and prompt injection[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

The working group operates under the technical oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and liaises with peer groups including the [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) and the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Technical Focus

The working group's scope covers technical disciplines essential for securing autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]:
- **Threat Modeling and Risk Taxonomy**: Mapping agentic attack surfaces, multi-agent failure modes, and red-teaming methodologies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
- **Agent Control and Containment**: Defining standards for human-in-the-loop (HITL) checkpoints, least-privilege tool execution, and runtime interceptors or protocol hooks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Data Protection and Memory Privacy**: Establishing privacy design patterns for agent memory stores, context retention, and multi-tenant isolation[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].
- **Cross-WG Security Reviews**: Publishing review checklists to embed security reviews early into sister working group deliverables[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

Explicitly excluded from scope are subjective ethical considerations, legal interpretation of regulatory frameworks, and formal third-party certification programs[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1].

## Active Deliverables

Workstreams operate asynchronously with focused coordination channels and report into regular all-hands meetings[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab]:
1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Primary near-term deliverable analyzing agentic threat models and framework gaps[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
2. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Technical catalog outlining patterns (e.g., hooks, checkpoints) and security anti-patterns[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
3. **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level prescriptive security guidance paired with the design patterns catalog[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security & Privacy Review Checklist**: Baseline checklist for cross-WG alignment during specification drafting[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
5. **Taxonomy Contribution**: The group's foundational taxonomy draft was transitioned into an AAIF-wide cross-working-group initiative[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

# Lifecycle History

- **Charter and Governance**: Initial draft charter established leadership roles (Chair Alex Frazer, Co-Chair Junjie Bu), 12-month terms (capped at 2 consecutive terms), 51% quorum rules, and open IP licensing (Apache-2.0/MIT for code, CC-BY-4.0/CC-BY-SA 4.0 for docs, DCO contribution policy)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-1]. Formal voting was routed through the Linux Foundation LFX platform[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].
- **Ecosystem Outreach**: The WG engages with adjacent standards bodies and specifications, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP) ACS group on hooks standardization, MCP Apps, and Vanta's AARM standard to drive cohesive industry recommendations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-973e1f067b5c-2436c8ab].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Client Protocol
proposed_concept.description: Open standard for communication between code editors or IDEs and AI coding agents over JSON-RPC or HTTP/WebSocket.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Client Protocol (ACP) is an open communication standard designed to connect code editors and integrated development environments (IDEs) with AI coding agents[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]. Co-developed by Zed Industries and JetBrains, ACP decouples coding agents from editors, addressing the M×N integration problem where each client previously required custom implementations for every agent[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Architecture / Specification
ACP standardizes the client-agent interaction layer and complements the Model Context Protocol (MCP)[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]. While MCP focuses on model-to-tool and data connectivity, ACP handles session UX and editor interactions[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

Key technical characteristics include:
- **Transport Layers**: Local agent support via JSON-RPC over standard I/O (`stdio`), and remote agent support via HTTP and WebSocket protocols[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **MCP Interoperability**: Reuses MCP JSON representations and allows client applications to configure MCP servers for connected agents[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].
- **Ecosystem Adoption**: Implemented natively or via plugins across editors such as Zed, JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, and Emacs, as well as agents like Goose, Augment Code, Cline, and OpenHands[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

# Lifecycle History
ACP was proposed as an AAIF project under the Apache 2.0 license and submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) for consideration[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1]. Specification changes are managed through a public Request for Dialog (RFD) process[^evt-project-proposals-issue-1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal governance framework for open technical projects joining AAIF, progressing through lifecycle stages, and undergoing annual reviews [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Architecture / Specification
## Lifecycle Stages
Projects within AAIF are classified into three defined stages [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- **Growth Stage**: Intake level for projects demonstrating community growth, active technical contribution, and alignment with AAIF objectives.
- **Impact Stage**: Advanced tier for established, widely adopted projects featuring multi-organization governance and sustained operational maturity.
- **Emeritus Stage**: End-of-cycle stage for projects that are no longer actively maintained [^evt-project-proposals-pr-30].

## Proposal Requirements
Project submissions are managed through the AAIF project proposals repository and must supply [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171]:
- Alignment statement with the AAIF mission and integration points with existing projects.
- OSI-approved permissive open source licensing.
- Public repository location, automated CI/CD release processes, and public issue tracking.
- Documented governance (`GOVERNANCE.md`), core maintainers list, and decision-making structures.
- Optional Technical Committee mentor sponsorship.

## Annual Review Process
Projects participate in periodic annual reviews conducted by foundation leadership to evaluate project vitality, ensure governance compliance, and approve stage transitions [^evt-project-proposals-file-8f732085cd4f-08f3b171].

# Overview
The Working Group Idea Submission Guidelines outline the intake process and requirements for establishing structured, time-bound Working Groups within the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

# Architecture / Specification
## Eligibility and Structure
Working Group proposals are accepted exclusively from AAIF member organizations in good standing across all membership tiers; submissions from non-members are not evaluated [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]. Working Groups operate on a typical 12–24 month charter cycle [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a].

## Proposal Components
Working Group submissions must include the following sections [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-67593d7c0dc3-63aded6a]:
- **Submitter Information**: Submitter identity, organizational affiliation, and leadership commitment.
- **Working Group Identity**: Plain-language group name and concise summary.
- **Problem Statement & Purpose**: Core problem description, agentic AI relevance, and foundation alignment.
- **Scope & Deliverables**: Proposed outputs including technical reports, standards, benchmarks, or guidance documents.
- **Timeline & Structure**: Target milestones, meeting frequency, and estimated duration.
- **Membership & Expertise**: Identified stakeholder groups and confirmed participant commitments.

The Social Media Governance and Guidelines define content standards, channel management, and contribution mechanisms administered by Linux Foundation staff for AAIF channels [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

# Architecture / Specification

Official social communication maintains a neutral, inclusive, professional, and vendor-neutral voice [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:
- **X**: Release notes, event announcements, and short technical updates.
- **LinkedIn**: Technical case studies, milestone summaries, and business discussions.

## Content Intake and Reposting Rules
Content is accepted and evaluated through two specific submission pathways [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637]:

Generic commercial promotions, vendor advertisements, and personal blogs are not permitted for official Foundation reposting [^evt-foundation-file-135a8fc4e3c5-bc2ab637].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging and aligning open specifications, interfaces, and reference architectures for agent-driven commerce workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (AC WG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group tasked with cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, reference models, and terminology for commerce workflows executed by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]. The group serves as a protocol-neutral forum rather than an author of competing commerce protocols, focusing on interoperability across discovery, checkout, payment orchestration, and post-purchase interactions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its domain across seven key commerce lifecycle stages and boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be]:
- **Discovery & Negotiation**: Interfaces between agents and merchants for catalog queries, dynamic offers, availability checks, and fulfillment terms.
- **Cart & Checkout**: Structured payloads for cart composition, validation, and transaction handoffs.
- **Identity & Delegated Authority**: Buyer identity verification, agent authority scoping, and consent conveyance in collaboration with the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md).
- **Agentic Payments**: Interfaces connecting agents, wallets, and payment networks (cards, real-time rails, and on-chain systems), covering intent, authorization, and settlement signals without specifying operational rail mechanics.
- **Fraud Signaling**: Exchange of risk-posture signals among agents, merchants, and fraud platforms.
- **Autonomy Boundaries & Human-in-the-Loop**: Conventions for step-up confirmations, escalations, and explicit autonomy-level declarations.
- **Post-Purchase Interfaces**: Signals for order status updates, claims, chargebacks, and dispute initiation.

Operational mechanics of specific payment rails, fraud mitigation algorithms, proprietary marketplace implementations, and end-user hardware are explicitly out of scope[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-15**: Working group charter approved under the leadership of co-chairs Ilya Grigorik and Rahul Bansal[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-d22b3d6550c3-4eccf8be].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation working group establishing shared threat models, security taxonomies, hook standardization, and privacy best practices for autonomous agent architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]. The working group provides cross-cutting security patterns, gap analyses, and review checklists to help foundation projects identify and mitigate risks across agent execution lifecycles[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group coordinates several core deliverable workstreams[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9]:
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream**: Cross-working-group initiative surveying ecosystem tools, frameworks, and security taxonomies, co-chaired with Foundation taxonomy efforts.
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Structured gap analysis evaluating agent-specific threat vectors, autonomy escalations, and runtime execution boundaries.
- **Agentic Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive recommendations for securing autonomous agent deployments and runtime components.
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable architectural patterns for privacy-preserving and secure multi-agent coordination.
- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Standardized review rubric for evaluating security posture across sibling working group outputs and proposals.

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-05-26**: Charter formally approved; Junjie Bu appointed co-chair of Taxonomy and chair of Landscape workstreams; workstream leadership structured via contributor self-selection[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3748d0afcd04-6e6b36e9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the governance framework, stage classifications, intake procedures, and review standards for open source projects hosted under the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]. It outlines how candidate projects apply for admission, undergo review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), and progress through project lifecycle stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Application and Intake Process
Prospective foundation projects apply by submitting a structured Project Proposal Application via the AAIF project proposals intake repository[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6][^evt-project-proposals-pr-35]. Submitted applications enter a public backlog tracked on the Project Proposals Board through predefined intake stages[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- `New`: Newly submitted application placed in the backlog for triage.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Reviewers have requested additional technical or governance details.
- `Too Early`: The project does not currently meet maturity requirements; guidance for reapplication is provided.
- `Approved`: The project is accepted into the foundation-hosted structure.
- `Declined`: The application is rejected with recorded rationale.

Rejected projects may reapply after addressing reviewer feedback, with reapplication permitted as soon as 3 months following a declined vote if tangible progress is demonstrated[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6].

## Review and Voting Governance
Project applications are formally evaluated by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- Applicants prepare a review presentation supported by AAIF staff for a scheduled Technical Committee meeting.
- The Technical Committee classifies the candidate project as either a **Growth** or **Impact** project.
- Approval requires an absolute majority vote (>50%) of all Technical Committee members before referral to the Governing Board for final ratification.

## Membership Independence
AAIF project hosting is decoupled from foundation corporate membership[^evt-project-proposals-file-b33563055168-aa8532b6]:
- Contributing organizations are not required to be AAIF member organizations to submit or host projects.
- Acceptance of a hosted project does not confer corporate membership tiers (such as Silver, Gold, or Platinum) or grant a seat on the AAIF Governing Board.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (GRRA WG) serves as a bridge between global AI policy developments and technical advancements in agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]. It addresses gaps in regulatory guidance, standards, and policy frameworks to ensure safe adoption of open source agentic AI projects [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Scope and Focus Areas

The working group's primary responsibilities and areas of investigation include [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0]:
- **Regulatory Monitoring:** Tracking emerging global AI regulations, policies, and standard frameworks affecting agentic systems.
- **Protocol Governance:** Examining organizational governance implementations of agent protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP).
- **Technical Governance Specifications:** Exploring formal methods for reversibility characterization, undo infrastructure, and Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) control patterns.
- **AI Agent Bill of Materials (AABOM):** Developing specifications covering models, scaffolding, tools, APIs, and third-party component provenance.
- **Risk Assessment:** Establishing risk classification schemas, deployment frameworks, incident reporting guidelines, and agent discovery policies.
- **Vertical Alignment:** Evaluating specifications from domain-specific frameworks, such as the FINOS AI Governance Framework.

## Out of Scope

The working group explicitly does not provide legal advice, develop commercial compliance solutions, or endorse specific commercial vendors [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0].

# Lifecycle History

The draft charter was authored under lead contact Ryan Hagemann and submitted for Technical Committee review [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-d22b3d6550c3-a860a9f0][^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-pr-1].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Working Group Submission Guidelines establish the formal intake process and evaluation requirements for proposing new Working Groups under the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]. Proposals are submitted via structured issue templates, triaged onto the Working Group Proposals Board, and evaluated by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

# Architecture / Specification

## Submission and Intake Process

1. **Application Submission:** Submitters complete a standardized proposal application form in the `aaif/working-group-proposals` repository [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
2. **Backlog Triage:** Newly submitted proposals enter the backlog and are tracked on the public project board [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].
3. **TC Review and Scheduling:** Proposals are scheduled for presentation and discussion during regular Technical Committee meetings [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981].

## Voting and Approval Criteria

Working Group acceptance requires [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- **Technical Committee Vote:** A simple majority vote of all Technical Committee members.
- **Governing Board Ratification:** Acceptance remains subject to final approval by the AAIF Governing Board.

## Proposal Status Labels

Proposals are tracked using standardized status labels [^evt-working-group-proposals-file-b33563055168-33233981]:
- `New`: Proposal is submitted and waiting in the intake backlog.
- `Approved`: Proposal has been formally accepted.
- `Declined`: Proposal has been rejected, with rationale provided in issue comments.
- `Waiting on Comment`: Additional clarification or information requested by reviewers.
- `Too Early`: Proposal is not yet mature enough; guidance provided for future reapplication.

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops vendor-neutral threat models, security review checklists, best practice guides, and defense-in-depth architectures for autonomous AI agent ecosystems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group aligns security controls across agent execution runtimes, tool protocols, and data protection boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables into specialized workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:

- **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, this stream establishes unified security and privacy evaluation criteria for AAIF initiatives [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Co-led by Matthew Khouzam and Fernando Lucktemberg, providing operational security guidance for deploying AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Co-led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, analyzing unique attack surfaces and vulnerability vectors in multi-agent workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Co-led by Sagar Dashora (with Dan Kommatas proposed), cataloging reusable mitigation patterns for agentic environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape Integration**: Jay White and Katherine Druckman serve as WG delegates to the cross-cutting [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) and taxonomy effort [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Governance & Operations
The group conducts regular meetings and coordinates workstreams using LFX tooling and dedicated community channels [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. Progress updates are submitted asynchronously to the Technical Committee via monthly GitHub reporting flows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

# Overview
The Government, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group bridges global AI policy, regulatory developments, and risk management frameworks with agentic AI system architectures [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. Chaired by Ryan Hagemann (IBM) and Deborah Eng (JPMorgan Chase), the group translates emerging compliance requirements into actionable guidance for open-source AI agent implementations [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group produces policy analyses, risk assessment matrices, and regulatory alignment frameworks for agent developers and deployers [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. It collaborates with peer bodies such as the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) and [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to address accountability and auditability across agent ecosystems.

# Governance & Operations
The working group is led by co-chairs Ryan Hagemann and Deborah Eng [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]. Operating under the oversight of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), the group reports monthly progress through asynchronous GitHub pull requests using a standardized reporting template, with submissions due by the final business day of each month and evaluated during a 7-day review period [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group develops vendor-neutral specifications, protocols, and architectural patterns for establishing AI agent identity, cryptographic attestation, and verifiable trust relationships [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23]. Chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE), the working group defines how autonomous agents authenticate, declare capabilities, and verify authorization across distributed systems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].

Key work areas include establishing standards for agent identity credentials, cryptographic attestation tokens, and interoperable authorization delegation models [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23]. The group cooperates closely with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to integrate identity primitives into runtime threat mitigation models.

Monthly operational updates are reported to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) via standardized pull requests submitted by the last business day of the month and subject to a 7-day review cycle [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23].

# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) serves as the primary technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]. It oversees project admission, project lifecycle transitions, working group formation, and cross-cutting technical alignment across all foundation initiatives [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].

# Architecture / Specification
The Technical Committee coordinates with foundation working groups and workstreams, including:
- [Government, Risk and Regulatory Alignment Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md) [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e]
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-9677055e316b-2e851e23]
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-9677055e316b-93d6f75a]
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]
- Cross-cutting Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream, co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-9677055e316b-9ddc8f32].

# Governance & Operations
The TC maintains visibility over working groups through a standardized asynchronous reporting process [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa]:
- Working groups submit monthly reports via GitHub pull requests by the final business day of each month [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- Standard sections capture progress against objectives, blockers, risks, next month focus areas, and explicit decisions needed from the TC [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e].
- The review window closes 7 calendar days after submission, allowing TC sign-off without turning routine updates into blocking gates [^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-9677055e316b-05c3ca6e, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-be1fe15b5b5e-b8f50afa].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security taxonomies, review checklists, and design patterns for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group (SP WG) establishes shared threat models, defensive architecture patterns, review checklists, and security taxonomies for the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem. The working group operates both as an independent research body addressing agent-specific vulnerabilities and as an intersecting horizontal review layer evaluating specifications produced by other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Workstreams

### Threat Modeling: Gap Analysis and Framework Design

Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP), this workstream evaluates existing AI risk frameworks (such as CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, and NIST AI RMF) against agentic AI threat profiles [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55]. Focus areas include multi-agent persuasion, tool invocation risks, delegated authorization boundaries, and supply-chain integrity (including prompt integrity, model provenance, and tools manifest verification) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-6a261a55].

### Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog

Led by Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), this catalog captures reusable problem-context-solution design patterns and anti-patterns for secure agent deployment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]. Topics include:

- Hooks and execution checkpointing
- Human-in-the-loop (HITL) integration patterns
- Privacy-preserving execution (zero-knowledge proofs, trusted execution environments, encrypted vector databases)
- Blast radius containment and runtime intervention (kill switches, rollback mechanisms, permission downgrades, off-task detection)
- Secure memory lifecycle management (retention, deletion, and data sovereignty)
- Agent authorization models [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-9c4ed1d4]

### Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist

Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy (Global Payments), this workstream defines an operational review checklist to assess deliverables from other AAIF bodies [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]. Target domains include:

- [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md): Agent identity attestations and delegated authorization [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md): Behavioral anomaly detection and audit logging [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]
- [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md): Payment guardrails, account leakage prevention, and transactional scope limits [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b0dad759cb11-f74bdc54]

### Taxonomy and Landscape Integration

The working group's initial terminology workstream transitioned into the cross-WG [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) and taxonomy effort led by Junjie Bu [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7]. Security and privacy representation is maintained by designated delegates Katherine Druckman (JetBrains) and Jay White (Microsoft) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-84f82d5fdbae-3ec725c7].

# Lifecycle History

Deliverables within the working group adhere to a strict progression lifecycle [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d]:

- **Draft**: New deliverables carry a `DRAFT-` filename prefix while undergoing active refinement [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Final**: Moving a deliverable to final status requires explicit approval recorded in the Decisions section of working group meeting minutes, at which point the prefix is removed [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d].
- **Moved**: Deliverables handed off to foundation-wide or cross-working group initiatives are converted into redirect stubs to preserve historical references [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-7a84413abf98-945bcd5d] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-8d5cff93].

mutations.rationale: Cross-WG workstream established to unify terminology, definitions, and landscape efforts across all AAIF working groups.

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-WG initiative establishing unified agentic AI terminology, definition taxonomies, and landscape maps across AAIF.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Taxonomy and Landscape workstream is a cross-working-group initiative tasked with establishing common terminology and resolving conflicting definitions across all Agentic AI Foundation working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. It maintains the unified AAIF taxonomy repository (`aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape`) and serves as the central coordination body for domain-specific definitions developed across the foundation's technical groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance and Operations

The workstream is led by Junjie Bu and coordinates asynchronously alongside a weekly 30-minute sync [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Individual working groups participate via appointed delegates who contribute domain terminology, align slice taxonomies, and resolve cross-cutting ambiguities [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

## Inter-Working-Group Coordination

- **Security and Privacy**: Contributed its foundational taxonomy draft and participates via delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86]. Topics include agent archetypes mapping capabilities such as tool use and network access [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Uses JSON-slice schema reviews (`s03-boundaries`, `s04-core`, `s08-failure`, etc.) aligned to Taxonomy WG standards [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-4].
- **Observability and Traceability**: Coordinates taxonomy planes (orchestration, execution, protocol, reasoning) and trace-model crosswalks with the central landscape [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-10].

# Lifecycle History

The initiative originally began within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) before being elevated to an AAIF-wide cross-WG initiative in May 2026 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes vendor-neutral threat frameworks, security design patterns, builder best practices, and review checklists for agentic AI architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]. The group serves as an architectural anchor within AAIF for analyzing vulnerabilities unique to autonomous systems, multi-agent interactions, and tool executions [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Workstreams

The working group organizes its technical outputs into distinct workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Evaluates gaps in existing AI threat frameworks (MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) relative to agent-specific risks such as memory poisoning, excessive agency, multi-agent persuasion, and blast radius containment (Co-leads: Alon Mazor, Fernando Lucktemberg) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Security Best Practices Guide**: High-level guidance for builders addressing secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and incident forensics (Co-leads: Fernando Lucktemberg, Matthew Khouzam) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-f8906e55, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Reusable secure and privacy-preserving implementation patterns in a problem/context/solution/trade-offs format (Co-leads: Dan Kommatas, Sagar Dashora) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Lightweight review process for evaluating other AAIF working group deliverables through a security and privacy lens (Lead: Govindaraj Palanisamy) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-5, ^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].
- **Taxonomy**: Original working group taxonomy effort migrated into the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), represented by delegates Jay White and Katherine Druckman [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-4907bad31f57-15bb7f86].

## Operations and Governance

Maturing workstream deliverables are maintained under GitHub as the authoritative system of record [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9]. Workgroup updates are submitted monthly to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under a formal review window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3e06e9f18d80-cd4359c9].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry formats, execution tracing models, and debugging standards across heterogeneous agent architectures and multi-agent systems within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its technical investigations into several focused workstreams and focus groups[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4]:
- **LLM Primitives**: Conducting landscape surveys and gap analyses regarding low-level language model execution and protocol audit formatting[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Agent State and Context**: Reviewing runtime state management, memory architectures, and state auditing across academic and commercial implementations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Orchestration and Coordination**: Investigating telemetry and interaction traces for multi-agent workflows.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Exploring white-box tracing representations and reasoning chain observation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].

## Trace Model Planning

The working group is developing evaluation criteria for an **Agent Behavior Trace Model** recommendation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12]. The evaluation framework follows a structured decision path:
1. Inventory and evaluate existing industry models and tracing standards against core use cases[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
2. Identify whether existing standards can be adopted directly or extended through upstream contributions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].
3. Formulate a new AAIF specification only where clear gap analysis demonstrates necessity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-25**: Public issue tracking enabled, focus group workstreams structured across LLM primitives, agent state/context, and reasoning, and taxonomy term reviews initiated[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e5ff91f04c01-f23cc1b4].
- **Trace Model Planning**: Defined scope to assess candidate standards before deciding whether to adopt, extend, or specify new trace conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-12].

- [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing standards, benchmarks, and architectural patterns for non-deterministic agent accuracy, failure recovery, and enterprise reliability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group chartered to establish the standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably under real-world enterprise conditions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]. The group classifies failure modes across non-deterministic agentic workloads, provides shared definitions for quality measurement, and standardizes proactive architecture patterns as well as reactive recovery mechanisms [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

The working group was formally approved on May 15, 2026, and is chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44].

# Architecture / Specification

## Strategic Objectives
The working group focuses on four core strategic objectives [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:
- **Shared understanding**: Establishing clear definitions, taxonomies, and vocabulary for agent accuracy and reliability across the ecosystem.
- **Measurement and detection**: Providing reference methodologies for evaluating agent quality and detecting drift or degradation in deployed systems.
- **Correction patterns**: Documenting autonomous recovery mechanisms, resilience patterns, and human-in-the-loop escalation triggers.
- **Design guidance**: Publishing blueprints that ensure reliability and accuracy are built into agent systems as first-class architectural properties.

## Scope Boundaries
The charter sets clear boundaries regarding the technical scope of the ARWG [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44]:

### In Scope
- **Accuracy and reliability frameworks**: Defining failure modes, evaluation techniques, quality thresholds, and metrics for autonomous systems.
- **Reliable architecture patterns**: Specifying verification loops and grounding mechanisms against authoritative data sources.
- **Recovery and corrective actions**: Standardizing safe-state restoration, rollback mechanisms, automated compensatory actions, and human intervention handoffs.

### Out of Scope
- **Model internals and training**: The group evaluates multi-agent systems as a whole, excluding foundation model training, fine-tuning, or prompt engineering.
- **Trace and log emission mechanics**: Delegated to the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md).
- **Production tooling and platforms**: Standards and blueprints are provided rather than production recovery platforms or commercial guardrail software.
- **Domain-specific compliance**: Prescribing legal or regulatory compliance policies is excluded.
- **Runtime development**: Standard interfaces for runtimes and orchestrators are defined without maintaining production runtime implementations.

## Deliverables Roadmap
The working group operates with a canonical deliverable structure spanning foundation (Phase 1), best practices (Phase 2), and normative standards (Phase 3), designated as deliverables D1 through D6 and internal operational item I1 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-f8e00aa928be-0c623c44][^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-6].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation working group focused on establishing formal definitions, architectural patterns, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks to measure and improve the reliability of agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. Chaired by Jordan Augé (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid), the group operates on a biweekly plenary cadence alternating with dedicated deliverable working sessions [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group advances three primary tracks [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]:
- **D1 (Architectural Framing & Taxonomy):** Covers evaluation subjects, accuracy and reliability dimensions, observability and attribution, grounding, failure symptoms, root causes, evaluation ecosystems, and correction mechanisms [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1]. ARWG coordinates vocabulary with the cross-working group effort led by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D2 (Applied Gap Analysis & Benchmark Survey):** Led by Sanjeev Suresh, this track captures B2B enterprise requirements across personas (product managers, operations, evaluators, and data scientists) to map tooling and interoperability gaps in production systems [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **D6 (Evaluation Protocol):** Scoped directly by the operational findings from D2 to build standard evaluation and benchmarking protocols [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-15:** Charter formally approved by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].
- **2026-06-29:** June 2026 monthly report recorded D1 reaching ~70% completion on initial term categorization and D2 table of contents finalization [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-a17a580f85c2-0e16c0a1].

# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation established to curate a canonical taxonomy of agentic AI terminology and build an interactive ecosystem landscape [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]. Its mission is to prevent terminology siloing, resolve contradictory definitions across technical working groups, and align terminology with international standards bodies such as ISO and NIST [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].

# Architecture / Specification

The workstream operates using a decoupled data structure and schema format [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1]:
- **Schema and Metadata:** Leverages CNCF-style metadata schemas for terminology and ecosystem mapping [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-f5653280f5fa-c283d985].
- **Two-tier Definitions:** Taxonomy entries contain concise summaries alongside comprehensive scope notes and citations to accommodate diverse audiences [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Review and Governance:** Operates via a delegate model with appointed domain editors from across AAIF working groups reviewing terms asynchronously via Pull Requests and cross-WG spreadsheet reviews [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1, ^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].
- **Landscape Directory:** Integrates with the foundation landscape directory at [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-01:** Established the PR-driven taxonomy workflow and CNCF metadata baseline [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8b7c1a965501-bdb232c1].
- **2026-06-15:** Charter sign-off achieved across six constituent working groups; initiated definition style guide and AI usage policies [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a51b00ec455f-a054be90].
- **2026-06-22:** Initiated universal terms consolidation and agent boundary debates across WG delegates [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-4885f35209fd-df51791c].

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation responsible for aligning definitions, eliminating siloed terminology, and publishing the ecosystem landscape directory.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0] Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream coordinates formal delegates nominated across AAIF working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream organizes foundation-wide knowledge using two primary data models:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
- **SKOS-Lite Taxonomy**: A lightweight Simple Knowledge Organization System schema capturing core agentic AI terms, definitions, and relationships across domains.
- **CNCF-Style Landscape**: A hierarchical ecosystem mapping configuration powering the interactive [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) web portal.

# Governance and Operations
The workstream operates through an asynchronous, pull-request-driven contribution workflow governed by designated domain editors and working group delegates:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a6b16668a40b-d9d68cd0]
- **Delegate Representation**: Participating working groups designate formal delegates to contribute domain-specific core terms (typically 10–20 terms during initial phases) and resolve cross-domain naming conflicts.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
- **Review Workflow**: Proposed terms are aggregated and cross-reviewed in a central tracking process prior to merging into master schemas.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a17a580f85c2-1ed5dbc1]
- **Reporting**: Monthly progress reports are submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on the final business day of each month with a seven-day review window.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-33d3ff4f1e08-3ee3542b]
