proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG Observability & Traceability) coordinates telemetry standards, execution tracing conventions, and evaluation instrumentation across heterogeneous agent runtimes and orchestration frameworks.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2] The working group is co-chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes technical work into five specialized focus groups addressing observability layers:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **LLM Primitives Observability**: Tracing and metric conventions for low-level foundation model invocations, token utilization, and latency.
- **Protocol Observability**: Monitoring and telemetry for agent interaction protocols such as the [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md).
- **Multi-Agentic Observability**: Distributed tracing for orchestration, agent-to-agent communication, and coordination patterns.
- **Agentic State and Context**: Instrumentation tracking memory, session state transitions, and context window dynamics.
- **Agentic Reasoning**: Telemetry capturing planning steps, reflection loops, and tool-use decision paths.

# Deliverables and Inter-Group Collaboration
- **Use Cases and Gap Analysis**: Development of reference use cases and observability gap analysis documents shared with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and peer groups.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Active coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to define common telemetry and tracing terminology.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a17a580f85c2-b3f2d5c2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral telemetry conventions, distributed execution tracing standards, and runtime provenance frameworks across multi-agent AI ecosystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]. The group coordinates cross-framework trace formats, context-propagation models, and discovery architectures to provide deterministic auditing and real-time operational visibility into autonomous agent workflows.

# Architecture / Specification

### Focus Group Structure and Consolidation
The working group organizes its technical work into problem-oriented streams rather than siloed architectural domains [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]:
- **Consolidated Protocol and Primitives Group**: Merged the former *LLM Primitives* and *Protocol Observability* focus groups to streamline work on runtime hooks, token-level telemetry, and protocol metrics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Agent State, Context, and Reasoning**: Addresses context graph tracking and reasoning-step observability, with active coordination alongside the consolidated protocol stream [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

### Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)
The working group evaluates the Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification for decentralized AI resource identification and trust verification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a]:
- **Catalog**: Static indexing layer for declaring tool, prompt, and skill endpoints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Registry**: Dynamic registry accessed through REST APIs supporting natural language search and query resolution [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].
- **Trust and Identity Integrations**: Native support for trust manifests and interoperability with identity frameworks including SPIFFE and Agent Name Service (ANS) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

### Hardened Traceability Architecture
The group is delivering reference recommendations for provable, hardened traceability architectures designed to secure execution logs and integrate with attestation frameworks across the ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-09**: Consolidated overlapping focus groups into a single bi-weekly meeting stream; reviewed the multi-vendor Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-4b349715463d-4901531a].

- Identity and trust alignment: [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- Security threat alignment: [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream serves as the central semantic harmonization engine for the Agentic AI Foundation, maintaining canonical definitions, classification taxonomies, and ecosystem maps across all AAIF working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2]. The workstream operates through designated delegates from each domain working group to curate an unambiguous terminology set for v1.0 publication.

# Architecture / Specification

### Terminology Intake and Review Pipeline
The workstream manages a unified catalog of approximately 250 candidate terms contributed across domain working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e]:
- **Domain Submissions**: Each working group submits 10–20 core domain terms through delegate representatives [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Consensus Cull and Debate Workflow**: Terms are tracked via a consensus column with conditional highlighting, flagging non-specific terms as "cull candidates" while elevating foundational cross-cutting concepts to a "Universal" category [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].
- **Boundary Disambiguation**: Ongoing debate resolution differentiates core AI agent concepts from legacy software terminology (e.g., establishing strict technical boundaries between autonomous agents and general bots, and separating *Agent Card* from *Agent Blueprint*) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e].

### Ecosystem Landscape
Aligns definitions with the interactive landscape directory, using CNCF-style schema definitions and Git pull request workflows for term proposals and monthly status reports to the Technical Committee [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-05-21**: Kickoff meeting reviewing charter and PR-driven taxonomy submission workflow [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-06-08**: Established cross-WG delegate structure and ongoing boundary definitions deliverable [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].
- **2026-07-06**: Transitioned to execution phase for v1.0 terminology release; implemented consensus cull workflows and expanded meeting cadence to one hour weekly [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-1ee494c46a19-56a82d6e][^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-d7a6875f36a3-d28591c2].

# References

- Technical leadership: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- Security domain terms: [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)
- Landscape mapping: [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md)

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and review checklists for agent ecosystems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops foundational threat models, mitigation architectures, security best practices, and evaluation checklists across autonomous AI agent environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d]. Chaired by Alexander Frazer and Junjie Bu, the group collaborates with external standards bodies and sister working groups to harden agent communication, tool invocation, and credential delegation against emerging attack vectors [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].

# Architecture / Specification

### Core Deliverables
1. **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg; synthesizes gap analyses across MITRE ATLAS, OWASP Top 10 for Agentic AI, MAESTRO, and the NIST AI RMF into a comprehensive agent threat model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
2. **Security Best Practices Guide**: Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam; establishes operational hardening guidance for agent deployment, tool execution safeguards, and attestation controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora; documents hardened architectural patterns for sandboxing, state isolation, and secure agent-to-agent communication [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
4. **Cross-Working Group Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy; provides a standardized security review rubric evaluated against all AAIF technical specifications [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

### External Alignment and Liaison
- **Standards Harmonization**: Engages with OWASP, AARM, and ETSI TC SAI (addressing European AI Act compliance for autonomous agents) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Ecosystem Deconfliction**: Coordinates with Linux Foundation sister initiatives such as FINOS AI Governance to align enterprise reference architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].
- **Protocol Security**: Investigates cryptographic tool attestation within agent protocols to prevent dynamic tool-swapping and rug-pull exploits [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

### Technical Committee Reporting
The working group submits monthly reports to the Technical Committee by the last business day of each month, tracking KPI metrics across Adoption, Quality, Community, and Timeliness subject to a 7-day async review window [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-33d3ff4f1e08-f33f7a28][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9677055e316b-27369ef5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-07-07**: Completed Deliverable 4 (Threat Modeling Gap Analysis) and initial draft of the Best Practices Guide; initiated external standards coordination with ETSI TC SAI and OWASP [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-aef0bad9a49f-35abad8d].

# References

- Governance oversight: [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)
- Identity architecture: [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)
- Telemetry alignment: [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)
- Terminology harmonization: [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream curates and maintains a shared glossary of agentic AI terminology and an interactive ecosystem map for the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), ensuring consistent definitions and technology mapping across all working groups.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream operates under a federated curation model where designated delegates and domain editors representing each Technical Working Group ingest, reconcile, and arbitrate shared definitions rather than drafting siloed domain glossaries.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

Key technical components and deliverables include:
- **SKOS-Lite Vocabulary Repository**: Standardized terminology schema encoding concepts with attributes such as `prefLabel`, `altLabel`, `broaderTerm`, `scopeNote`, `relatedTerms`, and `contrastsWith` stored in `taxonomy-data.js`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Global Ecosystem Architecture Map**: A CNCF Landscape 2-compatible ecosystem mapping defined in `landscape.yml` and maintained through cross-WG consensus.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]
- **Automated Web Portal**: GitHub Pages continuous deployment workflow distributing the Shared Taxonomy Explorer and Landscape Map web applications.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-0f132b096200-171c31ea]

# Lifecycle History
- **2026-06-21**: Charter formally approved under the leadership of chairs Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b41aaf03f7ac-76d5f60b]

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, security best practice guides, and architectural patterns to safeguard agentic AI systems against emerging vulnerabilities and privacy risks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates across five active workstreams led by confirmed leads[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]:
- **Threat Modeling**: Developing the Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis to identify agent-specific security threats and design defenses.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Best Practices**: Authoring the Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide for developers and operators.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]
- **Cross-WG Alignment**: Vocabulary and glossary efforts have been transitioned to the cross-WG [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), supported by dedicated delegates.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

The group coordinates with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) on engagement boundaries with external security consortia, including OWASP, AARM, and MCP ACS.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Lifecycle History
- **June 2026**: Transitioned from formation to execution; established five active workstreams and presented initial drafts for the Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Best Practices Guide.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a17a580f85c2-2e81780d]

# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, telemetry schemas, and instrumentation patterns for monitoring, debugging, and tracing agentic AI workflows.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c6471d290754-349d30a5]

Key ongoing focus areas and initiatives include:

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow models, runtime coordination patterns, and stateful execution standards for agentic AI systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (W&PI) advances the mission of the Agentic AI Foundation by defining a shared workflow model, establishing common terminology, and creating vendor-neutral reference architectures and interoperability guidelines for agentic execution across frameworks, tools, and environments [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]. Approved on May 13, 2026, the group addresses portability barriers, orchestration semantics, and operational patterns for non-deterministic AI agents operating in complex multi-step workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Leadership and Administration

- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]
- **Short Name:** W&PI [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]

# Scope

The working group's charter covers three core technical areas [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56]:

1. **Agent Workflow Models and Semantics:** Standardizing primitives (tasks, tool calls, branching, handoffs, retries) and structural representations across frameworks to bridge deterministic workflows and autonomous agent execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
2. **Long-Running and Stateful Agent Execution:** Defining state persistence models, recovery mechanisms, idempotency, and workflow-level audit logs for multi-step processes executing over extended durations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].
3. **Tool Invocation and External System Coordination:** Establishing standard integration patterns between autonomous agents, external APIs, CLIs, and enterprise human-in-the-loop reviewers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b41aaf03f7ac-ba2e4c56].

# Related Initiatives

- [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)

# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group (ARWG) advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing standards, benchmarks, and engineering practices required for AI agents to operate accurately and reliably in enterprise environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]. The group operates under a commitment to technical neutrality and antitrust compliance, meeting biweekly to advance agent evaluation methodologies and address non-deterministic execution failure modes [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019].

# Leadership and Administration

- **Chair:** Jordan Augé (Cisco) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Co-Chair:** Casper Nielsen (Diagrid) [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Appointed Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]
- **Cadence:** Biweekly on Tuesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-b33563055168-8ff39019]

- **D1 (Terminology & Methodology):** Methodology framework providing literature grounding and staged review batches for accuracy and reliability terms submitted to the cross-WG taxonomy [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **D2 (Enterprise Gap Analysis):** Practitioner-priority evaluation reframed from benchmark surveys toward analyzing persona requirements and reusable testing gaps [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].
- **I1 (Liaison Workstream):** Cross-working group coordination stream establishing active liaison channels with the [Observability & Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) Working Group [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-fa4050a9f626-df96ac2e].

# Overview

The Agentic Commerce Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by cataloging, aligning, and harmonizing open specifications, frameworks, and terminology for commerce workflows conducted by AI agents on behalf of users, businesses, and software systems [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]. The working group maintains protocol neutrality and focuses on identifying common ground across emerging specifications rather than authoring competing commerce protocols [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563].

# Leadership and Administration

- **Chair:** Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Co-Chair:** Rahul Bansal (OpenAI) [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Appointed Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]
- **Cadence:** Biweekly on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM PT [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]

# Scope

The working group provides reference architectures and interoperability guidelines across key stages of agentic transactions [^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-b33563055168-41e54563]:

- Discovery and catalog integration
- Negotiation and intent parsing
- Checkout orchestration and authorization
- Payment orchestration and settlement handoffs
- Post-purchase lifecycle interactions and dispute handling

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes shared threat models, security architectures, defensive design patterns, and best practice guides for agentic AI implementations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91]. The group evaluates protocol-level vulnerabilities (including prompt injection, MCP poisoning, and session replay risks) across disaggregated agent archetypes comprising LLM components, tool orchestrations, conversation histories, and resource channels [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

# Active Deliverables and Workstreams

- **Threat Modeling Gap Analysis & Framework Design:** Led by Alon Mazor and Fernando Lucktemberg, producing an foundational gap analysis and threat modeling framework [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam, documenting operational guidance and practical controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Led by Dan Kommatas and Sagar Dashora, categorizing structural security patterns alongside architecture guidance [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Led by Govindaraj Palanisamy, establishing security checklists and review criteria across other AAIF working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].
- **Taxonomy Collaboration:** Working with the [Taxonomy & Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) group (represented by Junjie Bu, Jay White, and Katherine Druckman) to define security-critical concepts including sessions, constraints, and guardrails [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-521fc71b9be5-d634fd91].

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group advancing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, and action verification.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, verifiable delegation, action verification, and counterparty trust across enterprise ecosystems [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. Chaired by Grant Miller (IBM) and Alper Dedeoēlu (SAP SE), the working group coordinates work across taxonomy, reference architecture, and critical use cases [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group executes across three primary sub-working groups [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]:

- **Taxonomy**: Develops formal definitions for terms including Agent, Action Record, Audit Log, Consent Receipt, and Human-in-the-Loop [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. The group distinguishes an *Action Record* (a tamper-evident, content-private, independently verifiable record of consequential action intended for counterparties and auditors) from operational runtime telemetry managed under [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Reference Architecture**: Produces a components table spanning Discovery Metadata, Identifier, Identity, Authorization, Revocability, Evidence, Verification, and Reputation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. Core architectural assumptions establish that sub-agents cannot hold broader permissions than their delegating agent, which cannot exceed the initiating user's permissions [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758]. The group also evaluated NVIDIA's Secure Agent Workspace (SAW) reference design and the Open Delegation and Identity Standard (ODIS) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Synthesizes agent lifecycle requirements across Internal, B2B, and B2C interaction models covering naming, deployment, delegation, dynamic per-request authorization, and principal-attested revocation [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

## Technical Committee Requests
The working group proposed profiling OAuth 2.0 as the normative baseline for cross-platform agent authorization presentation (token formats, delegation chains, and scope expressions), while explicitly keeping backend policy enforcement autonomous to target platforms [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

# Lifecycle History
- **July 2026**: Delivered monthly report outlining sub-WG taxonomy convergence, reference architecture component definitions, and the OAuth 2.0 baseline proposal submitted to the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) [^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-a17a580f85c2-1f6ad758].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group establishing shared threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and privacy guardrails across agent architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes shared threat models, secure architecture patterns, guardrail specifications, and privacy guidelines across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem. The working group coordinates joint reviews across technical working groups to establish cross-cutting security checklists and resolve scope overlaps.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group conducts cross-domain scope analyses to integrate security and privacy requirements across related AAIF disciplines:

- **Identity & Trust**: Reviewing identity boundaries, delegation verification, and credential protection in coordination with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12].
- **Observability & Traceability**: Assessing data redaction, secure audit logging, and tracing privacy with [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13].
- **Workflows & Process Integration**: Reviewing runtime execution sandboxing and orchestration attack surfaces with [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14].
- **Agentic Commerce**: Mapping transactional safety, payment negotiation security, and sensitive data leakage with [Agentic Commerce](../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15].
- **Accuracy & Reliability**: Reviewing verification boundaries, validation integrity, and failure mode protections with [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-17].

# Lifecycle History
- **Cross-WG Alignment**: Initiated cross-workgroup scope reviews and checklist identification across Identity & Trust, Observability & Traceability, Workflows, Commerce, and Accuracy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-12] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-13] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-14] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-15] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-17].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic Commerce Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group cataloging and harmonizing open specifications, protocols, and reference architectures across the agentic commerce lifecycle.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group (WG Agentic Commerce) is an AAIF technical body co-chaired by Ilya Grigorik (Shopify) and Rahul Bansal (OpenAI)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26]. The group focuses on protocol-neutral interfaces, capability mapping, and reference architectures across the entire agentic commerce lifecycle, spanning product discovery, delegated authority, checkout and negotiation, payment execution, fraud and trust signaling, and post-purchase operations[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its technical work around a lifecycle capability framework rather than introducing a competing monolithic protocol[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332]:

- **Product Discovery:** Compares asynchronous product feeds against live merchant or marketplace queries, addressing source discovery, catalog normalization, data freshness, and trust boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Checkout and Negotiation:** Analyzes merchant-authoritative stateful negotiations across protocols like ACP and UCP, capturing extension mechanisms, transport bindings, and human-handoff dimensions[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **Payment Abstractions:** Models payment handling across three core primitives—*handler*, *instrument*, and *credential*—while examining dynamic capability discovery, sensitive data isolation, delegated tokenization boundaries, and composition patterns like Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) challenge–credential–receipt flows[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **Fraud and Trust Signaling:** Separates agent identity and risk from shopper identity and risk, establishing evidence bindings across delegations and transactions with privacy-preserving signal portability and risk-triggered context requests[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **Post-Purchase Operations:** Evaluates order observation, return policy discovery, refund processing, dispute management, and state mutations, analyzing the integration of agent wallets and payment mandates (such as AP2 and x402)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

# Cross-Working Group Coordination
The working group coordinates with several AAIF working groups on cross-cutting capabilities:
- [Identity and Trust Working Group](identity-and-trust.md) for delegated authority and agent identity binding[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- [Security and Privacy Working Group](security-and-privacy.md) for sensitive data isolation and threat modeling[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- [Observability and Traceability Working Group](observability-and-traceability.md) for multi-agent transaction auditability and provenance[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].

# Lifecycle History
- **February 2026:** Working Group launched with initial capability inventory and problem mapping across commerce protocols (ACP, UCP, AP2, x402)[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-baf22ae9aa4b-28feda26].
- **March 2026:** Adopted problem-first lifecycle methodology and initiated discovery landscape analysis[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a439311d16f4-f0496332].
- **April 2026:** Drafted working group charter and framed the Agentic Commerce Capability Map across discovery and checkout[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-3e3f89e6a796-ee1af760].
- **May 2026:** Charter officially approved; analyzed payment handler models and MPP interoperability patterns[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-093fe1535af6-58b40393].
- **June 2026:** Analyzed fraud and trust signal preservation across distributed agent, platform, and merchant boundaries[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-a17a580f85c2-056b6afe].
- **July 2026:** Advanced post-purchase capability mapping and explored agent wallet architectures and mandate bindings[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-file-fa4050a9f626-c7520564].

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-WG initiative establishing unified agentic AI terminology, SKOS-Lite definition taxonomies, and an interactive industry landscape.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream (WS Taxonomy & Landscape) is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation tasked with standardizing terminology and mapping the agentic software ecosystem [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]. Co-chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg), the workstream arbitrates definitions across domain-specific working groups to publish an authoritative SKOS-Lite taxonomy and maintain the official [Agentic AI Landscape](../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Architecture / Specification

### Review Pipeline and Term Admission
The workstream operates a phased, two-step admission process where terms are reviewed and admitted into the taxonomy prior to defining detailed fields such as `definition`, `category`, and `broaderTerm` [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103]:
1. **Sequential Review**: Terms from a centralized review spreadsheet are evaluated weekly across universal concepts and domain working groups (such as [Identity & Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), [Workflows & Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
2. **Triage Categories**: Candidate terms are categorized as admitted, culled, or held for debate when cross-working-group consensus is pending [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].
3. **Public Deployment**: Admitted batches are merged via pull requests and published directly to the public taxonomy portal [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

# Lifecycle History

- **July–August 2026**: Reviewed 67 of the 128-term backlog across weekly sessions. Admitted initial batches comprising 13 terms via PR #33 (covering universal terms, Identity & Trust, and Workflows) and 8 terms via PR #35 (Governance, Risk & Regulatory), bringing the live taxonomy to 21 published terms [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-fa4050a9f626-a73c0103].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow models, runtime coordination patterns, and reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group defines runtime coordination models, integration interfaces, and architectural patterns for deterministic and agentic workflow orchestration within the Agentic AI Foundation. The group translates proven distributed workflow practices into agentic environments through standard patterns, decision records, and multi-agent coordination frameworks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054].

# Architecture / Specification

### Reference Architecture Pattern Specifications
The working group documents reusable architecture patterns using a standardized schema focused on invariants, failure modes, and implementation axes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-0f939e51d343-befb4054]:
- **Problem & Solution**: Context-free descriptions capturing core recurring sub-problems and minimal box topologies.
- **Invariants**: Mandatory properties that must hold across any compliant runtime implementation.
- **Failure Modes**: Explicit operational breakdowns that manifest when invariants are violated.
- **Implementation Approaches**: Matrix categorizing concrete mechanisms by platform axes, explicitly separating platform-provided features from required implementation controls.
- **Historical Precedents**: Pre-agent deterministic workflow precedents demonstrating discovered industry convergence.

### Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)
Decisions are tracked via structured ADR templates capturing proposal date, lifecycle status (Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Superseded), context, rationale, consequences, and evaluated alternatives [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3a311f3edf5a-27d0e407].

The Public Agent Skills repository provides a catalog of modular, interoperable agent skills, recipes, and automation definitions maintained across Agentic AI Foundation working groups. These skills supply agent runtimes with structured execution capabilities, evaluation workflows, and artifact generators [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

### Reference Architecture Generator Skill (`aaif-ref-arch`)
Contributed via the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), the `aaif-ref-arch` skill provides standardized instructions for generating AAIF reference architecture documents and technical evaluations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b]:
- **Compatibility**: Requires internet access and Git CLI capabilities; compatible with agent runtimes including Kiro [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].
- **Target Roles**: Solution architects and developers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].
- **Standardized Output Sections**: Enforces consistent documentation structure covering scope zoom levels, prerequisite dependencies, ASCII architecture diagrams, instrumentation walkthroughs, sample trace telemetry, cost profiling, and validation criteria [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1cf101000b0c-bfd60e7b].

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern requiring an authorized human to explicitly approve an immutable proposal before a protected effect is executed.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Human Approval Gate is a workflow pattern that pauses automated execution to require an explicit authorization decision from a designated human before a protected effect takes place[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]. Maintained within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), the pattern provides deterministic accountability and auditability for high-risk actions.

# Architecture / Specification
The pattern decouples proposal generation from execution by enforcing a durable wait state[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]:

```text
immutable proposal ──► present to authorized human ──► explicit decision
                              │                           │
                              └── durable wait ─────────┘
                                          │
                          decision record: who · what · when
```

Key invariants required across implementations include[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428]:
- **Identified Approver:** The approver must be a uniquely identified human principal authorized for the decision class; shared accounts are prohibited.
- **Immutable Proposal Binding:** The presented request is immutable; any modification invalidates pending state and requires a fresh approval flow.
- **Explicit Outcomes:** Approval and rejection require explicit actions. Silence, network timeouts, or errors never represent implicit approval.
- **Audit Record:** A decision record captures the proposal version, approver identity, decision outcome, and timestamp bound to the run identity.
- **Race Protection:** Duplicate, late, or conflicting decision events cannot trigger duplicate execution or invalid state resumption.

# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an AAIF technical body focused on defining workflow models, runtime coordination mechanisms, and integration patterns for autonomous agent systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a]. It creates standardized vocabularies, reusable architectural patterns, and end-to-end reference architectures to address practical integration needs[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group structures its deliverables across three core workstreams:
- **Reference Architectures:** Complete compositions organized around recognizable practitioner jobs rather than raw agent counts, establishing boundaries, guarantees, and exit states[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-f035520d0488-6fefbf62].
- **Workflow Patterns:** Modular, independently adoptable techniques for recurring execution challenges, such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and durable wait patterns[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-3e360b3d4277-1647d428].
- **Taxonomy:** Standard terminology clarifying workflow concepts across specifications, use cases, and reference implementations[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-84f82d5fdbae-2bafe01a].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent telemetry standards, multi-agent execution tracing, and resource discovery observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an AAIF technical working group establishing telemetry formats, tracing frameworks, and diagnostic standards for agentic AI workflows and peer-to-peer agent communications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763]. Chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog), the group standardizes execution semantics across runtime environments, protocols, and discovery registries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group operates across three consolidated focus tracks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7]:
- **LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability:** Covers Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) observability, skill provenance, pre-execution trust tracing, and cross-boundary observability gap models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7].
- **Multi-Agentic Observability (Orchestration & Coordination):** Advances peer-to-peer telemetry architectures (e.g., LibP2P and GossipSub integration), Verifiable Telemetry Objects (VTO), and Agent Action Capsules (AAC) for decentralized agent tracing[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].
- **Agentic State & Context:** Standardizes reasoning state capture, state transition telemetry, and context intelligence graph models[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

The group is also developing the Agent Behavior Trace Model recommendation to bridge OpenTelemetry standards with application-layer agent execution frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fa4050a9f626-d98d68f7][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-401e66e1fd5f-5d358763].

# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes a shared workflow model and common terminology for agentic AI systems, extending open specifications and producing interoperability guidelines and design patterns that enable agent workflows to operate across frameworks, tools, and execution environments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group focuses on core areas of agentic workflow infrastructure:
- **Shared Workflow Models:** Defining consistent domain abstractions and execution semantics for multi-step agent processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].
- **Specification Harmonization:** Extending open specifications and projects across diverse runtime systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].
- **Interoperability Guidelines:** Establishing design patterns enabling agent workflows to interact predictably across disparate tools and hosting platforms[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

# Governance and Operations

## Leadership
- **Chair:** Yaron Schneider (Diagrid)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Co-Chair:** Adam Seligman (Workato)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 (appointed by Platinum and Gold working group members)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]

## Operating Cadence
- **Meetings:** Biweekly on Thursdays at 8:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Mailing List:** `wg-workflows-process-integration@lists.aaif.io`[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87]
- **Governance:** Operates under [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) oversight, standard Linux Foundation antitrust compliance, and individual-capacity neutrality commitments[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-b33563055168-a6ab4b87].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops vendor-neutral security guidelines, architectural patterns, threat models, and operational evaluation frameworks for agentic AI deployments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Deliverables and Workstreams

The working group drives core guidance documents, including the *Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide*[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9]:
- **Secrets Management:** Controls and storage patterns for credential handling within agentic loops[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Secure Tool Invocation:** Safeguards spanning Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, supply chain verification, and least-privilege tool execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Guardrails:** Runtime protection mechanisms against prompt injection, context tampering, and unintended side effects[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Evaluation Frameworks:** Structured methodologies for auditing agent decision-making and robustness[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].
- **Post-Incident Forensics:** Trace collection and investigation protocols following security anomalies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

## Scope Boundaries

Identity architecture and delegated authorization mechanisms (such as SPIFFE/SVID and RFC 8693) are explicitly out of scope for this working group and reside within the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-9].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group advances the Agentic AI Foundation's mission by establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across the agentic AI ecosystem[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. It produces open threat models, a shared taxonomy, best practice guides, and security design patterns to foster shared responsibility for trustworthy autonomous agent execution[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

The working group is chaired by Alex Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) for the term spanning March 1, 2026, through January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95]. Meetings occur biweekly on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM PT[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-3c263a95].

# Active Workstreams
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design:** Evaluates agentic AI security threats and gaps across existing frameworks such as MITRE ATLAS, OWASP, MAESTRO, and NIST AI RMF, while analyzing alignment with STRIDE and PASTA methodologies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Formulates architectural guidance for secure agent operations, human accountability, and identity integration[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog:** Establishes reusable design patterns and pattern contribution templates for agent security architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist:** Coordinates baseline security and privacy review standards across other AAIF initiatives[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].
- **Taxonomy and Landscape:** Contributes security and privacy terminology to the cross-WG effort coordinated with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-fa4050a9f626-fb1414ed][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

# Operational Governance
Working group deliverables within the approved charter are reviewed and merged directly by the working group without awaiting [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) pre-approval, reporting monthly status updates back to the TC[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5]. Working group meetings, Discord channels, and repository artifacts default to public access[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-75f22d914368-03de91f5].

The working group designates GitHub as its durable source of truth for work tracking, decision logging, and deliverable progression[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e54af6eb3811-b61584ff]. Work items require GitHub issues tracking outcomes, drivers, and standardized status labels:

proposed_concept.title: Attested Isolated Runtime Pattern
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern isolating policy enforcement and evidence signing within hardware-attested boundaries while keeping untrusted agent execution external.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Attested Isolated Runtime pattern defines an architectural model for deploying agentic systems where the infrastructure operator sits inside the threat model [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]. It places policy decision enforcement and evidence signing within a hardware-isolated environment (such as a Trusted Execution Environment or TEE) while explicitly keeping untrusted agent runtime code outside the isolated boundary [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern requires four foundational elements to secure agent execution and data gating [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11]:

1. **External Agent Placement**: The agent runtime executes outside the trusted computing base (TCB) because agent code processes attacker-influenced inputs as normal operation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
2. **Internal Key Generation**: Cryptographic signing keys are generated inside the isolation boundary and bound directly to verifiable attestation evidence [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
3. **Measurement Sealing**: Enforcement policies are sealed to the hardware measurement of the boundary and released only upon valid appraisal [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
4. **Independent Appraisal**: An independent verifier appraises per-unit-of-work evidence before data release or downstream tool invocations are permitted [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

The pattern supports multiple confidential computing hardware stacks—including AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX, ARM CCA, NVIDIA GPU confidential computing, and TPM 2.0—while also specifying a software-only mode for development and testing [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].

# Lifecycle History

Proposed within the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) design patterns workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

proposed_concept.description: Governance framework defining admission requirements, stage progressions (Sandbox, Growth, Impact, Emeritus), and annual reviews for AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Lifecycle Policy defines the formal process for open technical projects to join the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), progress through maturity stages, and undergo annual evaluations [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]. Managed under the direction of the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md), it establishes uniform admission and graduation criteria across all foundation projects [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Architecture / Specification

## Project Proposal Process

Projects must be submitted through the AAIF project proposals repository with detailed intake metadata, including [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- Project description, mission alignment, and relationships with existing AAIF projects.
- Example use cases, evidence of adoption, and an identified Technical Committee sponsor.
- OSI-approved permissive licensing, public repository location, automated release processes, and issue tracker.
- Maintainer team structure, governance documentation, and official communication channels.

## Lifecycle Stages

The policy structures project maturity across four discrete stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0]:
- **Sandbox Stage**: Entry point for early-stage or experimental open-source efforts requiring incubation and foundation alignment.
- **Growth Stage**: Intermediate stage for projects with active multi-organizational contributor communities and demonstrated adoption.
- **Impact Stage**: Production-grade projects demonstrating widespread ecosystem adoption, sustained governance maturity, and high utility.
- **Emeritus Stage**: Retired or archived projects that are no longer under active development.

## Annual Review Process

All active projects participate in an annual review conducted by the Technical Committee to evaluate project health, community diversity, and stage progression readiness [^evt-technical-committee-file-8f732085cd4f-49330cd0].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, security design patterns, and engineering best practices to protect agentic systems against subversion, prompt injection, and unauthorized data leakage [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]. Chaired by Alex Frazer, the group coordinates closely with the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and cross-working-group initiatives such as [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group organizes its deliverables across dedicated workstreams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974]:

- **Threat Modeling**: Developing threat modeling gap analyses and reference attack surface models for agent architectures [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-8].
- **Security Design Patterns**: Standardizing technical patterns including the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) pattern for confidential execution boundaries [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-11].
- **Best Practices Guides**: Formulating actionable operational guidance for securing agent runtimes, tool invocation, and memory stores [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Participating in weekly sessions to define security, guardrail, and constraint terminology within the unified AAIF taxonomy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-02-17**: Initial orientation and scope exploration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-03-03**: Alex Frazer introduced as elected chair [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-05-26**: Charter formally approved [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].
- **2026-08-04**: Group established that workstream PRs can merge after internal group review without requiring upfront TC approval [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-18be1974].

# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive architectural map and directory maintained by the AAIF to document the evolving open-source and commercial agentic ecosystem [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18]. It provides categorization across agent runtimes, multi-agent frameworks, protocols, and gateway infrastructure [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape classifies technologies across key structural domains:

- **Frameworks & Infrastructure / Orchestration & Multi-Agent**: Runtimes, multi-agent orchestration frameworks, and cloud-native AI gateways (such as Higress and AgentGateway) that provide control planes for MCP server hosting, tool registry routing, and agent traffic governance [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].
- **Protocols & Standards**: Open interface specifications including Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md).
- **Security & Guardrails**: Sandboxing layers, policy enforcement points, and privacy-preserving execution tooling.

Entries in the landscape must meet defined open-source thresholds, foundation alignment criteria, and public repository visibility requirements [^evt-aaif-landscape-pr-18].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Agent skill for maintainers providing structured first-pass GitHub issue triage, root-cause analysis, and prompt injection defense.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The `issue-analysis` skill is an agent workflow developed in the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository that produces structured, first-pass technical assessments of filed GitHub issues for project maintainers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] Designed as an advisory tool rather than an automated decision maker, the skill evaluates issue reports, classifies severity, formulates root-cause hypotheses, and suggests maintainer actions while grounding conclusions in reference repository reviews and strictly isolating untrusted input data.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]

# Architecture / Specification

## Input Isolation and Injection Defense
The skill treats issue text strictly as data rather than executable instructions.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690] Issue text is ingested inside nonce-delimited blocks. Any directives embedded within issue reports (such as requests to disregard system instructions, execute commands, exfiltrate credentials, or trigger notifications) are categorized as security findings rather than tasks, triggering the `injectionSuspected` flag and logging context in `injectionNotes`.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]

## Grounding and Analysis Workflow
The skill executes a four-stage analysis process:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]
1. **Evidence Ingestion:** Inspecting explicit reporter claims, reproduction steps, environments, and author metadata without granting instruction authority.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]
2. **Codebase Exploration:** Reading local repository components to validate technical plausibility using concrete file paths while operating in read-only mode without executing network or build tools.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]
3. **Reference Review Grounding:** Consulting hand-written historical reviews in `references/` by matching tags and components to establish project-specific precedents for severity and failure modes.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5a7044042daa-94e76690]
4. **Structured Drafting:** Emitting evaluations conforming to a standardized template.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]

## Output Schema and Template Structure
Analyses follow a standard template comprising:[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Summary:** Single-paragraph restatement of the reported issue.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Classification:** Issue type (`bug`, `feature-request`, `documentation`, `question`, `security`, `ambiguous`), severity rating (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `informational`), and reproducibility status.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Severity Rationale:** Explicit justification based on user impact and precedent.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Affected Components:** Explicit file paths or module identifiers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Root-Cause Hypotheses:** Explanatory mechanisms with proposed confirmation/refutation steps.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Suggested Actions:** Prioritized, diagnostic next steps for maintainers.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Open Questions:** Inquiries required from reporters before proceeding.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]
- **Related Past Reviews:** Citations to relevant historical references.[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5e60bc4f0771-cf90cfef]

Related skills are cataloged in [Public Agent Skills](../resources/public-agent-skills.md).

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis
proposed_concept.description: Agent skill for maintainers providing structured first-pass GitHub issue triage, root-cause analysis, and adversarial prompt injection defenses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis skill provides automated first-pass triage, root-cause categorization, and defensive validation for untrusted issue submissions across Agentic AI Foundation repositories.

Because triage agents directly ingest untrusted user text, the skill incorporates testing fixtures to evaluate resilience against adversarial prompt injection and tool manipulation.

# Architecture / Specification
The issue analysis test suite in `aaif/submission-analyser` validates triage pipelines against several adversarial injection vectors:
- **Instruction Overrides**: Input payloads that attempt to overwrite system instructions or extract confidential prompt configurations [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6].
- **Synthesized Tool Invocations**: Markdown or XML blocks simulating fake tool calls (e.g., `<function_calls>` or `tool_call` JSON) to hijack agent actions and exfiltrate environment data [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f].
- **Concealed Comment Directives**: Instructions hidden within HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) or expandable `<details>` blocks attempting to silently alter severity and review statuses [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].
- **Obfuscation and Role-Playing**: Bidirectional/invisible Unicode characters and role-playing prompts designed to bypass content policy filters [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca].
- **Malicious External References**: Untrusted URLs, payload diffs, and scripts disguised as reference implementations or fixes [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd].

Security threat modeling and mitigation patterns align with practices overseen by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md).

# Lifecycle History
Adversarial test fixtures were added to the `aaif/submission-analyser` repository to benchmark and verify agent robustness against direct and indirect prompt injection during issue triage [^evt-submission-analyser-file-297ef7f1b871-f950e3d6] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-2e092a0c54ea-4363d97f] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-305b7ba8fb0c-d60ec9fe] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7385a2d6a676-148647ca] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-7cf6ee468c96-f0fe2bdd] [^evt-submission-analyser-file-a072a88a60fa-f5eaa4ea].

proposed_concept.title: PyTorch Profiler Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture documenting PyTorch Profiler instrumentation across Python dispatch, ATen backend, and GPU kernel execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
PyTorch Profiler is a reference architecture maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) demonstrating how PyTorch captures tensor execution paths from Python dispatch down to hardware GPU kernel execution.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7] It produces standardized Chrome Trace Format JSON consumable by visualization and analysis tools such as Perfetto, TensorBoard, and Holistic Trace Analysis.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]

# Architecture / Specification
The profiler bridges framework semantics and hardware execution across key architectural layers:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0ab0d50c96e0-9cea1fd7]
- **PyTorch Dispatcher (ATen):** Uses RecordFunction callbacks at op dispatch points to record operator names, input tensor shapes, data types, and stack traces.
- **Hardware Activity Tracing:** Utilizes the bundled Kineto library to interface with NVIDIA CUPTI or AMD roctracer for GPU kernel activities, memory allocations, and communication collectives.
- **Output & Consumption:** Exports execution data as Chrome Trace JSON files and formatted key average summary tables for latency analysis.

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for Linux FTrace kernel tracing infrastructure and event recording.

proposed_concept.title: FTrace Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Linux kernel-internal function tracing and event recording via tracefs and dynamic NOP patching.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
FTrace is a reference architecture cataloged by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) documenting the Linux kernel's built-in function tracing and event recording infrastructure.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1] It utilizes dynamic NOP-to-call patching to achieve zero-overhead-when-disabled function instrumentation accessible directly via the tracefs virtual filesystem.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]

# Architecture / Specification
FTrace operates within the kernel tracing layer through several primary mechanisms:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1b8b77018443-610a7fb1]
- **Dynamic Binary Patching:** Uses compiler instrumentation hooks with 5-byte NOPs replaced by ftrace_caller invocations when tracing is active.
- **Tracefs Interface:** Configured and inspected through `/sys/kernel/tracing/` without requiring external userspace runtime dependencies.
- **Tracers and Ring Buffers:** Supports function tracing, function graph call graphs, tracepoint events, and in-kernel histogram aggregation written to per-CPU ring buffers.

proposed_concept.title: OpenTelemetry for AI Agents
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for vendor-neutral agent telemetry collection, OTLP pipelines, and gen_ai semantic conventions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

OpenTelemetry (OTel) provides a vendor-neutral observability framework defining how traces, metrics, and logs are instrumented, collected, processed, and exported across AI agent infrastructure [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]. Developed as an open standard, OTel spans the full telemetry path from application SDKs through OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) collectors to analytical backends [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

Within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), OTel serves as a primary reference telemetry substrate for standardizing agent spans, tool execution attributes, and LLM gateway interactions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

# Architecture / Specification

The OTel reference pipeline separates instrumentation from storage and visualization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a]:

- **Application Instrumentation**: AI agents, LLM gateways, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers record spans using standardized `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **Transport Protocol (OTLP)**: Telemetry is serialized using Protocol Buffers or JSON over gRPC (port 4317) or HTTP (port 4318) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].
- **OTel Collector Pipeline**: Ingestion receivers forward data through batching, redaction, and sampling processors before routing to configured storage backends via exporter plugins [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1d5077c7f2d1-16c36d9a].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Trace Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open specification and reference architecture for line-level AI code attribution tracing in version-controlled repositories.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Trace is an open RFC specification demonstrating how AI coding agents emit line-level code attribution traces to track which models produced specific file edits within a repository [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]. It addresses the need for vendor-neutral provenance of AI-generated source code across multi-agent coding sessions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

The specification is tracked under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) landscape catalog [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

# Architecture / Specification

Agent Trace operates as a local-first telemetry format without requiring an active external collector [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756]:

- **Emission Hooks**: Coding assistants (e.g., Cursor hook events or Claude Code tool invocations) emit event payloads containing edited ranges, contributor metadata, and shell execution context [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **Trace Dispatcher**: A local dispatcher formats the events and appends JSONL records to `.agent-trace/traces.jsonl` within the target repository [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].
- **VCS Binding**: Traces reference local repository commits and revisions to provide auditable code provenance for downstream compliance and CI evaluation gates [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-58f77875accc-fcdb4756].

proposed_concept.title: NVIDIA Nsight Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for GPU profiling across AI workloads using Nsight Systems timeline tracing and Nsight Compute kernel profiling.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

NVIDIA Nsight provides system-level and kernel-level GPU profiling infrastructure for CUDA-accelerated artificial intelligence workloads [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]. It encompasses two primary tools: Nsight Systems (`nsys`) for cross-process timeline tracing and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) for detailed single-kernel hardware counter analysis [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

Nsight complements framework-level profilers like the [PyTorch Profiler](../resources/pytorch-profiler.md) and informs hardware telemetry within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

# Architecture / Specification

The architecture spans from framework dispatches through the CUDA driver down to GPU hardware counters [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff]:

- **Annotation Layer**: User code and runtime libraries emit NVIDIA Tools Extension (NVTX) range annotations to identify operations such as forward/backward passes and communication barriers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].
- **CUPTI Instrumentation**: The CUDA Profiling Tools Interface hooks runtime API dispatches, memory copies, and kernel launches [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].
- **Timeline vs. Kernel Profiling**: Nsight Systems aggregates multi-GPU timeline traces with minimal runtime overhead, while Nsight Compute executes kernel replay passes to measure Tensor Core utilization, memory throughput, and warp scheduling efficiency [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-6ce558ba5e3a-530b02ff].

proposed_concept.title: Datadog AI Agent Observability
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture evaluating Datadog LLM Observability, APM distributed tracing, and infrastructure monitoring for AI agent platforms.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Datadog provides an integrated commercial observability platform offering Application Performance Monitoring (APM), host telemetry, and dedicated LLM Observability features for AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df]. It delivers end-to-end ingestion, visualization, cost attribution, and alerting within a single SaaS ecosystem [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

Assessed under the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), Datadog illustrates an integrated SaaS pattern contrasted with unbundled open-source plumbing frameworks such as [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

# Architecture / Specification

The platform architecture comprises three main tiers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df]:

- **SDK Instrumentation**: Applications use `ddtrace.llmobs` to trace agent execution, tool invocations, prompts, token counts, and estimated model costs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].
- **Datadog Agent**: Host or container-level daemons collect APM spans, metrics, and system logs, forwarding them over authenticated HTTPS connections [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].
- **SaaS Platform**: Datadog ingests traces, correlates agent workflows with backend microservice latency, and presents evaluation dashboards and cost tracking interfaces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-70d9c41ccfb1-1a3eb2df].

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture covering Linux device driver instrumentation mechanisms including dynamic debug, TRACE_EVENT macros, and debugfs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux Driver Tracing encompasses the mechanisms used by device driver authors and system administrators to instrument, debug, and monitor driver subsystem behavior in the Linux kernel [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]. Positioned between core kernel tracing infrastructures (such as [FTrace](../resources/ftrace.md)) and hardware-specific profilers, it provides diagnostic visibility into peripheral devices, network adapters, and accelerator buses [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

This architecture is cataloged by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as part of the lower-level systems tracing landscape [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].

# Architecture / Specification

Driver observability relies on several layered mechanisms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321]:

- **Structured Device Logging**: Drivers log messages via `dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, and `dev_err`, carrying device context to kernel log buffers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Allows administrators to dynamically enable or disable debug logging at runtime per module, file, function, or line number with zero overhead when inactive [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Static Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`)**: Embedded macro declarations that emit binary trace records consumed by `tracefs`, `perf`, or `trace-cmd` [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
- **Diagnostic Virtual Filesystems**: `debugfs` and bus-specific monitors (such as `usbmon` and `blktrace`) expose low-level device state and request queues to userspace diagnostics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-633832607329-9b56d321].
