proposed_concept.title: LTTng-UST Userspace Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for LTTng-UST lock-free userspace tracing using compiled tracepoints and shared-memory ring buffers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

LTTng-UST (Linux Trace Toolkit: next generation Userspace Tracer) provides high-throughput, low-overhead userspace tracing by compiling static tracepoints directly into application binaries and streaming events through shared-memory ring buffers without kernel context switches or locks on the fast path.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]

Maintained by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this reference architecture demonstrates how native C/C++ applications and higher-level runtimes (Python, Java JUL/Log4j) record structured binary events formatted according to the [Common Trace Format](common-trace-format.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]

# Architecture / Specification

LTTng-UST operates within process memory and interacts with per-user or system session daemons without requiring root privileges:

- **Instrumentation Layer (`liblttng-ust`)**: Applications define tracepoint providers via C headers and link against `liblttng-ust` and Userspace RCU (`liburcu`). When disabled, tracepoints execute as single conditional branches. When enabled, probe functions write native binary payloads directly into per-process POSIX shared memory (`/dev/shm`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]
- **Session Coordination (`lttng-sessiond`)**: Coordinates registration of traced applications, manages session configurations, and orchestrates extraction.
- **Consumer Daemon (`lttng-consumerd`)**: Reads filled sub-buffers asynchronously and writes formatted CTF streams directly to persistent storage.
- **Language Bridges**: Runtimes such as Python leverage `lttng-ust-agent-python` to bind standard logging handlers directly to the LTTng userspace probe mechanism.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-75b688d43571-9301816c]

mutations.rationale: Merged WG Observability and Traceability reference architecture defining the CTF binary trace specification and TSDL metadata stream.

proposed_concept.title: Common Trace Format (CTF) Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for the Common Trace Format (CTF) binary specification, TSDL metadata syntax, and zero-copy packet layout.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Common Trace Format (CTF) is an open, self-describing binary trace format optimized for zero-copy write paths in high-throughput tracing systems such as [LTTng-UST](lttng-ust.md), [LTTng Kernel Tracing](lttng-kernel.md), and barectf.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]

CTF separates trace metadata from binary stream payloads. By embedding a Trace Software Description Language (TSDL) schema, decoders such as `babeltrace2` dynamically reconstruct packet layouts, native-endian bit-packed structures, and nanosecond timestamps without external compilation or schema registries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]

# Architecture / Specification

A CTF trace is stored as a directory containing metadata and binary data streams:

- **Metadata Stream (`metadata`)**: Plain text or packetized TSDL defining trace UUIDs, clock frequencies (e.g. 1 GHz monotonic), stream descriptions, packet contexts, and typed event layouts (fields, integers, floating points, compound structures).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]
- **Data Streams (`channel_*`)**: Binary channels broken into independent packets. Each packet begins with a magic header (`0xC1FC1FC1`), stream ID, packet size, content size, and CPU/stream context registers followed by packed binary events.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]
- **Zero-Copy Serialization**: Trace producers write native struct layouts directly into ring buffers with no intermediate JSON/string formatting overhead.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-794378d347ca-5370ccaf]

proposed_concept.title: LTTng Kernel Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for LTTng kernel tracing via lock-free per-CPU ring buffers and Common Trace Format generation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

LTTng Kernel Tracing provides low-overhead, production-grade Linux kernel observability by attaching probe modules to kernel tracepoints, system call boundaries, and kprobes, recording binary event streams into per-CPU ring buffers in the [Common Trace Format](common-trace-format.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]

Maintained as part of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) landscape, LTTng Kernel Tracing enables nanosecond-accurate multi-core correlation of scheduler switches (`sched_switch`), block I/O, network packets, and page faults.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]

# Architecture / Specification

The LTTng kernel subsystem architecture comprises:

- **Kernel Probe Modules (`lttng-modules`)**: Out-of-tree kernel modules linking tracepoint hooks directly to lock-free atomic ring buffer allocators with in-kernel bytecode filtering.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]
- **Per-CPU Ring Buffers**: High-speed memory allocations partitioned across CPU cores to eliminate lock contention during event recording.
- **Daemon Pipeline**: `lttng-sessiond` controls kernel sessions over `ioctl` control channels, while `lttng-consumerd` reads kernel sub-buffers and writes trace archives to disk or streams them to remote relay daemons.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]
- **Analysis Pipeline**: Trace outputs are decoded and correlated with userspace events using `babeltrace2` or Eclipse Trace Compass.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-a89c345fb239-c8c4744e]

proposed_concept.title: Linux perf Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Linux perf covering hardware PMU sampling, kernel tracepoints, and perf_events subsystem analysis.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux perf (also known as `perf_events`) is a hardware-assisted performance profiling and dynamic tracing subsystem integrated into the Linux kernel, enabling sampling-based CPU profiling, hardware performance monitoring unit (PMU) counter tracking, and kernel/userspace tracepoint observation.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]

Within the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) tracing landscape, perf serves as the standard interface for measuring low-level CPU execution metrics (e.g., instructions per cycle, cache misses, branch mispredictions, Intel PT branch traces) across system processes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]

# Architecture / Specification

The subsystem is structured across three core layers:

- **Hardware PMU Layer**: CPU hardware counters generate non-maskable interrupts (NMIs) upon counter overflow, recording instruction pointers and register state.
- **Kernel `perf_events` Subsystem**: Configured via the `perf_event_open()` system call, managing per-thread or per-CPU ring buffers with event filtering and call-chain unwinding.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]
- **Userspace Tooling**: `perf stat` (counting mode), `perf record`/`perf report` (sampling mode with DWARF call graph unwinding), and `perf trace` (system call tracking).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b86b123293cf-ed4113f1]

mutations.rationale: Merged WG Observability and Traceability reference architecture documenting Wireshark packet capture, dissection, and export formats.

proposed_concept.title: Wireshark Network Analysis Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Wireshark packet capture, dumpcap privilege separation, dissector trees, and structured export formats.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Wireshark is an open-source network packet analysis and deep packet inspection framework that captures raw wire traffic across network interfaces and dissects thousands of protocol layers into structured event data.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]

Documented by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), Wireshark and its headless counterpart `tshark` provide forensic packet-level observation, TLS session decryption analysis, and structured export formats (PCAPNG, JSON, PDML) for distributed network and multi-agent service tracing.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]

# Architecture / Specification

Wireshark enforces a strict privilege separation architecture:

- **Capture Engine (`dumpcap`)**: Minimal setuid or `CAP_NET_RAW` process that interfaces with kernel packet mechanisms (`AF_PACKET`, `libpcap`, Npcap) and writes raw PCAPNG capture files.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]
- **Dissection Engine (`libwireshark`)**: Unprivileged parsing engine executing modular protocol dissectors (C and Lua) to construct hierarchical protocol trees.
- **Analysis & Decryption**: Supports dynamic TLS session key injection (`SSLKEYLOGFILE`) for decrypting HTTP/2, gRPC, and application payloads.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]
- **Export Interfaces**: Command-line dissection via `tshark` allows JSON and Elasticsearch formatting for ingestion into modern telemetry backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c562de5e6df9-6055ebe1]

proposed_concept.title: Linux Driver Tracing Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture covering Linux device driver instrumentation mechanisms including dynamic debug, TRACE_EVENT macros, debugfs, and devcoredump.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Linux Driver Tracing encompasses the kernel-integrated facilities used to inspect hardware interaction, I/O dispatch queues, and internal device driver state without modifying or recompiling running driver code.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

Cataloged by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), this reference architecture defines how driver observability spans structured runtime logging, dynamic debug (`dyndbg`), compile-time tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`), subsystem-specific tracers (such as `usbmon` and `blktrace`), debugfs file interfaces, and post-mortem crash dumps (`devcoredump`).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

# Architecture / Specification

Driver observability operates across five primary layers:

- **Structured Logging (`dev_dbg`, `dev_info`, `dev_err`)**: Kernel logging functions bound to device topology (`struct device`), automatically prefixing subsystem, bus, and device IDs in `dmesg`.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
- **Dynamic Debug (`dyndbg`)**: Runtime control via `/sys/kernel/debug/dynamic_debug/control` that dynamically enables or disables debug callsites per module, file, function, or line number with zero runtime overhead when inactive.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
- **Static Tracepoints (`TRACE_EVENT`)**: Low-overhead binary instrumentation points exposed through `tracefs` (`/sys/kernel/tracing/events/`) consumable by [ftrace](ftrace.md), [perf](linux-perf.md), and [LTTng](lttng-kernel.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
- **Subsystem & Hardware Monitors**: Hardware-level statistics exposed via `sysfs`, specialized subsystem tracers (`blktrace`, `usbmon`), and PCIe Advanced Error Reporting (AER) counters.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]
- **Post-Mortem State (`devcoredump`)**: Crash capture mechanism providing synthetic device memory and register dumps in `/sys/class/devcoredump/` upon hardware hang or fatal timeout.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-8cb302c8ed1b-a2ffbef1]

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for Eclipse Trace Compass multi-format trace analysis framework.

proposed_concept.title: Eclipse Trace Compass
proposed_concept.description: Multi-format offline trace analysis and visualization framework correlating kernel, userspace, GPU, and PyTorch operator timelines via state systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Eclipse Trace Compass is an open-source, multi-format trace analysis and visualization engine that correlates kernel, userspace, GPU, network, and AI framework traces through a unified state-system engine [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a]. Rather than producing traces directly, Trace Compass functions as an offline consumer and analytical correlation layer spanning hardware counters to PyTorch operator execution timelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].

Maintained as part of the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) landscape, Trace Compass supports diverse inputs including [Common Trace Format](../resources/common-trace-format.md) (LTTng), [ftrace](../resources/ftrace.md), [Linux perf](../resources/linux-perf.md), pcap network captures via [Wireshark](../resources/wireshark.md), and Chrome Trace JSON outputs from the [PyTorch Profiler](../resources/pytorch-profiler.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].

# Architecture / Specification

Trace Compass models trace data using an interval-tree-backed disk state system that indexes system and runtime states over time intervals [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a]. The core architectural layers include:

- **Trace Parser Frontends**: Dedicated parsers for binary CTF, text/binary ftrace, GDB tracepoints, pcapng, and JSON execution events [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **State System Engine**: Builds history tree indices allowing fast logarithmic random-access queries to machine and thread state at any timestamp [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **Time Synchronization & Convex Hull**: Correlates independent traces across multiple hosts and clocks by calculating timing drift and computing convex hulls across synchronizing network exchanges [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].
- **Trace Server Protocol (TSP)**: Enables headless server deployments queryable via REST/JSON, supporting programmatic consumption by machine learning frameworks such as [TMLL](../resources/tmll.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-c7aa6ff812ce-5a7ffc2a].

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for PostHog agent telemetry and product analytics integration.

proposed_concept.title: PostHog Agent Telemetry Integration
proposed_concept.description: Open-source product analytics and behavioral event capture backend for privacy-preserving AI agent telemetry and session tracking.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

PostHog is an analytics telemetry backend utilized by agent frameworks to collect product usage analytics, adoption funnels, and operational error events while enforcing strict client-side PII sanitization [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]. Within agent architectures like [Goose](../resources/goose.md), PostHog operates as an asynchronous, out-of-process event sink capturing structured session metadata without impeding execution loops [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

# Architecture / Specification

The PostHog integration pattern consists of three core operational layers within the agent runtime [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75]:

- **Installation Tracking**: Persists an anonymous disk-bound UUID to correlate multi-session agent lifecycles without tying events to personal identities [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Event Construction & Filtering**: Packages agent lifecycle events (`session_start`, `error`, `onboarding_*`) into JSON payload schemas conforming to PostHog's Capture API [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **PII Sanitizer**: Executes regex-based stripping pipelines across event properties to remove file paths, auth keys, tokens, emails, and sensitive identifiers before network dispatch [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].
- **Ingestion Sink**: Ingests batched events over HTTPS POST directly into PostHog's Kafka and ClickHouse ingestion pipeline for cohort analysis, retention metrics, and feature flag evaluation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d36a782a2588-bde0dd75].

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for AMD ROCm profiling and hardware counter tracing stack.

proposed_concept.title: AMD ROCm Profiling Stack
proposed_concept.description: Open-source GPU kernel dispatch tracing and hardware counter profiling architecture for AMD Instinct accelerators across HIP, HSA, and CDNA architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AMD ROCm profiling stack comprises roctracer, rocprofiler, and the unified rocprofiler-sdk for deep hardware and driver observability across AMD Instinct accelerators (CDNA architecture) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f]. It provides end-to-end tracing across the full AI acceleration path, spanning PyTorch operator dispatches, HIP/HSA runtime API interactions, kernel driver job queues, and hardware Matrix Core (MFMA) execution units [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].

# Architecture / Specification

The ROCm instrumentation architecture operates across several abstraction boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f]:

- **Application & Framework Annotations**: PyTorch and ML frameworks leverage ROCTX markers to delimit training iterations, forward/backward passes, and collective communications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **API & Activity Tracing (`roctracer`)**: Intercepts HIP and HSA runtime calls, tracking asynchronous kernel dispatches, queue latencies, and signal synchronizations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **Hardware Performance Counters (`rocprofiler` / `rocprofiler-sdk`)**: Interfaces with on-chip performance monitoring counters to quantify Matrix Core (MFMA) instruction counts, High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) throughput, and ALU vector unit saturation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].
- **Kernel Driver Subsystem**: Integrates with the upstream `amdgpu` driver and Kernel Fusion Driver (KFD) via [ftrace](../resources/ftrace.md) tracepoints (`amdgpu_cs_ioctl`, `amdgpu_sched_run_job`) to observe GPU command submission rings and fence completions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-d6cdc4e175fe-7b24cc0f].

proposed_concept.title: Trace-Server Machine Learning Library (TMLL)
proposed_concept.description: Python analysis library and Model Context Protocol server applying machine learning pipelines and anomaly detection to Trace Compass telemetry for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

TMLL (Trace-Server Machine Learning Library) is an open-source Python library and Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that applies statistical and machine learning algorithms to low-level execution traces [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b]. By interfacing with [Eclipse Trace Compass](../resources/trace-compass.md) through the Trace Server Protocol (TSP), TMLL transforms deterministic system state metrics into automated anomaly detections, change point segments, and resource forecasts queryable by AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].

# Architecture / Specification

TMLL acts as an analytical bridge connecting deterministic trace state trees with autonomous agent workflows [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b]:

- **TSP Client Backend**: Communicates with Trace Compass Server instances over REST APIs to extract time-series intervals, CPU states, memory usage, and thread activity [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].
- **Statistical & ML Engines**: Utilizes scikit-learn (Isolation Forest, Local Outlier Factor), statsmodels (ARIMA forecasting), and ruptures (PELT change-point detection) to process aggregated telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].
- **MCP Tool Provider**: Exposes analytical tool endpoints (`detect_anomalies`, `detect_changepoints`, `detect_memory_leak`, `detect_idle_resources`, `plan_capacity`) over stdio JSON-RPC for interactive debugging by AI agents [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-e04f039081a4-3b16801b].

mutations.rationale: Add reference architecture for Goose AI agent runtime.

proposed_concept.title: Goose Agent Runtime
proposed_concept.description: Open-source general-purpose AI agent framework providing local multi-turn execution, tool invocation, permission guardrails, and telemetry export.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Goose is an open-source, general-purpose AI agent runtime that manages complete user desktop and CLI sessions, multi-turn LLM reasoning loops, extension orchestration, and operational telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]. Implemented in Rust, Goose operates as a local process (`goosed` / `goose-cli`) mediating interactions between client user interfaces, LLM backend providers, and external tools integrated via the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and [Agent Client Protocol](../standards/agent-client-protocol.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

# Architecture / Specification

The Goose system architecture consists of several specialized subsystems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c]:

- **API & Routing Layer**: An Axum-based web router exposing REST and Server-Sent Events (SSE) endpoints for session state, chat replies, recipe execution, and tool proxying [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Agent Loop & Context Engine**: Coordinates prompt templating, multi-turn tool calling, context compaction, and subagent delegation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Security & Permission Gateways**: Enforces security policies using pattern matching and ML scanners, coupled with explicit [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) before executing high-risk tools [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].
- **Observability Pipeline**: Provides native distributed tracing through [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) collector export (OTLP over HTTP/protobuf), Langfuse trace integration, and privacy-sanitized analytics ingestion to [PostHog](../resources/posthog.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ebe69a7a8f5d-31c4429c].

mutations.rationale: Add cross-vendor reference architecture for GPU driver tracing in AI acceleration workloads.

proposed_concept.title: GPU Driver Tracing for AI Acceleration
proposed_concept.description: Cross-vendor reference architecture capturing tensor core activity, kernel dispatch, memory transfers, and multi-GPU interconnects across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel hardware.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

GPU driver tracing for AI workloads encompasses the specialized interfaces, counters, and tracepoints used to observe tensor matrix computation, memory hierarchies, and multi-accelerator fabrics across modern hardware architectures [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826]. It bridges high-level model execution in frameworks like [PyTorch](../resources/pytorch-profiler.md) with low-level kernel driver scheduling and hardware execution units [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].

# Architecture / Specification

The cross-vendor GPU tracing stack spans three major hardware paradigms [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826]:

- **NVIDIA Ecosystem**: Uses CUPTI and [NVIDIA Nsight](../resources/nvidia-nsight.md) for CUDA API timeline collection and Tensor Core instruction tracking, paired with Data Center GPU Manager (DCGM) for telemetry fields including `TENSOR_ACTIVE`, `SM_OCCUPANCY`, and NVLink interconnect metrics [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].
- **AMD Ecosystem**: Leverages [AMD ROCm profiling](../resources/amd-rocprofiler.md) (`roctracer` and `rocprofiler`) to trace HIP dispatch queues, HSA asynchronous signals, and CDNA Matrix Core (MFMA) hardware counters alongside kernel-level `amdgpu` scheduler tracepoints [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].
- **Intel Ecosystem**: Implements Intel oneAPI Level Zero tracing APIs and Open Source Observation Architecture (OA) metrics to monitor Xe Matrix Extensions (XMX) engine utilization and command queue latencies [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f612edccd3bb-3e43a826].

proposed_concept.title: Langfuse Reference Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for Langfuse as an LLM observability backend capturing hierarchical agent execution traces, spans, and generations via batch ingestion APIs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Langfuse is an open-source LLM observability and tracing platform evaluated by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) as an external telemetry sink for AI agent runtimes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44]. It ingests structured execution data—including root traces, intermediate execution spans, and generation metadata—to provide hierarchical visualization, latency profiling, token cost calculation, and evaluation dataset management[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

# Architecture / Specification

In the reference implementation with [Goose](../resources/goose.md), Langfuse operates outside the core agent loop using asynchronous batch ingestion[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44]:

- **Instrumentation Layer**: Implemented as an `ObservationLayer` over the Rust `tracing-subscriber` ecosystem. It tracks span lifecycles (`SpanTracker`), maps internal log levels to Langfuse observation levels, and flattens metadata into model configuration and input/output payloads[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].
- **Batch Manager**: An internal `LangfuseBatchManager` buffers observation events in memory and flushes payloads periodically (e.g., every 5 seconds) over HTTP using basic authentication[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].
- **Resilience and Isolation**: Ingestion failures or network partitions do not block or terminate the agent execution runtime; failures are logged while agent tool invocations and replies proceed normally[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-06-29**: Reference architecture published within the Observability & Traceability Working Group landscape for Langfuse v2.x integrations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-f704e4b7956f-e57d4c44].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Agent skill for maintainers providing structured first-pass GitHub issue triage, root-cause analysis, and threat-modeled external publication.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Issue Analysis skill is an automated maintainer agent skill designed to provide structured first-pass GitHub issue triage, duplicate detection, and root-cause analysis without granting the agent write permissions to target source repositories[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]. It operates on untrusted public issue submissions, retrieves matching historical analyses from a curated project corpus, and publishes summaries to external maintainer destinations such as Google Docs and Discord[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].

# Architecture / Specification

## Threat Model & Security Boundaries

Because anyone on the public internet can file an issue, issue titles, descriptions, and comments are treated strictly as untrusted data rather than instructions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901]:

- **Prompt Injection Defense**: Issues are presented within delimited data blocks. If indirect prompt injection is suspected, the agent reports the attempt via `injectionSuspected: true` and logs details in `injectionNotes` while proceeding with technical triage[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Read-Only Sandbox Execution**: The agent cannot modify, create, or delete repository files, nor make unapproved network calls or access ambient environment credentials[^evt-submission-analyser-file-a54ff182c7e8-7be29901].
- **Cross-Repository Trust Boundary**: The analysis agent runs in an isolated runner repository. Target repositories trigger analyses via GitHub `workflow_dispatch` using fine-grained tokens with `Actions: write` scope only, preventing target repositories from rewriting analyst workflow definitions or exfiltrating publishing credentials[^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6][^evt-submission-analyser-file-9fd5455b8db0-50f35660].
- **Supply Chain Hardening**: GitHub Actions workflows pin all third-party dependencies to immutable full commit SHAs, and verification is tested offline with mock model providers without secrets[^evt-submission-analyser-file-b803fcb7f17e-c4652926].

## Reference Corpus Retrieval

The skill reads frontmatter metadata (`tags`, `components`, `severity`) across historical analyses, selects the most relevant precedents (typically 3–5 items), and feeds them into context to guide project-specific judgment[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03**: Initial specification and threat model merged for Flue 2.0-based issue analyst implementations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-562ca4e251fc-8c9734e5][^evt-submission-analyser-file-6ae19f00f4c0-5634c5c6].

proposed_concept.title: Issue Analysis Skill
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skill providing structured GitHub issue triage, rubric evaluation, and report drafting without repository write access.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Issue Analysis Skill provides a standardized prompt, rubric, and template package for automated agent evaluation of newly opened GitHub issues and project submissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Designed for execution within the Flue 2.0 runtime, the skill isolates analysis templates and reference examples to maintain deterministic evaluations across diverse submissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill implements progressive context disclosure through Flue's `useSkill()` pattern[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]:
- **Catalog Entry**: Mounts a single catalog line in the model's system prompt to minimize idle context token consumption[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec].
- **Activation**: Full instructions and schema constraints are injected only upon the model invoking `activate_skill`[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec].
- **Reference Retrieval**: Supporting review references (including synthetic bug, feature request, and security reviews) remain unread on disk until explicitly referenced[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].
- **Security and Injection Handling**: Schema definitions require explicit `injectionSuspected` flags and diagnostic notes rather than failing silently when adversarial prompts are detected in untrusted issue bodies[^evt-submission-analyser-file-5c6a1301c6b5-a75aa6c4].

# References
- [Submission Analyser](../resources/submission-analyser.md)

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing Flue 2.0 and GitHub Copilot inference to triage repository submissions into Google Docs and Discord.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Submission Analyser is an automated, headless GitHub Actions agent developed by AAIF to evaluate incoming issue submissions from external repositories without repository write privileges[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec]. Built on top of the Flue 2.0 runtime and Pi model provider framework, the agent runs analysis routines across GitHub Copilot endpoints and outputs formatted reports to Google Docs and Discord notifications[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

# Architecture / Specification
The analyzer operates with strict privilege separation and deterministic dispatch orchestration:
- **Trigger Model**: Invoked via `workflow_dispatch` from a central tooling repository (`aaif/submission-analyser`) rather than standard repository-local `on: issues` triggers[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. Target repositories dispatch analysis events targeting specific issue numbers across public or private boundaries[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f][^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].
- **Zero-Write Threat Mitigation**: The workflow requests only `contents: read` and `copilot-requests: write` permissions[^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f]. By eliminating `issues: write` tokens, prompt-injection attacks contained within issue descriptions cannot manipulate repository contents, issue trackers, or workflow configurations[^evt-submission-analyser-file-3dc5dd454e08-fa24a9ec][^evt-submission-analyser-file-cbe7142ed7e3-716e943f].
- **Inference and Token Exchange**: LLM inference requests are authenticated using GitHub Actions tokens with Copilot entitlements exchanged via internal token routes (`https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`)[^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c][^evt-submission-analyser-file-31e1ac583aa4-9cc8bb73]. Primary execution defaults to `github-copilot/claude-opus-4.7` with automated failover to `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` on upstream failure[^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e][^evt-submission-analyser-file-4a20043f76a6-7597f83c].
- **Integrations**: Output documents are generated via Google Drive multipart file uploads using service account credentials, followed by fire-and-forget notifications over Discord webhooks configured with suppressed mention parsing[^evt-submission-analyser-file-973b5680342c-d651657e].

# References
- [Issue Analysis Skill](../skills/issue-analysis.md)

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Architecture Principles
proposed_concept.description: Eight core design principles governing the composition of capability roles, boundary controls, and patterns in AAIF workflow reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflow Architecture Principles provide shared design guidance for composing patterns, capability roles, and boundary controls into vendor-neutral reference architectures within the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]. Rather than prescribing specific model providers, cloud hosts, or agent frameworks, the principles establish enforceable boundaries and structural guarantees for AI-assisted business processes.

# Architecture / Specification

The framework defines eight core design principles[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-9dabf9708248-88f92181]:

1. **Design around practitioner jobs, not agent count**: Name architectures by the operational job and guarantees required (e.g., human-approved operation, bounded autonomous remediation) rather than agent topology.
2. **Prefer the smallest safe amount of autonomy**: Retain deterministic workflow control over admission, scope limits, policy checks, external effects, and terminal outcomes, restricting model reasoning to non-deterministic interpretation or generation.
3. **Make authority and external effects explicit**: Clearly separate proposal generation, evaluation, authorization, execution, and state ownership roles.
4. **Protect consequential effects structurally**: Prevent agents from directly executing high-impact side effects by enforcing policy gates, constrained credentials, or patterns such as the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md).
5. **Design for failure, recovery, and explicit outcomes**: Define explicit terminal outcomes, retry behavior, reconciliation paths, timeouts, and state preservation for non-happy path conditions.
6. **Compose reusable patterns; do not duplicate their guarantees**: Reference established patterns and focus architecture documentation on composition-level integration risks.
7. **Keep requirements portable and implementation-neutral**: Specify abstract capability roles (e.g., durable state store, constrained executor) before product choices.
8. **Validate guidance against real scenarios**: Ground reference architectures in worked real-world scenarios and validation records.

# References

- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)
- [Human Approval Gate Pattern](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent telemetry standards, multi-agent execution tracing, cross-layer system observability, and behavioral auditing.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates standards, reference architectures, and semantic conventions for monitoring, profiling, and auditing agentic AI workloads across all computational layers[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512]. Its scope spans application-level agent telemetry, multi-agent session tracking, execution replays, runtime debugging, and deep cross-layer correlation encompassing user-space runtimes, Linux kernel events, and hardware accelerator telemetry.

# Architecture / Specification

The working group's scope and technical focus areas include:

- **Full-Stack Observability Stack**: Investigating a five-layer observability model addressing gaps where application-layer tracing (such as standard [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)) lacks visibility into underlying network, operating system, and hardware accelerator operations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Focus Groups**: Conducting specialized workstreams, including *Protocols and Primitives* as well as *State, Context, and Reasoning*[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Agent Trace and Behavioral Models**: Developing standardized formats for agent execution tracking, session-level attribution, and immutable execution artifacts (such as Agent Action Capsules and Merkle link graphs)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Defining unified observability terminology in coordination with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-04-15**: Working Group approved its formal charter and submitted it for [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) review[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-2].
- **2026-08-19**: Group reviewed 5-layer observability gap analysis and established open focus groups for Protocols/Primitives and State/Context/Reasoning[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-46582f69bbb5-d989d512].

# References

- [OpenTelemetry Reference Architecture](../resources/opentelemetry.md)
- [Agent Trace Standard](../standards/agent-trace.md)
- [Technical Committee Governance](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy Contributions skill (`aaif-taxonomy-contributions`) guides automated agents in preparing, validating, and routing submissions to the AAIF Common Taxonomy and Landscape workstream [^evt-public-agents-pr-3]. It codifies repository contribution rules, schema constraints, and triage workflows to ensure third-party landscape entries and terminology definitions meet baseline quality standards before submission [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill encapsulates contribution logic across several verification stages [^evt-public-agents-pr-3]:
- **Pre-Drafting Checks**: Inspects the target repository for in-flight issues or pull requests proposing identical terms or landscape components to prevent duplicates [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Routing Rules**: Directs agents to appropriate submission channels (e.g., structured `Define` issue templates versus weekly sync agenda items for deferred definition fields) [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Schema Conformance**: Strips marketing superlatives from landscape descriptions, validates required fields (including undocumented live fields like `logo`), and verifies term syntax against the data schema [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].
- **Dynamic Documentation Retrieval**: Instructs agents to fetch live repository guidelines prior to drafting, degrading safely when upstream workstream schemas evolve [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed in PR #3 within the `public-agents` repository to streamline multi-step agent triage for `aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape` contributions [^evt-public-agents-pr-3].

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group coordinating agent telemetry standards, multi-agent execution tracing, cross-layer profiling, and tamper-evident audit evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates vendor-neutral telemetry, execution tracing, and compliance-grade audit standards across the agentic AI lifecycle [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30]. The group establishes semantic conventions, trace schemas, and integrity verification models to capture hierarchical multi-agent workflows, tool invocations, and runtime execution state across diverse infrastructure layers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group focuses on several core architectural and operational areas:
- **Safety and Compliance Use Cases**: Codifies requirements for tamper-evident audit records (Use Case E4), including Merkle-chained event logs, Write Once Read Many (WORM) storage, RFC 3161 timestamps, approval chain verifications, and standardized evidence-grade ladders (E0 Declared to E4 Anchored) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- **Action Accountability**: Evaluates orthogonal accountability primitives, such as `action_ref` (IETF draft-etcheverry-action-ref) and Mycelium Trails, to enable post-hoc third-party verifiability of discrete agent actions [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23].
- **Standards Coordination and Liaisons**: Maintains structured intake trackers and liaison rosters to align with OpenTelemetry GenAI, W3C Trace Context, OWASP AOS, Model Context Protocol (MCP), AGNTCY, and internal groups including [`working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape`](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].
- **Telemetry Standardization**: Defines OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for agent spans, tool interactions, and session trace models.

# Lifecycle History
- Established under the AAIF Technical Committee.
- Added Use Case E4 (Tamper-Evident Evidence for Audit and Dispute Resolution) and integrity priorities to the use-case catalog [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-30].
- Integrated action verification surveys and established cross-WG liaison trackers [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-23] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-11].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow models, runtime coordination patterns, and reference architectures for enterprise agent integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group establishes standardized workflow representations, execution patterns, and architectural blueprints for integrating autonomous and human-in-the-loop agents into enterprise systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b]. The group aligns execution models with common taxonomy definitions, providing formal specifications for agent workflows, role boundaries, and control overlays [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives reference specifications across several key workstreams:
- **Single-Agent Workflow Reference Architecture (SAW-RA)**: Develops documentation blueprints and reference models covering architectural foundations, invariant rules, primitive catalogs, pattern selection, enterprise control overlays, and operational lifecycle governance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
- **Critical Use Cases and Schemas**: Maintains a catalog of critical agentic use cases standardized around activity-based execution modeling, replacing sequential step terminology with taxonomy-aligned "Activity" units [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].
- **Process Integration Patterns**: Defines compositional rules and runtime components for integrating agents with legacy enterprise orchestration engines, event brokers, and human approval gates.

# Lifecycle History
- Established under the AAIF Technical Committee.
- Formalized SAW-RA documentation blueprint structure for reference architectures [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-4196f7be533b-30a5187b].
- Harmonized use-case schemas with taxonomy standards by adopting "Activity" nomenclature [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-32].

proposed_concept.title: Durable Wait
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern converting blocking process waits into persisted, discoverable state records that survive host restarts and resume upon correlated external events.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Durable Wait pattern transforms a physical, thread-blocking wait into a logical, recorded park state so that long-running workflows can outlive transient host processes[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7]. While parked, the workflow state record is the entire representation of the run, allowing underlying compute instances to terminate or redeploy without losing progress[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].

# Architecture / Specification
When an execution reaches a wait condition (such as awaiting a human approval gate, external webhook, or timer), the execution engine records its execution state, activity position, and correlation identity before parking the run[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].

Core invariants required for any compliant implementation include[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7]:
- **Process Survival**: A parked run survives process death, restarts, and infrastructure deployments.
- **Context Restoration**: Resume operations restore the exact activity position, inputs, and intermediate state context without requiring recomputation.
- **Idempotency**: Duplicate wake-up event deliveries result in a single, idempotent resumption.
- **Discoverability**: Parked runs remain queryable and discoverable across engine restarts.

# References
- Complements [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7fc9dc05d148-f1943cf7].
- Adheres to [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md).

proposed_concept.title: Project Proposal Process
proposed_concept.description: Operating procedure defining the intake workflow, Technical Committee engagement bars, voting stages, and legal onboarding for prospective AAIF projects.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Project Proposal Process defines the operating workflow for proposing, reviewing, approving, and onboarding open-source projects into the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]. Serving as the practical implementation of the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md), it defaults to asynchronous evaluation and automated compliance checks to ensure thorough review across a distributed committee[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

# Architecture / Specification
The lifecycle operates through distinct sequential and parallel stages[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a]:
1. **Initial Intake**: The CTO and automated intake agents perform technical compliance checks, initial smoke testing, and chair reviews via GitHub issues.
2. **TC Q&A Window**: An asynchronous review period requiring a minimum engagement bar from [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) members. If the engagement threshold is not met, an on-demand TC supporter is assigned to champion the proposal.
3. **Parallel Contributor Paperwork**: Contributor licensing and governance documents are initiated via the LF PMO.
4. **TC Vote**: The Technical Committee votes asynchronously via LFX Vote on admission and initial stage placement (Sandbox, Growth, or Impact).
5. **Governing Board Approval**: The Governing Board reviews and votes on organizational readiness and resource allocations.
6. **Legal & Technical Onboarding**: Final technical charters, trademark assignments, and repository ownership transfers are completed by LF Legal and LF IT.

# References
- Implements the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].
- Administered by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)[^evt-technical-committee-file-05a7e66403db-81ecc37a].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Workflow Patterns Comparison
proposed_concept.description: Comparative taxonomy and operational analysis evaluating agentic workflow orchestration patterns, complexity tiers, and agency levels across major AI ecosystems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Workflow Patterns Comparison is a reference analysis cataloging agentic workflow design patterns across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Anthropic architectures[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab]. It classifies patterns by agency level, operational complexity, cost implications, and control guarantees to assist engineers in selecting appropriate workflow topologies[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].

# Architecture / Specification
The resource categorizes patterns across standard orchestration tiers[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab]:
- **Augmented and Deterministic**: Prompt Chaining, Routing, and LLM-Augmented Workflows featuring deterministic activity paths with model-driven classification and programmatic validation gates.
- **Autonomous & ReAct**: Single-Agent ReAct and autonomous loop patterns executing dynamic tool selection, memory lookups, and environmental feedback.
- **Multi-Agent Coordination**: Sequential pipelines, parallel fan-out/fan-in, coordinator-worker delegations, hierarchical task decompositions, and swarm debate roundtables.
- **Control & Review**: Review-and-critique loops, iterative refinement, and human-in-the-loop approval gates for safety and auditability.

Following working group conventions, workflow sub-steps are formally specified as activities to maintain alignment across the AAIF taxonomy[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-33].

# References
- Maintained by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-d47ac6a6752f-a44a75ab].
- Aligned with [Workflow Architecture Principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md).

mutations.rationale: Add the deterministic acceptance gate pattern introduced by the Workflows & Process Integration Working Group reference architecture workstream.

proposed_concept.title: Deterministic Acceptance Gate
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern evaluating candidate agent outputs against explicit, repeatable checks and scope rules rather than model self-assessment.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Deterministic Acceptance Gate is an architectural pattern that decides whether an agent-generated candidate result is permitted to advance by applying explicit, repeatable criteria rather than relying on model self-assessment [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658]. In agentic workflows, self-evaluation by the generating model is vulnerable to confident hallucination and unwarranted self-certification; this pattern enforces external verification via test suites, contracts, schema validations, and policy constraints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern requires three core capabilities: a deterministic evaluator, a policy/scope validator, and an evidence store [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    I["Candidate result + declared scope"] --> G["Run explicit checks and validate policy"]
    G -->|"accepted and scope-valid"| E["Record acceptance evidence"]
    G -->|"not accepted or insufficient evidence"| W["Return gate result to workflow control"]
```

### Key Invariants

- **Pre-declared Criteria:** Acceptance criteria and allowable scopes are established before candidate evaluation begins [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Independence:** The evaluator operates strictly independently of the model or agent that produced the candidate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Cryptographic/Digest Binding:** Verification evidence is permanently bound to the specific version or digest of the candidate artifact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Dual Validation:** A result must pass both deterministic technical checks and scope/policy validation; passing tests alone is insufficient if the change exceeds allowed boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].
- **Fail-Closed:** Missing, failed, or ambiguous validation results default to non-acceptance [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-970f1ea4eefc-f3be8658].

# Lifecycle History

Introduced by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) as part of the bounded autonomous remediation reference architecture [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26] alongside [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md) and [Proposal/Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md).

mutations.rationale: Add the bounded convergence loop pattern establishing controlled agent retry loops governed by deterministic evaluation and explicit budgets.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Convergence Loop
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern safely iterating an agent-driven task within explicit budget limits until a deterministic acceptance gate passes or a safe terminal outcome occurs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Bounded Convergence Loop is an orchestration pattern for multi-attempt agent tasks—such as dependency remediation, type fixing, or documentation corrections—that ensures iterations operate within strict computational budgets and terminate safely [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0]. Rather than granting an agent open-ended execution autonomy or letting it decide when a task is finished, the loop evaluates each candidate attempt against an external [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern integrates a workflow engine, a bounded agent/tool execution environment, a deterministic gate, a state store, and an audit logger [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Admit bounded task"] --> B["Agent attempts permitted work"]
    B --> G["Deterministic gate evaluates result"]
    G -->|"accepted"| E["Exit to controlled effect"]
    G -->|"not accepted"| C{"Configured retry criteria permit?"}
    C -->|"yes"| B
    C -->|"no"| S["Escalate, stop, or fail"]
```

### Invariants

- **Explicit Scope and Acceptance:** The problem scope, tool permissions, and completion criteria are locked before the loop starts [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
- **No Model Self-Convergence:** The agent cannot declare its own success; only the deterministic gate can confirm convergence [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
- **Mandatory Budgets:** Every loop execution requires an iteration limit and at least one cost or time ceiling [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
- **Recorded State & Resumption:** Attempt counters, gate outcomes, and terminal escalation reasons are recorded; workflow restarts resume from persisted state without resetting consumed budgets [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].
- **Controlled Downstream Effect:** Upon gate acceptance, the resulting effect is executed through a separate controlled executor rather than direct agent privileges [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-dc0b08806fbd-19da1bf0].

# Lifecycle History

Established within the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) reference architecture workstream as a foundational pattern for bounded autonomous operations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-26].

mutations.rationale: Add the proposal/execution split pattern separating probabilistic agent intent from deterministic authorization and execution.

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern enforcing authorization and attribution at protected boundaries by separating agent intent generation, policy authorization, and effect execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Proposal/Execution Split is a core security and orchestration pattern that decouples probabilistic intent generation from authorization and execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]. Because agent reasoning is probabilistic and non-deterministic, systems cannot allow models to directly execute protected or irreversible side effects (such as payments, configuration modifications, or code pushes); instead, the agent emits an immutable proposal that is evaluated by an authorization gate and executed by a separate workflow-controlled system [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern enforces three distinct functional roles and records each transition independently [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950]:

1. **Proposer (Agent):** Produces immutable structured data describing intended changes without having the capability to execute them [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
2. **Authorization Authority (Human or Policy Engine):** Inspects the exact proposed data and grants or rejects permission using explicit policy rules or human approval gates [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].
3. **Executor (System):** A deterministic, workflow-controlled runtime that executes authorized proposals and records cryptographic proof of the outcome [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-e3cb5264d4e0-5b43d950].

### Relationships to Other Patterns

The pattern composes with [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md) and [Durable Wait](durable-wait.md) for human-in-the-loop workflows, and with [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [Bounded Convergence Loop](bounded-convergence-loop.md) for autonomous remediation pipelines [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

# Lifecycle History

Documented as an architectural invariant in the Reference Architectures Workstream of the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-7443f6b14b82-702c4424].

proposed_concept.title: Workflows and Process Integration Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared workflow models, runtime coordination patterns, and activity-based execution taxonomies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group tasked with establishing shared workflow execution models, coordination patterns, and taxonomy definitions for agentic workflows.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f] The group focuses on formalizing concepts around agent execution, lifecycle control, and enterprise system integration.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group maintains core taxonomy definitions for agentic workflows, organizing execution and control structures across key areas:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]

- **Foundational Concepts**:
  - *Activity*: A single, bounded task with defined inputs and outputs that can be tracked to completion.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]
  - *Workflow*: The primary unit of structured, multi-activity work with a defined goal and outcome, composed of activities, relationships, and execution logic.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
  - *Workflow Execution*: A runtime instance of a workflow definition maintaining its own state and lifecycle.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
  - *Workflow State & Context*: Runtime conditions, inputs, shared metadata, and execution history across activity boundaries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Execution & Control**: Covers control flow, trigger mechanisms, lifecycle transitions, state durability across failures, and determinism properties.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]
- **Coordination Models & Roles**: Defines orchestration, choreography, composition patterns, role assignments, agent cards, and human-in-the-loop interactions.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-612fd92abd3a-7d19866f]

# Lifecycle History
- The working group refactored its core taxonomy to adopt "Activity" as the foundational primitive instead of "Workflow Step" or "Workflow Task" to prevent circular definitions with Workflow.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-31]
- Vocabulary proposals coordinate directly with the cross-group initiative in `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

proposed_concept.title: Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream
proposed_concept.description: Cross-WG initiative establishing unified agentic AI terminology, landscape categorizations, and formal concept definitions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg).[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2] The workstream establishes unified agentic AI terminology, standard definition frameworks, and landscape maps across all participating foundation working groups.

# Architecture / Specification
The workstream conducts structured terminology reviews, categorizations, and definition drafting across multiple foundational domains:[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- **Domain Coverage**: Reconciles candidate terms from Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment, Security & Privacy, `../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`, `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`, `../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md`, and `../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- **Definition Reviews**: Enforces formal relational drafting, establishing explicit boundaries between adjacent concepts such as Skill vs. Tool, Kill Switch vs. Reversibility, Harness vs. Meta-harness, and Delegation vs. Handoff.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- **Landscape Categorization**: Evaluates domain additions including Attestation & Verifiable Evidence (AVE) and execution harnesses.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

# Lifecycle History
- During August 2026, the workstream evaluated 53 candidate terms, keeping 37 and culling 15, while advancing 19 accepted definitions into pull request reviews.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- The definition for `Harness` merged, while definition proposals for `Human in the loop`, `Meta-harness`, and Identity & Trust advanced through review sessions.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]
- Expanded cross-WG representation with Leonardo Galesky representing both `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md` and `../working-groups/agentic-commerce.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group chaired by Jordan Auge (Cisco) and Casper Nielsen (Diagrid).[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7] The group is responsible for developing measurement rubrics, gap analyses, and terminology frameworks to evaluate and improve the consistency and reliability of agentic AI systems.

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its deliverables into core tracks:[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]
- **Deliverable 1 (D1 - Terminology & Taxonomy)**: Focuses on domain-specific reliability vocabulary and definitions contributed to the shared `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` workstream.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]
- **Deliverable 2 (D2 - Gap Analysis & Practitioner Survey)**: Gathers empirical feedback and pain-point prioritization from agent system practitioners through structured surveys and operational research.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

# Lifecycle History
- In August 2026, the group advanced its D2 survey specification toward merge review to establish comparative evidence for agent failure modes and reliability priorities.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]
- The group opened initial review batches for D1 terminology to align reliability primitives across foundation working groups.[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-922f59c26329-135870e7]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Commerce Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) working group focused on standardizing interoperable protocols, capability maps, and trust frameworks for autonomous commercial workflows and transactions.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group develops reference architectures and domain deliverables across several capability areas:[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
- **Deliverable 1 (Capability Map)**: Categorizes end-to-end commerce capabilities including post-purchase lifecycle workflows (eligibility inquiries, remedy negotiations, buyer consent evidence, state-change execution signals, evidence binding, claims initiation, and adjustment ledgers).[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
- **Evidence & Auditability**: Incorporates bounded verdict envelopes containing machine-readable verdicts, verifier signatures, witness scopes, and evidence fingerprints to enable cross-boundary verification.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
- **Protocol Harmonization**: Maps commercial primitives across emerging agent commerce specifications, including UCP, ACP, AP2, and x402.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]

# Lifecycle History
- Proposed post-purchase capability rows (P1–P7) and machine-readable evidence contracts to inform the Deliverable 1 Capability Map and Deliverable 2 Gap Analysis.[^evt-wg-agentic-commerce-pr-6]
- Integrated taxonomy contributions into `../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md` through joint representation with `../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md`.[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-922f59c26329-fc7cfef2]

proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group coordinating agent telemetry standards, multi-agent execution tracing, cross-layer provenance, and lifecycle observability.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates technical standards, data models, and reference implementations for observing, tracing, and auditing autonomous agent behaviors across heterogeneous runtimes and system boundaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. Its scope spans application-level GenAI spans, protocol-level interactions, cross-turn continuity, and sub-L7 system and kernel telemetry [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

# Architecture / Specification

### Agent Behavior Trace Model Workstream
The working group drives a structured multi-task execution plan defining standardized behavior tracing across diverse agent runtimes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40]:
- **Baseline Telemetry & Gap Analysis**: Capturing reproducible execution traces against agents such as [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and secondary SDKs to categorize unsupported behaviors, instrumentation defects, and semantic gaps [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40].
- **Session & Turn Continuity**: Establishing trace correlation mechanics across discrete turns, dislocated traces, and conversation pause/resume cycles without requiring persistent monolithic spans [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-43].
- **Extensible Integration Harness**: Maintaining portable fixtures, test services, and contributor documentation for multi-provider API evaluations and tooling verifications [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-46].

### Primitives & Protocol Observability Focus Group
The Primitives and Protocol Observability focus group investigates lower-layer observability (syscall, network, and sub-L7 telemetry) and cross-layer provenance correlation [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611]. It also oversees evaluation of complementary verification architectures such as Agent Action Capsules for tamper-evident ledger tracking [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

### Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) Lifecycle Instrumentation
The group tracks and coordinates experimental instrumentation evaluating the five stages of ARD—discovery, provenance, governance, trust evaluation, and admission decision—correlating gateway policy decisions with downstream agent skill activations over standard [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) pipelines [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08 / 2026-09**: Formalized the Agent Behavior Trace Model execution plan, organized lower-layer protocol observability focus tracks, and initiated ARD lifecycle proof-of-concept evaluations [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-40][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-49][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-ec358f3e3170-5d21c611].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared threat models, security design patterns, best practice guides, and cross-working group security review checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group develops threat models, architectural safeguards, actionable security guidelines, and design patterns for agentic AI deployments across the Agentic AI Foundation ecosystem [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d]. It maintains cross-group alignment to verify that emerging workflow, discovery, and runtime specifications implement adequate security and privacy controls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Architecture / Specification

### Deliverables & Active Workstreams
- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: Comprehensive security baseline document establishing hardening guidelines across major agent SDKs; transitioning into machine-enforceable static-analysis rules for CI/CD integration [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural catalog capturing operational safety controls, including diverse kill-switch implementations and memory-isolation patterns [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Unified security and privacy assessment checklist facilitating reviews across the [Governance, Risk, and Regulatory](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md), [Observability and Traceability](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md), [Workflows and Process Integration](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md), and [Accuracy and Reliability](../working-groups/accuracy-and-reliability.md) working groups [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].
- **Taxonomy and Terminology**: Curating core security and privacy domain definitions in collaboration with the [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) initiative [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

### Collaborative Boundaries
Domain boundaries delineate identity and trust topics, which are routed to the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to preserve scoped ownership across AAIF deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-01**: Working group froze v1 of the Security Best Practices Guide, reviewed kill-switch pattern additions, initiated static-analysis rule development, and launched cross-WG outreach [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-5d17bf85b2af-7c215d2d].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) brand guidelines define the visual, typographic, and architectural design system for all official assets, publications, and programmatic reports.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07] The identity balances editorial neutrality and technical precision through a structured token system and explicit surface rules.

# Architecture / Specification

### Color Palette and Accents
- **Primary Accent**: The core action accent is black (`--accent: var(--ink)`).[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Spectrum Accents**: The spectrum palette (`--spec-1` through `--spec-10`) is utilized for accents within individual surfaces, allowing one leading hue at a time. Coral corresponds to `--spec-8` rather than a primary brand accent.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Surfaces**: Two first-class surfaces are defined: white editorial and black plate. Dark mode inversion via `prefers-color-scheme` is explicitly excluded to preserve intentional contrast and visual hierarchy. Base ground is `--paper`, section banding uses `--paper-2`, and panel tinting uses `--paper-3`.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

### Typography and Geometry
- **Typeface**: Instrument Sans is the primary typeface across display, UI, and body copy across weights 400, 500, 600, and 700. Monospace is reserved strictly for metadata and eyebrow labels.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Headings**: Set at weight 500 with tracking of `-0.02em` and line height 1.05–1.15 (with h5/h6 scaled at weight 600).[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Geometry**: Aesthetics are flat with zero drop shadows. Structure relies on 1px hairlines and surface tint transitions. Cards, stats, and tables maintain square borders (`border-radius: 0`), reserving rounded pill geometry solely for functional pills and badges.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

### Marks and Motifs
- **Official Marks**: Master SVG assets (`aaif-mark.svg`, `aaif-mark-square.svg`, `aaif-logo-white.svg`) must be rendered verbatim without redrawing or geometric modifications.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
- **Agent Motif**: The agent motif character is designated for empty states, loading sequences, event visual collateral, and dividers. It is strictly prohibited within governance, board, or press communications.[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]

# References

- [Design System and Tokens](https://github.com/aaif/community-events/blob/main/DESIGN.md)[^evt-community-events-file-3dc5dd454e08-ae040d07]
