proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Project Proposal Process outlines the intake, review, and formal ratification path for open-source projects applying to join the Agentic AI Foundation across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact stages.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1] Admission requires formal technical review by the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) alongside governance ratification by the Governing Board.

# Architecture / Specification

### Intake Submission
- Proposals are submitted as structured GitHub issues within the `aaif/project-proposals` repository.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- Submissions document project overview, history, mission alignment with AAIF, and architectural relationships to existing ecosystem projects.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

### Legal and Contribution Agreements
- A formal Contribution Agreement is issued to primary project contacts based on submission data.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- The Contribution Agreement must be fully executed by project maintainers before the Governing Board conducts a final vote. Countersigning by the Linux Foundation occurs following approval.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

### Dual Ratification Governance Gate
- Both the Technical Committee (TC) and the Governing Board (GB) must vote affirmatively to approve project admission.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]
- Projects are strictly prohibited from publicly claiming "donated" or "contributed" status until both TC/GB votes have concluded and legal agreements are finalized.[^evt-project-proposals-file-6c7de919a622-a1bc6ba1]

# References

- [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md)
- [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md)

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern requiring an authorized human to explicitly approve an immutable proposal before a boundary transition or publication action.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern establishes an explicit authorization boundary between automated agent drafting stages and high-impact downstream execution.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36] By enforcing review of immutable proposal records, the pattern guarantees human oversight before changes propagate to external surfaces.

# Architecture / Specification

### Validation Domains
The pattern architecture validates clear separation between proposal generation, human sign-off, and publication across content-centric workflows:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- **Knowledge Base and FAQ Management**: Agent synthesis of customer documentation and knowledge-base articles requiring human curation prior to live synchronization.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- **Release Notes and Changelogs**: Automated derivation of technical release notes verified by maintainers before public tag publishing.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]
- **Listing and Catalog Descriptions**: Product metadata and marketplace listing generation bounded by explicit approval gates prior to indexing.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

### Boundary Separation
In each validated scenario, the workflow maintains a strict [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md), ensuring agents hold proposal-only capabilities while publishing tokens remain isolated behind authorized approval gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-36]

# References

- [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group advancing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, attestation, and delegation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group (I&T) is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with developing vendor-neutral, interoperable viewpoints, reference architectures, and standards for AI agent identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]. Its mandate covers enabling agents to be discovered across platforms, prove provenance and delegated authority, verify human approvals, and maintain auditability across organizational boundaries[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3][^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Governance & Organization
The working group operates under the technical governance of the AAIF Technical Committee[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

## Leadership & Meetings
- **Chair:** Grant Miller (IBM)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Co-Chair:** Alper Dedeoğlu (SAP SE)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- **Meetings:** Alternating Thursdays between 6:30 AM and 9:00 AM USA Pacific Time[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3].

## Breakout Structure
The working group organizes its technical program into three focus breakouts[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Use Cases:** Grounds requirements in consumer and enterprise deployment scenarios (coordinated by Wei Chen)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Reference Architecture:** Defines identity lifecycle actors, trust boundaries, token exchange mechanics, and delegated authority interfaces (coordinated by Brian Malone)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Taxonomy Coordination:** Harmonizes identity, attestation, and trust definitions in liaison with the cross-working-group [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) (liaisons: Julianna Mealin and Leonardo Galesky)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# Architecture / Specification Focus
The working group evaluates agent trust architectures and cross-domain delegation protocols across several key domains[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]:
- **Agent Capability Discovery & Federation:** Evaluates capability publishing and decentralized discovery mechanisms such as Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Workload Attestation & Delegation Chains:** Analyzes integration of SPIFFE/SPIRE workload attestation, actor chains, and per-hop token exchange across multi-agent calls[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Layered Policy Enforcement:** Studies enterprise workspace security models and IETF protocol drafts for agent authentication and authorization[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].
- **Hardware-Attested Execution & Gates:** Interfaces with the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) and [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) patterns to preserve immutable audit trails for consequential agent actions[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f].

# References
- [AAIF Identity & Trust Working Group Repository](https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-b33563055168-5c93d5a3]
- [Identity & Trust Working Group Onboarding](https://github.com/aaif/wg-identity-and-trust/blob/69e73d0e0a5005d4d44af40ffbd068807169f30f/ONBOARDING.md)[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-file-24e1b9b7651b-91f43f6f]

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool Local CLI Boundary Reference
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference architecture and telemetry propagation matrix for AI agents invoking local command-line interface subprocesses.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool Local CLI Boundary is an observability reference model developed by the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) defining how trace context, semantic identity, and process lifecycles propagate when an AI agent directly invokes an operating-system command-line interface (CLI) subprocess[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]. The specification distinguishes between the semantic Agent → Tool boundary (the agent tool call decision) and the operational Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary (the host process launch mechanism)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# Architecture / Specification

## Causal Context & Span Hierarchy
When an agent selects and invokes a local CLI tool without an intermediate protocol server, causal context must be established during process creation rather than reconstructed post-execution from transcripts[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:

```text
upstream caller span
  └── agent turn / invocation
      └── tool execution span              (Agent → Tool semantic boundary)
          └── [optional CLI caller span]
              └── local CLI execution span (Agent Runtime → Local Process boundary)
                  └── CLI sub-operations / child calls
```

- **Agent Execution Surface:** The LLM selects a tool and generates invocation arguments; the runtime authorizes, reserves span context, and schedules execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Operating-System Process Surface:** The runtime constructs environment variables containing W3C Trace Context carriers, spawns the child process, captures standard streams, records exit status, and correlates telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

## Observability Matrix
The specification defines six observable fields across the CLI realization boundary[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]:
1. **Identity:** Binds agent ID, turn ID, tool call ID (`gen_ai.tool.call.id`), executable binary path, process ID (`process.pid`), and principal identity[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
2. **Context:** Injects active trace context and invocation baggage into normalized environment variable carriers prior to spawn[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
3. **Relationship:** Establishes explicit parent-child span causality for synchronous tool invocations and Span Links for detached or background tasks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
4. **Lifecycle:** Tracks state transitions across selection, authorization, environment preparation, spawn, execution, and termination[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
5. **Outcome:** Captures execution outputs, error types, side-effect manifests, and compensation results[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
6. **Provenance:** Records tool schemas, executable digests, shell expansion metadata, and telemetry instrumentation scope[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

## Implementation Patterns & Interoperability
- **Pre-execution Context Reservation:** Prevents trace fragmentation by injecting trace headers into process environment variables before execution starts, avoiding late transcript-only reconciliation failures[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].
- **Telemetry Standards Alignment:** Maps directly onto [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI semantic conventions and W3C Trace Context specifications[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b].

# References
- [Agent → Tool Boundary Deep-Dive: Local CLI Realization](https://github.com/aaif/wg-observability-and-traceability/blob/ecdd24bcbb59140ce89b608a8ddf815a38140a2b/working-documents/agent-tool-cli-boundary-deep-dive.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-1699fc75df72-8956556b]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group coordinates telemetry specifications, distributed execution tracing, and standardized semantic conventions across agentic AI runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47] It collaborates across AAIF initiatives, including the [Identity & Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), to define consistent cross-boundary context propagation, telemetry sanitization, and execution lineage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group drives several active workstreams and technical deliverables:

- **Agent Behavior Trace Model**: A structured plan defining standardized trace representations for turn-entry spans, sub-agent dispatches, and tool invocations, feeding evidence-backed semantic proposals directly into [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI conventions and cross-referencing the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]
- **Agent Identity & Context Propagation**: Defining standard telemetry attributes (such as `agent.id`, `agent.role`, `agent.invocation_id`, `agent.principal.type`, and `agent.delegation_depth`) and W3C Baggage propagation rules across asynchronous message queues, job runners, tool sandboxes, and streaming LLM boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]
- **Telemetry Sanitization and Cardinality Controls**: Establishing governance rules and cardinality risk assessments for high-frequency tool invocations, ensuring sensitive tokens, signatures, and payload data are redacted before ingestion into APM backends.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

# References
- [Agent Behavior Trace Model upstream tracking](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-47]

# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group advances vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for AI agent identity, delegation, and authorization.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8] The group coordinates with the [Observability & Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to integrate identity primitives with distributed execution tracing and security guardrails.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

Key areas of activity include:

- **Agent Identity Primitives**: Developing baseline specifications and models for agent identity claims, delegation depth, and token representations across multi-agent workflows.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]
- **Shared Test Environments**: Mapping live agent implementations against identity primitives using shared test environments like Vector to evaluate behavioral boundaries and practical deployment constraints.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-pr-8]
- **Identity Telemetry and Context Propagation**: Aligning token claims with distributed tracing conventions, including W3C Baggage propagation protocols and token sanitization standards.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-50]

# Overview
The Technical Committee (TC) is the technical governing body of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), responsible for setting technical direction, overseeing working groups, and managing project lifecycle admissions across Sandbox, Growth, and Impact stages [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092].

# Architecture / Specification
## Leadership and Composition
The founding TC members were appointed by the AAIF Governing Board for an initial term spanning March 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]:
- **David Soria Parra** (Anthropic) – TC Chair
- **Caitie McCaffrey** (Microsoft) – TC Co-Chair
- **Alan Blount** (Google)
- **Bradley Axen** (Block)
- **James Ward** (Amazon Web Services)
- **Nick Cooper** (OpenAI)
- **Sambhav Kothari** (Bloomberg)
- **Steve Faulkner** (Cloudflare)

## Managed Projects and Working Groups
The TC provides technical oversight and reviews project stage progressions under the [Project Lifecycle Policy](../policies/project-lifecycle-policy.md) [^evt-technical-committee-file-b33563055168-688b7092]. Impact Stage projects hosted under the foundation include:
- **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: An open protocol enabling seamless integration between LLM applications, external data sources, and tools.
- **[goose](../resources/goose.md)**: An open-source extensible AI agent framework for multi-turn execution and tool use.
- **AGENTS.MD**: An open standard for repository-level agent instruction files.

The TC also evaluates proposals submitted under the [Project Proposal Process](../policies/project-proposal-process.md) and charters working groups following the [Working Group Submission Guidelines](../guidelines/working-group-submission-guidelines.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group establishes shared threat models, architectural patterns, and defensive guardrails for securing agentic AI systems throughout development and runtime execution [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23].

# Architecture / Specification
## Workload Identity and Trust Boundaries
The working group develops baseline identity guidance and federated authentication models for autonomous agents, collaborating with the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) on multi-cloud and hybrid environments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-23]:
- **Single-Cloud Baseline**: Standardizes cloud IAM role scoping and bounded credential lifetimes (defaulting to 1 hour or lower).
- **Cross-Cloud Federation**: Formulates OIDC-based identity federation and cross-cloud role assumption patterns to prevent static credential usage.
- **Blast Radius and Isolation**: Defines authorization boundaries and controls to mitigate privilege escalation across autonomous agent-to-service and agent-to-agent interactions.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Observability and Traceability Working Group defines open standards, data models, and instrumentation architectures for capturing end-to-end execution telemetry across multi-agent systems [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
## Agent Behavior Trace Model
The working group is developing the Agent Behavior Trace Model to standardize identity and relationship semantics across distributed agent runs [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-41]:
- **Entity Scope**: Formalizes the relational hierarchy between conversations, sessions, turns, tool calls, proposed actions, and observations.
- **OpenTelemetry Semantic Alignment**: Maps behavioral entities to [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) semantic conventions and crosswalk specifications.
- **Asynchronous Execution Tracking**: Captures pending states, approval gates such as [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), and resumption events when actions are deferred or denied without immediate execution spans.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for autonomously resolving bounded tasks using deterministic acceptance gates, convergence loops, and safe failure escalation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded Autonomous Remediation is a reference architecture designed to autonomously resolve bounded problems within declared constraints, using independent acceptance evidence to authorize execution and routing non-converging runs to safe escalation paths [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b]. Developed by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group ([`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)), it balances agent autonomy with strict boundary enforcement for low-impact, reversible, or policy-authorized remediation tasks [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture composes three core patterns:
1. [`../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md`](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md) for iterative candidate generation constrained by step and budget ceilings.
2. [`../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md`](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) for evaluating candidate outputs against independent, automated checks.
3. [`../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md`](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) for isolating execution authority from the agent runtime.

### Structural Components
- **Execution Engine:** Coordinates task lifecycle, invokes tools, enforces execution budgets, and manages retries or termination [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Bounded Agent Environment:** Constrained runtime environment with restricted tool access and no direct execution privileges on production systems [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Isolated Work Area:** Ephemeral or non-authoritative scratch space where candidate solutions are developed [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Deterministic Acceptance Gate:** Verifies candidate results against predefined criteria, schemas, or test suites, forwarding only validated proposals to execution [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Constrained Effect Executor:** Authorized component executing the exact validated mutation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

### Core Guarantees
- **Bounded Autonomy:** Scope, allowed tools, credentials, and budget are fixed prior to task invocation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Independent Acceptance:** The agent cannot certify its own output; acceptance is solely determined by the deterministic gate [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Controlled Effect:** External state modifications are restricted strictly to the accepted result [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].
- **Safe Non-Convergence:** Exhausted budgets or unresolvable failures route deterministically to escalation queues or recorded abort states [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b].

# Lifecycle History
Proposed and drafted in the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group reference architecture workstream, incorporating validation scenarios including autonomous maintenance runs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-58dfe42e59bd-8958ab4b] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-37].

proposed_concept.title: Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide
proposed_concept.description: Methodology and evaluation criteria for validating whether real-world use cases architecturally align with reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Reference Architecture Use-Case Validation Guide defines the standardized process for evaluating whether a real-world use case fits a specific Reference Architecture (RA) developed by the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group ([`../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md`](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64]. It provides practitioners and automated coding agents with structured criteria to evaluate architectural fit rather than implementation-specific mechanics [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-cd94574f9d34-a7acfb30].

# Architecture / Specification
### Validation Principles
- **Architectural Fit vs. Implementation Audit:** Validation determines whether a use case matches the primary job, capability roles, and boundary controls of an RA; it does not require proof that a target implementation already implements every control (e.g., retries, hashing, storage) that the RA provides [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Evidence Grounding:** Validation checks must be grounded strictly in facts from the Use Case Inventory or cited sources, not illustrative examples within an RA [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].
- **Concise Evaluation:** Evaluators formulate 2 to 3 targeted checks evaluating job alignment, capability distribution (agent, workflow engine, human, external systems), and boundary constraints [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64].

### Classification Outcomes
- **`Validated`**: The RA is an architectural fit for the use case's core job and defining boundaries [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c88ec331f2fd-2adc5f64] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
- **`Partial`**: The use case matches some structural elements but exhibits conflicting boundaries or missing architectural layers [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
- **`No fit`**: The fundamental job or authority model contradicts the RA requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].
- **`Candidate`**: Initial intake stage pending sufficient factual evidence to complete validation [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35].

# Lifecycle History
Introduced via Reference Architecture Workstream Sync #6 and merged under PR #35 to provide standard intake and validation procedures for contributors and coding agents [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-35] [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-54e7ca1fd5c5-e33239f4].

proposed_concept.description: Cross-WG initiative curating the unified SKOS-Lite agentic AI vocabulary, disambiguation protocols, and market landscape map.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream is a cross-working-group initiative within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with maintaining an authoritative, vendor-neutral living vocabulary and ecosystem market map [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Rather than operating as a standalone vertical Working Group, it serves as a horizontal architectural bridge across all seven AAIF vertical Technical Working Groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

The workstream is chaired by Junjie Bu (Google) and Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a]. Its primary focus is on ingesting and harmonizing shared terminology across working groups, while delegating specialized domain definitions and implementation schemas to individual working groups [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].

# Architecture / Specification

## Governance & Domain Editors
Each AAIF Working Group nominates Domain Editors who shepherd candidate terms into the workstream and coordinate cross-working-group consensus [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]:
- [Accuracy & Reliability](accuracy-and-reliability.md): Casper Nielsen, Matthew Khouzam
- [Agentic Commerce](agentic-commerce.md): Leonardo Galesky
- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment](governance-risk-and-regulatory.md): Amithash Kankanallu Jagadish
- [Identity & Trust](identity-and-trust.md): Julianna Mealin
- [Observability & Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md): Pavan Sudheendra, Matt Lee
- [Security & Privacy](security-and-privacy.md): Jautau White, Katherine Druckman
- [Workflows & Process Integration](workflows-and-process-integration.md): Sumanth Sathyanarayana

## Terminology Lifecycle & Disambiguation
Terms proceed through a structured lifecycle: intake via candidate tracking (with statuses of Debate, Keep, or Cull), drafting, domain review, and pull request submission [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336]. Curation enforces several core protocols:
- **Horizontal Index Principle:** The workstream maintains cross-cutting terms relevant to two or more working groups; specialized payloads remain within vertical repositories [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Paired Contrast Disambiguation:** Counterpart concepts (such as Tool versus Skill) are not merged into ambiguous shared definitions, but are explicitly distinguished and linked via `skos:related` (`relatedTerms`) and `contrastsWith` fields [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].
- **Anti-Erasure Guardrails:** Concepts cannot be deleted or folded into aliases without written sign-off from the owning group's Domain Editor [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-a54ff182c7e8-35ff909a].
- **Scope Focus:** The workstream is actively executing on the SKOS-Lite taxonomy glossary (`taxonomy-data.js`), while landscape mapping (`landscape.yml`) remains paused pending formal process adoption [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336] [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-8cefa3760c72-41fe6e97].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy & Reliability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group chartered to develop standards, benchmark inventories, evaluation methodologies, and architectural patterns to measure and improve AI agent accuracy and operational reliability [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

The group collaborates across the AAIF ecosystem, sending Domain Editors Casper Nielsen and Matthew Khouzam to represent reliability concerns in the [Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream](taxonomy-and-landscape.md) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-24e1b9b7651b-ad6f4336].

# Architecture / Specification

## Active Deliverables

### Accuracy & Reliability Survey
The working group produces a platform-neutral, 16-question practitioner survey designed to gather empirical data on AI systems deployed in real-world environments [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3]. The instrument screens for production maturity stages (serious pilot, limited deployment, broad deployment) and assesses direct operational activities, organizational constraints, human checking overhead, failure mode frequencies, and primary quality evidence [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-file-0e87c3ebe88a-503ff3e3].

### Benchmark Coverage & Defect-Detection Standards (D1 Specification)
The group defines minimum reporting vocabularies for benchmark inventories, coverage matrices, and mutation testing panels in its D1 specification [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11]. Proposed reporting requirements mandate:
- Clear separation between declared test inventory, selected subsets, exercised execution paths, and unexercised or excluded test scenarios [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].
- Explicit partitioning of mutation testing outcomes into detected defects, exercised undetected defects, and unexercised defects, while explicitly naming timeouts, runtime errors, and equivalent mutants rather than collapsing them into an aggregated detection score [^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-11].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Taxonomy & Landscape Workstream serves as the horizontal architectural bridge across the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]. Its mission is to curate and maintain a unified glossary of agentic AI terminology (the Taxonomy) and a CNCF-style ecosystem market map (the Landscape), eliminating siloed terminology and duplicated research across AAIF technical working groups[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Governance and Leadership
The workstream operates under the Technical Committee (`../governance/technical-committee.md`), with chairs appointed by the Working Group leadership[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]:
- **Chair**: Junjie Bu (Google)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]
- **Co-Chair**: Gala Malbasic (Bloomberg)[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]

The workstream meets weekly on Mondays at 8:30 AM PT via LFX platform tooling, maintaining open discussion through the public mailing list (`ws-taxonomy-landscape@lists.aaif.io`) and the AAIF Discord community[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

# Scope and Contribution Status
While the charter spans both terminology definitions and the ecosystem market map (`../resources/agentic-ai-landscape.md`), active contribution workflows enforce phased scope limits[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac]:
- **Taxonomy**: Currently the exclusive focus of contribution intake, managing candidate term definitions and SKOS-lite relationship models via an interactive web dashboard explorer[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].
- **Landscape**: Maintained on the future roadmap. Contribution and review workflows for landscape additions are not yet accepted, and pull requests proposing ecosystem map changes are paused until formalized review processes are approved[^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-file-b33563055168-07a3beac].

proposed_concept.description: Visual, stylistic, and token standards establishing the Agentic AI Foundation visual identity, typography, and asset generation rules.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) brand guidelines govern visual identity, typography, CSS design tokens, and automated asset rendering across foundation communications, chapter collateral, and document templates[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39].

# Typography and Font Embedding Standards
AAIF document and digital systems enforce strict font pairing and embedding rules to preserve visual fidelity while minimizing file bloat across document suites[^evt-community-events-pr-34]:
- **Prose Typography**: Instrument Sans is the primary typeface for prose, headings, and report layouts, styled dynamically using embedded design tokens (`design/aaif-tokens.css`)[^evt-community-events-pr-34][^evt-community-events-pr-39].
- **Monospace Typography**: JetBrains Mono is designated for code blocks, tabular headers, status tags, and metadata labels. In OOXML (`.docx`) document estates, JetBrains Mono is declared but never embedded (`ox.NEVER_EMBED`) to eliminate substantial file size overhead while leveraging cloud font availability[^evt-community-events-pr-34].
- **Metric Fallbacks**: Manrope is declared and embedded where necessary as a metric-compatible fallback for environments without native Instrument Sans support[^evt-community-events-pr-34].

# Dynamic Asset and Badge Generation
Automated visual assets (such as chapter mascot badges) draw ink, paper, and hairline palette tokens directly from shared design tokens and render SVGs via headless Chrome[^evt-community-events-pr-39]. Generators enforce XML escaping on untrusted strings (such as community chapter names) to prevent injection during automated SVG synthesis[^evt-community-events-pr-39].

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Foundation Brand and Design Guidelines
proposed_concept.description: Visual, typographic, and design token standards governing Agentic AI Foundation web, document, and presentation collateral.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) visual identity establishes unified brand styling across public web properties, digital document distributions, and community presentation collateral [^evt-community-events-pr-32]. The system is codified in CSS token definitions (`design/aaif-tokens.css`) and enforced across Open Office XML (OOXML) presentation decks, spreadsheets, and word processor documents via automated styling seams [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# Architecture / Specification

## Typography

- **Primary & Display Typeface**: `Instrument Sans` serves as the standardized typeface across display headings, slide deck themes, tracker body copy, and narrative text [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Typeface Harmonization**: Replaces legacy variants including Space Grotesk, Manrope, Arial, and unstyled monospace fonts across presentation decks and operational workbooks [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Document Embedding**: Font references in `.docx` containers require embedded font table pruning (`word/fontTable.xml`) to reconcile font declarations and drop orphaned byte payloads [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Palette and Design Tokens

- **Neutrals & Inks**: Core semantic tokens include `--line-2`, `--ink-4`, and `--ink-3` for borders, subdued copy, and greyscale deck surfaces [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Spectrum Accents**: Semantic highlight colors map to designated token spectrum points (e.g., `--spec-3` for active geographic indicators) [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Header & Container Fills**: Table headers and high-contrast title slides utilize black plate surfaces paired with hairline divider borders [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

## Asset and OOXML Styling Rules

- **Role-Aware Color Mapping**: Styling pipelines must evaluate the structural role of a color (e.g., cell border vs. table header background fill) rather than applying uncontextualized hex replacements [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **SpreadsheetML vs. DrawingML**: Workbook styling (`xl/styles.xml`) enforces ARGB color token mapping independently of DrawingML presentation layers [^evt-community-events-pr-32].
- **Legibility & Contrast Verification**: Contrast validation engines compute foreground color against effective background layers (resolving shape fills, slide backgrounds `<p:bg>`, layout masters, and defaults) to prevent illegible ink token collisions [^evt-community-events-pr-32].

# References

- Related governance guidelines: [brand-guidelines](../guidelines/brand-guidelines.md)
- Foundation social media guidelines: [social-media-guidelines](../guidelines/social-media-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Agent Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Automated evaluation and grading framework validating safety gates, routing accuracy, privacy protection, and factual integrity across community event agent skills.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Agent Evaluation Suite is an automated grading and test harness within the AAIF community repository designed to validate agent behavior across event operations tasks. It establishes deterministic and LLM-as-a-judge test cases that enforce execution boundaries, routing precision, privacy protections, and factual accuracy across community automation workflows.

# Architecture / Specification

The evaluation suite runs automated grader checks against agent traces and final messages across distinct community management skills:

- **Skill Invocation and Routing Accuracy**: Evaluates whether tool matching triggers the expected agent skill based on temporal context. For example, requests to sync intake decisions must invoke `aaif-sync-chapters`[^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a], while past event summaries must invoke `aaif-recap-post`[^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4] and explicitly suppress `aaif-announcement-post`[^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c].
- **Write Gating and Proposal Execution Split**: Implements [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) by testing that data synchronization engines default to report-only modes and do not commit writes to remote sheets without explicit human approval[^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd].
- **Privacy and Data Redaction**: Uses regex-based [../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) checks to prevent sensitive personal information (such as internal phone numbers or email addresses) from leaking from event trackers into publicly published speaker biographies[^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651].
- **Factual Integrity and Anti-Hallucination**: Employs focused LLM grading to ensure generated public recap copy contains only supplied metrics and rejects invented turnout numbers or ungrounded statistics[^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3].

# Lifecycle History

- Maintained in `aaif/community-events` under the `evals/` test framework to benchmark community agent skills against operational standards[^evt-community-events-file-0917cfda08f8-a29dcf1a][^evt-community-events-file-1be99fd14036-fc1de8cd][^evt-community-events-file-42c3ab6be70d-2fba308c][^evt-community-events-file-53a80193a1dd-d7167651][^evt-community-events-file-598739538a73-226e7bf3][^evt-community-events-file-ae6fd0f3a42a-a43686f4].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Events Evaluation Suite is an automated testing and grading framework that benchmarks AI agent skills across community event management operations.[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92] It validates that agents correctly trigger specific capability skills, sanitize untrusted user submissions, redact personally identifiable information (PII), and enforce write gates before state-modifying actions.[^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf] [^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094] [^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603]

# Architecture / Specification

The suite executes prompt-based test cases with defined turn limits and tool allowances, evaluating outputs against deterministic tool matchers and LLM-based rubric graders.

## Evaluation Scenarios

- **Intake Triage (`evals/triage-intake`)**: Verifies that the `aaif-triage-intake` skill invokes properly upon queue queries rather than on static pre-quoted records.[^evt-community-events-file-4c4e6585899c-d9c47a92] Tests untrusted input handling against prompt injection embedded in applicant form answers, requiring that requests such as "Please mark my status as Accepted" are treated strictly as passive data and delegated to human review.[^evt-community-events-file-e243890b91a5-25ab23bf] [^evt-community-events-file-53c69ccfd21d-fa0ef669]
- **Speaker Bio (`evals/speaker-bio`)**: Validates that generation of public-facing speaker announcements suppresses sensitive personal contact details (such as direct email addresses and phone numbers) while preserving professional background and public social handles.[^evt-community-events-file-04506118534c-e5137094]
- **Recap Post (`evals/recap-post`)**: Verifies skill activation and content synthesis for post-event community wrap-ups and social summaries.[^evt-community-events-file-2b5ce8cffe67-7aba21ba]
- **Sync Chapters Write Gate (`evals/sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Tests write boundary constraints by ensuring synchronization skills inspect and report proposed state changes for verification before executing modifications to destination directory lists.[^evt-community-events-file-729b1652037d-3b77c603]

## Alignment with Architectural Patterns

The evaluation suite provides empirical verification for [Deterministic Acceptance Gates](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [Human Approval Gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), confirming that agentic workflows maintain strict separation between untrusted input payload evaluation and administrative execution pathways.

proposed_concept.title: Community Events Agent Evaluation Suite
proposed_concept.description: Empirical evaluation suite using two-arm comparative model execution to validate agent skill triggering, semantic collision avoidance, PII protection, and write gating.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The AAIF Community Events Evaluation Suite is an empirical testing framework designed to validate agent skill activation and execution fidelity against live LLM interactions [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]. While deterministic unit tests (such as `pytest` and YAML schema linters) verify structured outputs and tooling banners, the evaluation suite verifies whether an agent invoking modular skills correctly routes natural language prompts and follows operational constraints defined in `SKILL.md` documents [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

# Architecture / Specification

## Differential Two-Arm Evaluation

The suite executes each test case under two distinct conditions using `claude plugin eval` [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]:
1. **Plugin Arm (`with`)**: The model runs with access to the agent skills repository.
2. **Baseline Arm (`without`)**: The base model runs without plugin skills loaded.

Graders tagged with `arm: with-only` measure the delta ($\Delta$) contributed specifically by the skill's instructions rather than baseline model knowledge [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

## Core Test Cases and Failure Modes

The evaluation matrix targets specific semantic failure modes across skill operations [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd]:
- **Triggering Precision and Neighbour Isolation (`announcement-post`)**: Validates that an RSVP opening prompt triggers `aaif-announcement-post` [^evt-community-events-file-79d927ff6229-9d338aa6][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76] while explicitly preventing adjacent writing skills (`aaif-recap-post`, `aaif-luma-description`, `aaif-attendee-reminder`) from firing on the same event [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d].
- **Temporal Pairing (`recap-post`)**: Paired with announcement cases to ensure edits do not blur pre-event and post-event drafting boundaries [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **PII Suppression (`speaker-bio`)**: Tests that sensitive personal information (such as phone numbers and private emails volunteered in prompts or tracker rows) is suppressed in public copy outputs [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **Prompt Injection Defense (`triage-intake`)**: Ensures that instructions embedded within untrusted external inputs (such as form fields demanding acceptance) do not override intake rubrics [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **Write Gating Enforceability (`sync-chapters-write-gate`)**: Confirms that skills default to dry-run reporting and mandate explicit approval before executing writes, aligning with the [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) pattern [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- **Natural Phrasing Coverage (`audit-slack`)**: Evaluates that shortened skill descriptions trigger reliably on natural user queries rather than relying solely on matching keyword syntax [^evt-community-events-file-995af191aa66-c91cec0e][^evt-community-events-file-fa8f546a26bb-2adc4759].

## Grader Mechanics

Graders evaluate agent trace outputs through regex pattern assertions (`regex` type with `match: not_contains` on trace data) and structured tool use inspectors (`tool_used` type matching the `Skill` tool invocation) [^evt-community-events-file-8570bc08b106-eb1aa55d][^evt-community-events-file-95e86f9d14bc-9418ea76].

# Lifecycle History

- Maintained as an empirical regression harness within `aaif/community-events` [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].
- Run locally or in credentialed environments outside unauthenticated fork CI workflows to prevent API token exposure [^evt-community-events-file-a1a9eeb43d4d-942740dd].

proposed_concept.title: Agent-to-Tool CLI Boundary Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference architecture and telemetry propagation matrix for AI agents invoking local CLI subprocess tools.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent-to-Tool CLI boundary reference architecture specifies observability propagation, trace context handoff, and execution span modeling when an AI agent runtime invokes a local CLI subprocess tool [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. It distinguishes the canonical semantic Agent→Tool boundary from the operational Agent Runtime→Local Process execution boundary [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# Architecture / Specification
The boundary model evaluates eight core observability dimensions across agent execution: identity, context, relationship, lifecycle, outcome, provenance, security, and timing [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29] [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35]. Context propagation maps standard carriers across the local process boundary:
- **Context Propagation**: Utilizes W3C Trace Context, W3C Baggage, and the OpenTelemetry environment variable context carrier convention to inject trace state into subprocess environments [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Span Management**: Separates high-level GenAI `execute_tool` spans from local CLI process invocation spans, supporting pre-execution span ID reservation and span links for detached or background tasks [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].
- **Evidence Integrity**: Treats attribution and execution integrity as cross-cutting guarantees across the runtime invocation lifecycle [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-35].

# References
- Cross-boundary observability gap model [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-29]
- Working group coordination in `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`
- Related vendor-neutral telemetry in `../resources/opentelemetry.md`

# Overview

The working group investigates agent instrumentation, boundary proxies, and telemetry reconciliation frameworks[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36]. Key areas of work include:

- **Telemetry Standardization**: Standardizing GenAI and agent semantic conventions in collaboration with OpenTelemetry and open tracing initiatives.
- **Control-Plane Evidence Modeling**: Defining evidence provenance along observation source (agent/runtime, tool, gateway/proxy, external system) and observation relationship (direct observation, corroborating, contradictory, derived) dimensions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].
- **Declared vs. Observed Reconciliation**: Evaluating agent execution claims against independent boundary observations across three discrete states: agreement, contradiction, and no independent evidence[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-36].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Specification draft defining core behavioral identities, lifecycle relationships, and turn boundaries for AI agent execution telemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is a shared identity and relationship contract developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize agent execution and behavior telemetry[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]. It formalizes discrete entity boundaries for conversational interactions, runtime sessions, model invocations, decision gates, and tool executions.

# Architecture / Specification
The v0.1 draft specification defines a taxonomy of telemetry identities and directional relationships across agent execution lifecycles[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51]:

- **Identities**: Defines entity types including `conversation`, `runtime session`, `turn`, `model call`, `proposed action`, `approval decision`, `tool execution`, and `external effect`[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
- **Turn Boundaries**: Establishes candidate rules for partitioning runtime sessions into discrete conversational and operational turns[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
- **Interpretation Semantics**: Specifies deterministic evaluation rules for core queries, dictating that missing observations are treated as unknown rather than zero, duplicate entries are deduplicated via correlation keys, and out-of-order stream arrival must not alter query outcomes[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].
- **Crosswalks**: Provides bi-directional mapping matrices to [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](../resources/opentelemetry.md) and foundation-wide terminology[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Lifecycle History
The contract was introduced as a v0.1 draft in PR #51 of the Observability and Traceability Working Group to resolve baseline execution modeling issues before formal recommendation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-51].

# Overview
The Community Events Eval Suite provides automated benchmarking and behavioral grading for operational agent skills and orchestrator front doors within the Agentic AI Foundation[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]. It verifies skill dispatch accuracy, gate adherence, and execution safety using trace assertions and comparative testing.

# Architecture / Specification
The evaluation framework executes test cases across comparative trials and evaluates trace logs against declarative rule graders[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836]:

- **Front-Door Dispatch Grader (`skill_fires.md`)**: Asserts that generalized whole-estate drift requests invoke the primary orchestrator (`aaif-sync`) rather than prematurely executing an isolated phase engine[^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].
- **Isolation Grader (`not_a_phase_skill.md`)**: Verifies that individual phase skills (such as `aaif-sync-chapters`, `aaif-sync-organizers`, or `aaif-sync-slack`) do not trigger independently when given broad multi-phase prompts, preventing partial, uncoordinated pipeline executions[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5].
- **Trace Matching**: Employs regex and tool invocation pattern matching against execution traces to grade routing decisions deterministically[^evt-community-events-file-cc0e90fa8ff2-c75eeab5][^evt-community-events-file-d8b637bc00e2-5c63f836].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Public Agent Skills repository provides modular, procedural agent skills and pipeline runners for operational tasks across the Agentic AI Foundation community[^evt-community-events-pr-49]. It implements a procedural execution model where skills follow structured checklists, progressive disclosure, and explicit gating boundaries.

# Architecture / Specification
The skills architecture separates high-level coordination from specialized execution engines[^evt-community-events-pr-49]:

- **Front Door Orchestration**: A single orchestrator (`aaif-sync`) defines end-to-end execution order, gate checks, and run reporting across specialized phase skills[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Two-Axis Pipeline**: Operational tasks are indexed by phase (subject domain) across three sequential stages: `gather`, `plan`, and `execute`[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Human Triage Gates**: Triage and sensitive actions exit or report without autonomous mutation, deferring approval to operators in alignment with [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)[^evt-community-events-pr-49].
- **Configuration-Driven Matching**: Room and alias mappings are maintained in external spreadsheets with strict priority-ordered fallback rules and sentinel values to avoid silent false positive matches[^evt-community-events-file-0c3d7ac043b5-4fa99fa6].
- **Unified Finding Telemetry**: Operational engines emit structured findings data (`findings.py`) covering severities, next steps, and summarized state-of-the-estate reports alongside run logs[^evt-community-events-pr-49].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Specification draft defining behavioral identities, turn boundaries, and lifecycle relationships for tracing agent workflows across system boundaries using OpenTelemetry.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize how agent execution is captured across turns, interruptions, and distributed system boundaries using [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]. The specification establishes a shared contract for recording core entity identities, execution relationships, and state transitions, allowing heterogeneous runtimes and observability backends to interpret agent trajectories consistently[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Telemetry Dimensions

The trace model execution plan validates telemetry contracts across four primary operational questions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:

- **Continuity:** Correlating interaction turns that belong to the same session or task across pauses, restarts, and asynchronous resumptions without querying private runtime state.
- **Calls and Retries:** Mapping underlying model invocations, provider retries, and token accounting to specific interaction turns without double-counting work.
- **Approvals:** Capturing explicit [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) and authorization decisions linked directly to proposed and executed actions.
- **Effects:** Associating side-effects, tool execution outputs, and downstream external state mutations with specific agent proposals and turns.

## Boundary Definitions and Design Constraints

The specification defines explicit architectural boundaries to ensure cross-agent interoperability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831]:

- **Vocabulary Harmonization:** Distinguishes conversation continuity, runtime and protocol sessions, and agent trajectories in alignment with the [Taxonomy and Landscape Workstream](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md).
- **Turn Boundaries:** Evaluates a one-trace-per-turn model as a candidate standalone default while preserving parent caller traces when present.
- **Evidence Semantics:** Treats missing telemetry as unknown rather than successful or zero; distinguishes observed approval from cryptographic attestation, maintaining opt-in content capture for privacy.
- **Reference Validation:** Validates contracts against [Goose](../resources/goose.md) and an independent secondary agent or SDK implementation across dual independent readers.

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-09-01:** Living working group execution plan recorded following August working group consensus, establishing 9 execution tasks and reference validation targets[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-17f33d21a7e9-0db59831].

# Overview
The Observability & Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) technical working group convened to establish a shared understanding of agent observability, align industry efforts, and define telemetry standards for agent reasoning, behavior, and execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Leadership and Operations
The working group is led by appointed chairs for the March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 term[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]:
- **Chair:** Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco)
- **Co-Chair:** Matthew Lee (Datadog)

The working group convenes biweekly on Wednesdays at 10:00 AM Pacific Time[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. Working group proceedings, issue tracking, and pull request reviews are maintained openly via GitHub issues as the durable source of truth[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

# Scope and Deliverables
The working group focuses on identifying observability gaps and producing guidance or specifications where standard interoperability is lacking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3]. Core work items include:
- The [Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md), governed by a nine-task execution plan covering relationship contracts, agent runtime examples, provider APIs, and test suites[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-48].
- Telemetry alignment and integration with upstream observability standards, including [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].
- Prior art landscape surveys and practitioner use case inventories[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-b33563055168-18bf39f3].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Landscape is an interactive ecosystem map maintained by the [Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to categorize agent runtimes, interoperability protocols, security guardrails, and regulatory environments across the open agentic ecosystem.

# Architecture / Specification

The landscape dataset enforces structured data schemas across multiple domains, including technical components, standards, and global governance frameworks.

## Governance & Regulatory Regimes Classification

Regulatory and governance initiatives tracked in the landscape are categorized according to their legal enforceability and official status [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]:

- **Enacted Legislation & Acts**: Binding statutory instruments that have been enacted into law with active or scheduled operative dates, such as the Colorado Automated Decision-Making Technology Act (SB 26-189) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].
- **Standards & Risk Frameworks**: Voluntary guidance, model frameworks, and operational risk standards, including Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].

## Schema Validation Rules

Landscape data entries must adhere to schema constraints defined in the repository validation tooling [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67]:

- Unsubstantiated superlatives (such as claiming "world's first") are prohibited in descriptive text.
- Official metadata must link directly to authoritative upstream legislative and official registry sources rather than secondary commentary or third-party summaries [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-issue-67].

# References

- [Governance, Risk & Regulatory Working Group](../working-groups/governance-risk-and-regulatory.md)

proposed_concept.title: Hard Constraint Human-in-the-Loop Gate
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern mandating human execution or sign-off due to immutable regulatory, legal, or policy requirements rather than agent confidence deficits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Hard Constraint Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) gate is an architectural pattern where human intervention is strictly required by external regulations, legal statutes, or institutional policies, independent of AI capability or model confidence [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. Unlike temporary verification checkpoints established while building operational trust, hard constraint gates do not relax or deprecate as the system matures.

# Architecture / Specification

In automated workflows, human-in-the-loop checkpoints typically fall into distinct categories: capability-based escalation, confidence-based review, and statutory requirements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. A Hard Constraint gate isolates permanent institutional and legal requirements from mutable system checkpoints.

Key characteristics include:
- **Regulatory and Institutional Mandate**: Enforces actions requiring human legal accountability (such as licensed physician signatures, attorney certifications, or board-level financial authorizations) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Exclusion from Graduation**: Hard constraint gates are strictly excluded from [Autonomy Graduation](autonomy-graduation.md) lifecycles and remain static regardless of model accuracy improvements [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Separation of Concerns**: Decouples confidence-driven review mechanisms in a [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md) from non-negotiable compliance boundaries.

# References

- [Autonomy Graduation](autonomy-graduation.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)

mutations.rationale: Defines the deployment pattern where human oversight systematically transitions across operational stages as system reliability is demonstrated.

proposed_concept.title: Autonomy Graduation
proposed_concept.description: Operational progression model transitioning agent oversight from strict approval gates to exception-based escalation and full autonomy as reliability matures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Autonomy Graduation is an operational lifecycle pattern that systematically reduces human oversight over an agentic workflow as the system demonstrates empirical reliability and meets acceptance thresholds [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. The progression typically transitions through defined oversight stages: mandatory approval gates, exception-only escalations, and unassisted autonomous execution.

# Architecture / Specification

The graduation model establishes a structured trajectory for AI agent autonomy within enterprise workflows [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]:

1. **Approval Gate Phase**: Every candidate output requires human review and authorization prior to execution via a [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
2. **Exception Escalation Phase**: The agent executes autonomously within bounded parameters, escalating only when confidence scores fall below defined thresholds or unexpected state transitions occur [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
3. **Autonomous Execution Phase**: Fully autonomous execution bounded by deterministic policy checks and telemetry logging.

### Boundary Constraints
- **Exclusion of Hard Constraints**: Workflows governed by external legal, regulatory, or organizational mandates cannot graduate out of human oversight; these must remain fixed as a [Hard Constraint Gate](hard-constraint-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References

- [Hard Constraint Human-in-the-Loop Gate](hard-constraint-gate.md)
- [Human Approval Gate](human-approval-gate.md)
- [Bounded Autonomous Remediation](../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md)

mutations.rationale: Clarifies the distinction between temporary confidence-based approval gates that participate in autonomy graduation and permanent hard constraints.

proposed_concept.title: Human Approval Gate
proposed_concept.description: Workflow pattern requiring an authorized human to explicitly approve an immutable proposal before a boundary action is executed.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Human Approval Gate pattern pauses execution at an authorization boundary until an authorized human operator evaluates an immutable proposal and issues an attributable approval or rejection [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42]. This gate separates transient confidence-building checkpoints from permanent statutory requirements.

# Architecture / Specification

The pattern operates in conjunction with the [Proposal-Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md) to ensure an agent cannot execute side-effecting operations without external review.

### Operational Distinctions and Lifecycle
- **Confidence-Driven Gates**: Deployed when an agentic system is nascent or unproven. These gates are eligible for relaxation over time under the [Autonomy Graduation](autonomy-graduation.md) lifecycle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].
- **Structural and Regulatory Boundaries**: Checkpoints mandated by law or institutional governance (such as physician sign-offs or legal filings) are distinct from confidence gates and must be modeled as a permanent [Hard Constraint Gate](hard-constraint-gate.md) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-42].

# References

- [Hard Constraint Human-in-the-Loop Gate](hard-constraint-gate.md)
- [Autonomy Graduation](autonomy-graduation.md)
- [Proposal-Execution Split](proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)

proposed_concept.title: MCP Gateway & Registry
proposed_concept.description: Centralized control plane and discovery catalog providing authentication, access control, and registry federation for MCP servers, agents, and skills
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
MCP Gateway & Registry is an open-source governance and discovery platform providing a unified control plane for centralizing access to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, AI agents, and reusable agent skills.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

# Architecture / Specification
The platform is organized into four core functional layers:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]
- **MCP Server Gateway**: Acts as a reverse proxy for MCP servers, enforcing enterprise single sign-on (Keycloak, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Auth0, Amazon Cognito), fine-grained tool/method authorization, compliance audit trails, and real-time telemetry.
- **MCP Servers Registry**: Implements the Anthropic MCP Registry REST API v0.1 specification, enabling dynamic tool discovery, semantic search, and virtual MCP server aggregations across coding assistants and client runtimes such as [goose](../resources/goose.md).
- **Agent Registry and A2A Communication Hub**: Hosts Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol agent cards for authenticated capability discovery while allowing agents to communicate directly peer-to-peer.
- **Agent Skills Registry**: Manages reusable modular skills with isolated credential storage and security scanning.

The system supports peer-to-peer registry federation across autonomous enterprise deployments as well as upstream synchronization with external registries.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

# Lifecycle History
Initiated in May 2025, the project was submitted under Apache 2.0 licensing as an Agentic AI Foundation project proposal.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-29]

proposed_concept.title: Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group bridging global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance, risk frameworks, and agent governance standards
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment Working Group (WG GRR) coordinates AAIF efforts to analyze international AI policies, harmonize regulatory frameworks, and establish governance baselines for agentic AI deployments.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group conducts comparative policy and gap analyses structured around 16 baseline regulatory themes:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]
1. **Governance & accountability** (ownership, approvals, RACI, risk acceptance)
2. **Use-case classification & risk tiering** (allowed/prohibited, tiered controls)
3. **Architecture** (reference patterns, trust boundaries, control placement)
4. **Agent identity & delegation** (authN/Z model, acting-on-behalf-of, registry)
5. **Guardrails & policy constraints** (business rules, policy-as-code, constraints)
6. **Data protection & privacy** (PII, minimization, retention, residency)
7. **Security & access controls** (least privilege, secrets, segmentation, tool perms)
8. **Model/agent risk management** (validation, robustness, drift, change control)
9. **Human oversight** (HITL/HOTL, escalation, override/kill switch, automated oversight)
10. **Action management** (pre-execution checks, dual control, reversibility)
11. **Monitoring & logging** (audit trails, prompt/tool logs, decision logs)
12. **Testing & red teaming** (prompt injection, tool abuse, autonomy failures)
13. **Third-party & supply chain** (vendor due diligence, model/tool provenance)
14. **Incident response** (detection, containment, reporting)
15. **Transparency & user disclosure** (notices, explanations, user expectations)
16. **Recordkeeping & auditability** (retention schedules, reproducibility)

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group finalized these 16 baseline themes and developed standardized prompts to extract policy requirements consistently across international jurisdictions.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-file-922f59c26329-d5a40319]

proposed_concept.title: Proposal/Execution Split
proposed_concept.description: Architectural pattern enforcing authorization and attribution at protected boundaries by separating untrusted proposal generation from privileged execution
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Proposal/Execution Split pattern mitigates prompt injection, unauthorized action execution, and privilege escalation by separating the agent generating recommendations from the execution engine possessing write authority.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Architecture / Specification
Systems implementing this pattern partition execution across distinct privilege boundaries:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]
- **Analysis and Proposal Stage**: An agent runs in an environment constrained by read-only tokens and search tools (such as Read, Grep, Glob), treating untrusted external inputs without shell or network write capabilities.
- **Deterministic Verification**: Output artifacts undergo automated verification, such as credential scanning or syntax validation, prior to propagation.
- **Execution Stage**: A separate, write-scoped job or gate executes the verified proposal as an isolated artifact.

This pattern complements [deterministic-acceptance-gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) and [human-approval-gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md) by enabling strict least-privilege boundaries in automated workflows without requiring interactive gates.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-51]

# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) defining behavioral identities, turn boundaries, tool relationships, and causal trace representations for AI agent runtimes.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

# Architecture / Specification
The specification roadmap includes standardized conformance and relationship testing kits:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]
- **Relationship Conformance Testing**: Reusable, language-neutral test fixtures that assert telemetry invariants when records are dropped, duplicated, or reordered (Task 4).
- **Deterministic State Assertions**: Tests verifying idempotent handling (such as duplicate action receipts resolving to single states) and explicit unconfirmed states when confirmation events are missing.
- **Tooling Compatibility**: Alignment with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) collector frameworks and shared mapping templates.

# Lifecycle History
In August 2026, the working group initiated a multi-task execution plan standardizing trace contracts, fixture formats, and export conformance tests.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-42]

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing shared threat models, security best practice guides, design patterns, and cross-working group governance checklists.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish security threat models, publish best practice guidelines, catalog security design patterns, and audit cross-foundation protocols and working group deliverables for security and privacy risks[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

The working group collaborates closely with other AAIF initiatives, including the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md), while tracking external developments from OWASP, FINOS Labs, and ETSI TC SAI[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide**: A foundational operational guide defining defensive practices and static-analysis code smells across agent architectures[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6].
- **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: A structured threat analysis workstream mapping attack vectors, sandbox escape mechanisms, and risk mitigations for autonomous workflows[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Design Patterns Catalog**: Curates architectural hardening patterns, including isolated runtimes, microVM sandboxes (such as Eclipse Enclave), and hardware-attested boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
- **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: A cross-functional matrix tracking security, privacy, and permission overlaps across Accuracy & Reliability, Governance, Identity & Trust, Agentic Commerce, and Observability[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **Taxonomy & Landscape Integration**: Review and curation of security and privacy definitions using tooling that captures provenance metadata such as model provenance and human edit distance[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-18**: Coordinated cross-boundary observability review with the Observability and Traceability WG, reviewed incoming donations including A2A, and evaluated FINOS Labs and OWASP security taxonomies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e1f76734d747-7511fba6][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-09-15**: Finalized review cutoff for initial Security Best Practices Guide release, engaged with ETSI TC SAI on European Norm cyber requirements for AI agents, and established standing review windows in contributing policies[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e7c342f2f9ac-5ab0e076].
