proposed_concept.title: Observability and Traceability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining behavioral tracing models, observability standards, prior-work surveys, and cross-boundary telemetry frameworks.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body chartered to establish open behavioral tracing specifications, survey prior industry work, define telemetry use cases, and coordinate telemetry interoperability across agent runtimes, protocols, and security boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

The group coordinates standardizations across OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions, OWASP Agent Observability Standard (AOS), OCSF, AGNTCY Observe, and A2A traceability extensions, while collaborating with the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) on cross-boundary observability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].

# Architecture / Specification

## Core Documents and Workstreams

- **Prior Work Survey (`PRIOR-WORK.md`)**: A living landscape document surveying implementations, auto-instrumentation libraries, and specifications including OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, OWASP AOS, OpenInference, MLflow Tracing, AGNTCY Observe SDK, OCSF Schema 1.9, Monocle, and Cursor Agent Trace[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **Observability Use Cases Inventory (`USE-CASES.md`)**: A structured taxonomy of practitioner requirements covering nine domains:
  1. *Debugging & Root Cause Analysis*: Decision sequence reconstruction and retry bottleneck identification[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  2. *Cost Management & Optimization*: Session token accounting and waste detection[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  3. *Code Attribution & Provenance*: Granular AI authorship and review tracking[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  4. *Evaluation & QA*: Regression benchmarks and model comparative execution[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  5. *Safety & Compliance*: Authorized scope verification and tamper-evident audit logs (E4)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
  6. *Multi-Agent Systems*: Distributed tracing across agent and delegation boundaries[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  7. *Operational Monitoring*: Real-time agent health and capacity metrics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  8. *Research & Improvement*: Failure discovery and fine-tuning datasets[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
  9. *Identity & Ownership*: Cross-surface identity resolution (I1)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].
- **Cross-Cutting Telemetry Principles**: Enforcing explicit source and trust declarations, privacy minimization/redaction, completeness declaring sampling gaps, schema versioning, and causal correlation independent of parent-child trees[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-03-15**: Initial drafts of `PRIOR-WORK.md` and `USE-CASES.md` published to survey the agent observability landscape and establish telemetry requirements[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-7ac80cf9ff9c-21a525e3].
- **2026-08-13**: Mid-year landscape refresh incorporating OpenTelemetry GenAI repository split, OCSF 1.9 AI agent classes, AGNTCY Observe SDK 1.0.43, and eBPF/OBI instrumentation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-dcf5c1ecc194-085a2853].
- **2026-08-18**: Merged tamper-evident audit use case E4 and submitted cross-boundary framework to Security and Privacy WG[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-24].
- **2026-08-19**: Merged cross-surface identity resolution use case I1[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-53].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body focused on defining standardized interaction patterns, workflow definitions, and architectural templates for agentic automation and human-agent collaboration [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

In August 2026, the working group became the first AAIF working group to deliver an official asset upon the approval and shipment of its Phase One Core Terms taxonomy artifact [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

- **Taxonomy:** Standardized foundational workflow definitions. The Phase One Core Terms delivery established "activity" as the foundational non-circular primitive, with "workflow" defined as a composition of activities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. Evaluation, gate, and security checks are explicitly scoped to partner working groups such as `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` and `../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Reference Architectures:** Standardizes repeatable execution patterns across workflow lifecycles. Key deliverables include architectural principles, contributing guidelines, the "human-approved operation" architecture, and `../architectures/bounded-autonomous-remediation.md` [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7]. The workstream applies a 4-outcome validation matrix (`validated`, `partial`, `candidate`, `no fit`) to evaluate architectural alignment against the use case catalog [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].
- **Critical Use Cases:** Maintains an empirical catalog of end-to-end agentic workflows, reconciling real-world automation scenarios against foundation terminology [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7].

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-31:** Approved Phase One Core Terms as the working group's first shipped asset and established the Reference Architecture deliverable scope [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-922f59c26329-f75096f7][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-38].

- `../guidelines/reference-architecture-validation.md`

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Standardized specification and execution plan defining behavioral identities, turn boundaries, and reconstruction logic for agent telemetry across independent consumers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification developed by `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md` defining how agent execution turns, proposals, approvals, tool invocations, and external effects are represented across telemetry streams [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. It ensures that distributed, multi-turn AI agent operations can be unambiguously reconstructed and evaluated by vendor-neutral observability tooling.

# Interoperability and Independent Interpretation

A central acceptance requirement of the trace model execution plan is independent consumer interpretation (Task 7) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45]. Interoperability mandates that two independent readers or query paths parse exported agent telemetry without relying on private runtime state, proprietary fixture mappings, or shared reconstruction code [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

Key validation criteria include:
- **Arrival Invariance:** Readers must reconstruct identical behavioral states regardless of event arrival order (e.g., verifying proposal approval, execution observation, and independent effect reporting) [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Incomplete Evidence Handling:** In the absence of corroborating service receipts or traces, readers must consistently identify reported effects as unconfirmed [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].
- **Semantic Agreement:** Readers are evaluated against known expected results, and any mapping losses or semantic divergence must be documented during conformance tests [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-issue-45].

# References

- `../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`
- `../resources/opentelemetry.md`
- `../standards/agent-trace.md`

proposed_concept.title: Accuracy and Reliability Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing measurement standards, reliability surveys, benchmark inventories, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Accuracy and Reliability Working Group (ARWG) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing measurement frameworks, empirical evaluation methodologies, benchmark inventories, and developer surveys to assess AI agent precision, consistency, and operational safety.

# Activities and Deliverables

The working group maintains industry benchmarking initiatives and community surveys to evaluate production agent accuracy[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9].

## Platform-Neutral Reliability Survey

ARWG developed a 16-question platform-neutral survey assessing agent deployment challenges and reliability practices across five functional sections[^evt-wg-accuracy-and-reliability-pr-9]:
- **Eligibility**: Initial qualification screening for agent practitioners.
- **About the System**: Agent system architecture characteristics, operational models, and framework configurations.
- **Benefits and Challenges**: Perceived operational benefits, failure modes, and deployment obstacles.
- **Accuracy and Reliability**: Empirical reliability baselines, hallucination controls, and measurement practices.
- **Future Priorities**: Practitioner needs for standardized benchmarks, evaluation tooling, and deterministic verification.

# Cross-Working Group Collaboration

ARWG coordinates with the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) and [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) on empirical testing of agent behavior models and acceptance gates.

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Observability and Traceability Working Group (WG O&T) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing vendor-neutral specifications, metadata schemas, and telemetry architectures for AI agent execution, multi-agent interactions, and external tool invocations[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Focus Areas and Technical Tracks

WG O&T executes its charter through specialized technical tracks and cross-WG initiatives[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]:

- **[Agent Behavior Trace Model](../standards/agent-behavior-trace-model.md)**: Establishing portable telemetry context across agent runtimes, SDKs, and gateways without displacing underlying OpenTelemetry GenAI semantics[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Cross-Boundary Observability**: Developing metadata propagation schemas and gap models for agent-to-skill, skill-to-tool, agent-to-agent, and agent-to-MCP interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **ARD Trust-Pipeline Observability**: Defining span attributes and lifecycle tracing for the Agent Resource Discovery (ARD) workflow from discovery and identity verification to skill execution, developed in collaboration with [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) and [Security and Privacy](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Curating foundational terminology for the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), including accepted definitions for Reasoning, Agent Trajectory, Context Propagation, Memory Access, Context Assembly, Retrieval, and Traceability[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

# Organization and Working Methods

The working group is chaired by Pavan Sudheendra (Cisco) and Matthew Lee (Datadog)[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. Track coordination spans LLM Primitives & Protocol Observability, Agentic State, Context & Reasoning, while Orchestration & Coordination activities operate directly within the general WG structure[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b]. The working group maintains external liaison tracking with OpenTelemetry GenAI SIG, OWASP AOS, W3C Trace Context, and protocol bodies[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-18].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open specification and reference implementation defining portable telemetry context, turn boundaries, and causal execution tracing across AI agent systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open standard and reference architecture developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to standardize portable telemetry context across diverse agent frameworks, SDKs, gateways, and observability backends[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-38].

# Architecture / Specification

The trace model preserves behavioral context, causal relationships, and decision trajectories across distributed agent components without requiring raw chain-of-thought logging[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

## Core Capabilities and Design Principles

- **Portable Telemetry Context**: Serves as a vendor-neutral context propagation mechanism designed to augment and interoperate with [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md) GenAI conventions rather than replace them[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Causal Decision Linking**: Maps plans, tool dispatches, state updates, and observable side effects to final task outcomes across long-running autonomous workflows[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Cross-Boundary Interaction Correlation**: Standardizes span metadata across multi-agent handoffs, local CLI tool invocations, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].
- **Auditability and Verifiable Evidence**: Formulates tamper-evident execution records suitable for audit logging, compliance verification, and dispute resolution across jurisdictions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b][^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-56].

# Lifecycle History

The Agent Behavior Trace Model scope was established following a decision-neutral evaluation plan comparing existing telemetry specifications and identifying standards gaps[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-19]. Reference library development, synthetic validation suites, and conformance tests are coordinated under the leadership of Matthew Lee within WG O&T[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-922f59c26329-f5c1b95b].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing threat models, security best practice guides, design patterns, and cross-group review checklists for agentic systems.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical group tasked with analyzing security postures, defining threat models, and curating architectural design patterns and best practice guides for agentic systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. It coordinates across foundational efforts including the [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) and cross-working group initiatives with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) and [Identity and Trust](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group is chaired by Alexander Frazer (Runlayer) and Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f]. Its agenda is structured around four primary workstreams:

1. **Agentic AI Threat Modeling Gap Analysis and Framework Design**: Benchmarking existing threat modeling frameworks (OWASP Top 10 for Agentic systems, MITRE ATLAS, MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF) alongside STRIDE and PASTA methodologies, incorporating Model Context Protocol (MCP) and UI/Human-User Agent (HUA) attack surfaces [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
2. **Security Best Practices Guide**: Developing baseline implementation recommendations across agent lifecycle stages, with dedicated sections addressing HUA and coordinating identity/authorization ownership with partner WGs [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
3. **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Codifying repeatable architectural patterns and mitigation templates for hardened agent deployments [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].
4. **Cross-Working Group Review Checklist**: Establishing shared review criteria across AAIF working groups to evaluate deliverables against security and privacy baselines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-922f59c26329-785b273f].

# Lifecycle History

In August 2026, the working group transitioned past meeting recordings to public access by default and progressed skeleton drafts for its threat modeling gap analysis, best practices guide, and design patterns catalog [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22]. The group also engaged the Technical Committee to clarify working group scope boundaries concerning protocol-level security in light of incoming foundation donations [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-22].

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining reference architectures, execution profiles, and workflow orchestration patterns for enterprise agent integration.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group develops shared workflow models, runtime coordination patterns, and reference architectures for integrating autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents into human and enterprise business processes [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The group standardizes patterns balancing deterministic execution controls with autonomous agent capabilities across industry use cases [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group is chaired by Yaron Schneider (Diagrid) and Adam Seligman (Workato) [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. Its technical agenda is structured across three primary workstreams:

- **Reference Architectures**: Standardizes a framework of 7 execution profiles ranging from profile 1 (fully deterministic) to profile 7 (fully agentic), advocating a "least agentic default" architectural design principle [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26]. The workstream demonstrates a specification-driven design flow that transforms machine-readable YAML specifications into concrete architecture documentation and diagrams across multiple execution profile variants [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Critical Use Cases**: Analyzes real-world deployment scenarios (evaluating 89 distinct enterprise use cases) to extract primitive patterns such as trigger mechanics, human-in-the-loop gates, coordination structures, and autonomous convergence loops [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].
- **Taxonomy Alignment**: Coordinates with [Taxonomy and Landscape](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) to harmonize cross-WG workflow primitives, short codes, and universal definitions [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

# Lifecycle History

In July 2026, the group validated end-to-end specification-driven flows on representative use cases (invoice processing and autonomous maintenance runs), finalized a catalog of under 10 reusable workflow patterns, and prepared foundational repository contributions for voting [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-fa4050a9f626-89594a26].

proposed_concept.title: Submission Analyser
proposed_concept.description: Headless GitHub Actions agent utilizing Copilot inference and dry-run canary pipelines to triage and evaluate foundation submissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Submission Analyser is a headless GitHub Actions agent designed to evaluate incoming issue submissions, perform rubric assessments, and draft triage summaries for AAIF repositories [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10]. It executes autonomous triage pipelines without requiring local infrastructure by relying on GitHub-native workflow execution and model inference entitlements [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Architecture / Specification

The submission analyser architecture incorporates automated model resilience and permission containment mechanisms:

- **Canary Verification Pipeline**: Implements independent primary (e.g. `claude-opus-4.7`) and fallback (e.g. `gpt-5.4`) matrix legs configured with `fail-fast: false` to ensure fallback availability is continuously validated without masking silent failures [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Dry-Run Isolation**: Supports `DRY_RUN=1` modes for execution runs, analyzing and rendering output without mutating issues or publishing external documents, thereby avoiding unnecessary secret and credential exposure [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].
- **Scoped Inference Permissions**: Operates under minimal read-only token permissions (`contents: read`, `issues: read`) coupled with `copilot-requests: write` to grant model inference directly through organization-billed tokens rather than personal access tokens (PATs) [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

# Lifecycle History

The canary workflow was integrated to provide daily health verification against fragile model provider endpoints and header shifts [^evt-submission-analyser-file-4b56c7c159ef-381bcc10].

proposed_concept.title: Subagent
proposed_concept.description: Universal taxonomy term defining an agent spawned by an existing agent without inherent inheritance of identity or permissions.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
A subagent is an agent spawned by an existing agent to execute delegated tasks or sub-workflows [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68].

# Architecture / Specification
In the Agentic AI Foundation taxonomy curated by the [Taxonomy and Landscape Working Group](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md), subagent is categorized as a universal term directly related to the base concept of an agent [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68].

A subagent relationship is strictly structural; being spawned by another agent does not imply or automatically transfer operational properties, including [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68]:
- Authentication and identity attribution
- Access control privileges and security boundaries
- Execution environment or sandbox boundaries
- Permission sets and operational scopes

# References
- AAIF Taxonomy & Landscape Working Group: [PR #68](https://github.com/aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape/pull/68) [^evt-ws-taxonomy-landscape-pr-68]

proposed_concept.title: Open Responses
proposed_concept.description: Vendor-neutral specification and conformance suite standardizing language model request, response, streaming, and tool-call APIs.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Open Responses is a vendor-neutral specification and conformance project that defines standard application programming interfaces for language-model inference, output items, multimodal payloads, tool calls, and streaming events [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]. Derived from the OpenAI Responses API, it establishes a shared model-inference contract across foundation model providers, inference gateways, client libraries, and agent frameworks [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Architecture / Specification
Open Responses establishes a common inference layer within the agentic stack, complementing tool-integration protocols such as the [Model Context Protocol](../resources/mcp-gateway-registry.md) and agent runtimes like [Goose](../resources/goose.md) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]:
- **Inference Protocol**: Defines structured representations for model requests, output item lifecycles, and streaming events across HTTP and WebSocket transports [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Tool Invocations**: Standardizes how tool definitions, execution requests, and tool outputs are represented in model exchanges [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].
- **Acceptance & Conformance Suites**: Supplies machine-readable OpenAPI schemas, date-versioned snapshots, and browser/CLI conformance test suites to validate provider interoperability [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# Lifecycle History
In July 2026, Open Responses was submitted as an open project proposal to the Agentic AI Foundation [Technical Committee](../governance/technical-committee.md) under Apache-2.0 and CC-BY-4.0 licensing with multi-vendor technical steering committee governance [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41].

# References
- AAIF Project Proposals: [Issue #41](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/41) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-41]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
ContextForge is an open-source registry and proxy platform that federates Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent-to-Agent (A2A), and REST/gRPC interfaces with centralized discovery, policy governance, and observability [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]. It provides an extensible integration layer designed to manage agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent interactions across development and production environments [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

# Architecture / Specification
ContextForge serves as a management and federation plane for agent tool and capability runtimes [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]:
- **Protocol Federation**: Aggregates disparate interfaces including MCP, A2A, REST, and gRPC endpoints behind a unified gateway [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **Extensible Plugin System**: Features a modular architecture supporting custom transports, authentication mechanisms, policy controls, and integrations without modifying the core gateway [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **Registry and Discovery**: Provides centralized catalogs for publishing, browsing, and resolving available tools, prompts, resources, and agent capabilities [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].
- **Governance and Observability**: Enforces centralized access policies, telemetry collection, and compliance verification across tool calls [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

# Lifecycle History
ContextForge was submitted to the Agentic AI Foundation as a hosted project proposal in July 2026 under the Apache License 2.0 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39].

# References
- AAIF Project Proposals: [Issue #39](https://github.com/aaif/project-proposals/issues/39) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-39]

mutations.rationale: Introduces the runtime governance Approval Checkpoint pattern defined in the Security and Privacy Working Group design patterns catalog.

proposed_concept.title: Approval Checkpoint
proposed_concept.description: Runtime governance pattern binding approval records to exact execution payloads and tracking decision, execution, and confirmation states independently.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Approval Checkpoint pattern binds human or automated policy approvals directly to specific action payloads and validity constraints, ensuring executed actions cannot silently deviate from what was authorized[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]. It decouples authorization decisions from execution attempts and downstream effect receipts to maintain clear provenance across asynchronous or retried operations[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].

# Architecture / Specification
Runtime policy enforcement points validate that incoming agent actions match bound parameters, target identifiers, and digest values computed over canonical representations prior to dispatch[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5]. The pattern segregates state tracking across three distinct records:
1. **Decision Record**: Captures the approval authority, validity interval, scope, constraints, and canonical payload digest.
2. **Execution Record**: Tracks execution attempts and assigns unique enforcement point identifiers, charging against approval quota limits.
3. **Effect Record**: Logs verified target service confirmation responses, treating missing confirmations as unconfirmed rather than absent.

This pattern complements [Proposal-Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [Deterministic Acceptance Gate](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md) by providing cryptographically bound verification at runtime execution boundaries[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-8fb7a6935b72-65c58be5].

mutations.rationale: Adds the AI Agent Bill of Materials (AI-BOM) taxonomy term proposed within the Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group.

proposed_concept.title: AI Agent Bill of Materials
proposed_concept.description: Machine-readable inventory defining the foundation models, harness software, tools, and third-party dependencies comprising an AI agent system.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
An AI Agent Bill of Materials (AI-BOM) is a standardized, machine-readable inventory detailing the constituent components and supply chain dependencies of an AI agent[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]. It extends traditional Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) concepts by capturing behavioral drivers including foundation models, runtime harnesses, invocable tools, and underlying software dependencies along with supplier identity and version metadata[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].

# Architecture / Specification
AI-BOM manifests map agent dependency graphs across multiple abstraction layers, providing structured provenance compatible with standards such as SPDX 3.0 AI profiles and CycloneDX ML-BOM specifications[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10]. The inventory encompasses base model weights, prompt harnesses, tool schemas, and third-party library dependencies required for regulatory transparency and supply chain traceability[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-10].

mutations.rationale: Add the Kill Switch pattern drafted in the Security and Privacy Working Group design patterns catalog for agent containment and out-of-band execution termination.

proposed_concept.title: Kill Switch
proposed_concept.description: Architectural control plane pattern establishing an independent out-of-band mechanism to immediately halt agent execution, sever network access, and invalidate credentials.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Kill Switch pattern defines an independent, out-of-band runtime control plane that immediately halts agent execution, severs external network communications, and invalidates active session credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]. By decoupling containment controls from an agent's prompt context, internal memory, and execution loops, the pattern prevents misbehaving or hijacked autonomous agents from bypassing deactivation or leaving orphaned background tasks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].

# Architecture / Specification

Traditional process termination (`SIGKILL`) is insufficient for autonomous agent systems due to shutdown resistance, model evasion, asynchronous task orphanage (zombie processes), high execution velocity in runaway loops, and unexpired credential exposure [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01]. The pattern separates declarative stopping criteria from the technical enforcement control plane across a three-stage containment loop:

1. **Detect**: External policy engines, circuit breakers, and anomaly detection services evaluate runtime telemetry outside the model's reach.
2. **Halt**: The control plane initiates immediate execution termination across the host runtime, dispatches network isolation commands to gateways, and revokes all active API tokens and ephemeral session credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].
3. **Rollback**: Compensating transactions and state rollbacks reconcile modified resources to safe checkpoints.

### Relationship to Other Patterns

- [Attested Isolated Runtime](attested-isolated-runtime.md): Provides confidential hardware-isolated enforcement boundaries, hardware attestation, and scoped credential release, complementing kill-switch containment [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d2691d0f1f64-8e9abf01].
- [Approval Checkpoint](approval-checkpoint.md): Establishes verifiable pre-execution authorizations and audits prior to runtime tool calls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50].

# Lifecycle History

- Proposed and merged into the Security and Privacy Working Group design patterns catalog via PR #26 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26].
- Issue #27 identified an edge case where credential revocation at sidecar enforcement points could be misinterpreted as an outage by fallback handlers, emphasizing strict fail-closed behavior on HTTP 401/403 responses [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-27].

# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing reusable threat models, architectural security guidelines, privacy-preserving execution frameworks, and security design pattern catalogs for autonomous agent ecosystems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

# Architecture / Specification

The working group operates active workstreams across multiple core deliverables:

- **Security and Privacy Design Patterns Catalog**: Maintained by workstream leads Dan Kommatas (Circle) and Sagar Dashora (JPMorgan Chase), cataloging reusable architectural patterns including [Approval Checkpoint](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md), [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md), and [Kill Switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-9d8108887b54-74938a50][^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-26].

- **Cross-WG Review Checklist**: Joint initiative coordinating evaluation criteria with [Observability and Traceability](observability-and-traceability.md) and [Identity and Trust](identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-3b2755238b15-1588e821].

proposed_concept.title: Security and Privacy Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group establishing open threat models, security best practice guides, and runtime defense patterns across the agentic AI ecosystem.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Security and Privacy Working Group is a technical working group within the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) tasked with establishing security and privacy as a shared discipline across agent runtimes, tool protocols, and autonomous workflows [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. The working group develops open threat models, security evaluation rubrics, best practice implementation guides, and reusable architectural design patterns that providers and operators can implement to share responsibility for trustworthy AI agents [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

# Organization and Governance

The working group operates under the technical governance of the AAIF Technical Committee [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]. Leadership is appointed by Platinum and Gold member representatives:

- **Chair:** Alex Frazer (Runlayer) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Co-Chair:** Junjie Bu (Google) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- **Term:** March 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027 [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

The working group holds public biweekly meetings on Tuesdays at 10:00 AM US Pacific Time, with running agendas and notes managed via Linux Foundation LFX tools [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56].

# Workstreams and Deliverables

The group organizes its work across several distinct workstreams and deliverables [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]:

1. **Threat Modeling & Gap Analysis:** Evaluates established AI security frameworks (e.g., CSA MAESTRO, OWASP, NIST AI RMF) against agentic-specific threat surfaces such as multi-agent persuasion, dynamic tool invocation, delegated authorization, and prompt-injection supply chain risks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85]. Led by Alon Mazor (Ocean Security) and Fernando Lucktemberg (SAP) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-0e2b23067e13-ece26d85].
2. **Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide:** Practical architectural guidance covering secrets management, Model Context Protocol (MCP) transport hardening, skill verification, input/output guardrails, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157]. Led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
3. **Design Patterns Catalog:** Reference catalog capturing architectural mitigations such as [../patterns/kill-switch.md](../patterns/kill-switch.md) and [../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].
4. **Cross-WG Collaboration:** Contributes security and privacy terminology to the [../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md](../working-groups/taxonomy-and-landscape.md) workstream [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-a9e41c531556-11747157], coordinates identity delegation and credential tokens with [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b], and aligns on telemetry integrity with [../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-d7a6875f36a3-5484c59b].

# References

- Repository: [aaif/wg-security-and-privacy](https://github.com/aaif/wg-security-and-privacy) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]
- Working group mailing list: `wg-security-privacy@lists.aaif.io` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b33563055168-511b4a56]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide
proposed_concept.description: Technical guidance consolidating practical security controls across secrets elimination, MCP protocol hardening, skill supply-chain verification, guardrails, and forensics.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic AI Security Best Practices Guide is a technical deliverable developed by the [../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) that consolidates actionable security controls for engineering teams deploying agentic AI systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide addresses five core domains: secrets management, secure tool invocation and protocol security, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. Broad identity architecture and delegation-chain token designs are deferred to [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

# Architecture / Specification

## 1. Secrets Management

Static and long-lived API keys represent a severe vulnerability surface in agent deployments because prompts or deserialization flaws (e.g. CVE-2025-68664) can extract persistent credentials from environment memory [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]. The guide mandates replacing stored assets with ephemeral attestations through a prioritized hierarchy [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:

- **Workload Identity:** Native cloud platform OIDC federations (AWS IRSA, GCP Workload Identity, Azure Managed Identity) providing automatically rotated short-lived tokens without storing secrets in agent runtime images [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Dynamic Secrets Engines:** HashiCorp Vault or equivalent dynamic providers generating per-request, short-TTL credentials [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Network-Layer Injection:** Sidecars and reverse proxies injecting authorization tokens out-of-band for legacy systems [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].
- **Confidential Computing:** Enclave environments (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV-SNP) providing hardware-isolated attestation for multi-tenant or regulated workloads [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf].

## 2. Secure Tool Invocation and MCP Hardening

For agent-to-tool communication via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the guide specifies defensive controls against tool description poisoning (including hidden Unicode tag manipulation), cross-server shadowing, and rug pulls [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]:

- **Pre-deployment Verification:** Mandatory source repository activity verification (>=90-day threshold), vulnerability tracker cross-referencing, and static and runtime tool schema scanning [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Transport Isolation:** Treating `stdio` transport servers as unvetted local binaries requiring strict sandbox boundaries; requiring OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, TLS enforcement, and RFC 8707 resource audience binding on all HTTP MCP connections [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Runtime Invariants:** Session-start tool description hash comparisons to detect unexpected schema modifications and out-of-scope parameter injections [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

## 3. Skill and Extension Verification

The guide outlines a tiered supply-chain verification process for modular agent skills [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]:

- **Tier 1 (Automated Pre-Scanning):** Static pattern matching and behavioral dataflow analysis to block Critical and High findings prior to invocation [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].
- **Tier 2 (Manual Authorization):** Manual security review for elevated permissions, verifying declared `allowed-tools` against functionality and inspecting for obfuscated code or unauthorized external network domains [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc].

# References

- Document: `deliverables/DRAFT-agentic-ai-security-best-practices-guide.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-b8b8567533b6-28cc0dbf]
- Feature Matrix: `workstreams/best-practices/security-best-practices-feature-matrix.md` [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-22190b4c1053-5db87bbc]

mutations.rationale: Captures the merged Agent to MCP Server boundary deep-dive defining telemetry propagation, session versus request lifecycles, and observability gaps.

proposed_concept.title: Agent to MCP Server Boundary Deep-Dive
proposed_concept.description: Observability reference matrix and telemetry propagation model analyzing the protocol boundary between MCP clients and MCP servers.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent to MCP Server boundary deep-dive defines the observability requirements, metadata field mappings, and telemetry propagation mechanisms across the Model Context Protocol (MCP) boundary[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711]. While conceptually labeled as an Agent → MCP Server relationship, the operational protocol boundary occurs between an MCP Client (often a host application, agent runtime, or gateway) and an MCP Server over JSON-RPC 2.0 transport[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].

# Architecture / Specification
The specification separates lifecycle concerns and trace propagation rules into distinct architectural layers:

- **Session Lifecycle vs. Request Lifecycle**: Session lifecycle governs connection initialization, capability negotiation (`clientInfo`, `serverInfo`, protocol version), and transport state over stdio or Streamable HTTP. Request lifecycle governs individual JSON-RPC invocations, parameters, results, streaming responses, and errors. The two must be instrumented independently so request-level errors do not corrupt session metadata[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].
- **Context Propagation**: Distributed trace context across client and server spans is correlated via W3C trace context passed within the `params._meta.traceparent` protocol field, aligning with OpenTelemetry GenAI MCP semantic conventions[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-462a9edc1364-8b0b8711].
- **Core Observability Matrix Dimensions**: Maps identity, context, relationship, lifecycle, outcome, provenance, security, and timing across declared and observed states[^evt-wg-observability-pr-32].
- **Load-Bearing Open Gaps**: Identifies divergences between declared tool capabilities and runtime observed behavior, missing server-side side-effect manifests, consent-chain observability, and consumer-evaluated evidence integrity[^evt-wg-observability-pr-32].

# Lifecycle History
Developed under the Observability and Traceability Working Group ([`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)) as part of the cross-boundary observability work package complementing the Agent to CLI tool model in [`../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md`](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md)[^evt-wg-observability-pr-32].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Behavior Trace Model
proposed_concept.description: Open specification and reference implementation defining portable telemetry context, turn boundaries, and behavioral event schemas for agent execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model is an open specification defining portable telemetry context, execution turn boundaries, and behavioral event schemas for AI agent systems[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]. It standardizes how agent runs, planning loops, tool executions, and delegations are represented across heterogeneous runtimes and observability backends.

# Architecture / Specification
The trace model delivery roadmap follows an evidence-first execution plan structured across four sequential phases[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60]:

1. **Agree**: Establish initial dimension coverage and boundary criteria.
2. **Evidence**: Capture and benchmark empirical telemetry emitted by live agent SDKs and engines to catalog inconsistencies in OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions adoption.
3. **Interpret**: Maintain a centralized gap register analyzing deviations between declared standards and real-world runtime telemetry.
4. **Contribute**: Formulate standardized upstream proposals to OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions based on empirical traces.

The initial reference implementation baseline is built against Goose ([`../resources/goose.md`](../resources/goose.md)), an open-source general-purpose agent with native OpenTelemetry instrumentation[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Lifecycle History
Maintained by the Observability and Traceability Working Group ([`../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md`](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md)). The execution strategy was restructured to prioritize captured telemetry evidence over parallel theoretical work packages[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-60].

# Overview
The Security and Privacy Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body establishing open threat models, architectural patterns, and operational security guidelines across multi-agent systems, tool integration layers, and delegated execution environments[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Architecture / Specification
The working group organizes its technical outputs across a five-part deliverable portfolio[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308]:

- **D1: Taxonomy of Terms**: Shared vocabulary and ontology for agentic-specific threat surfaces.
- **D2: Threat Modeling Gap Analysis**: Evaluation of established security frameworks (OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 / ASI01–ASI10, MITRE ATLAS v4.6.0+, CSA MAESTRO, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and CSA AI Controls Matrix) across eight agent threat domains: memory/context poisoning, multi-agent persuasion, agent sabotage/derailment, tool invocation risk, blast radius containment, delegated authorization boundaries, supply chain integrity, and commerce/payment risk[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].
- **D3: Design Patterns Catalog**: Architectural security patterns addressing verified framework voids (such as [`../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md`](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) and [`../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md`](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)).
- **D4: Best Practices Guide**: Practical implementation guidance covering secrets management, secure tool invocation, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and post-incident forensics (led by Fernando Lucktemberg and Matthew Khouzam)[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-e24f19bec4ac-d0ff1066].
- **D5: Cross-WG Security and Privacy Review Checklist**: Governance checklists and review gates for security crosswalks with sibling working groups[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-file-bc22580e2387-ad459308].

# Lifecycle History
Operates under the technical governance of the AAIF Technical Committee ([`../governance/technical-committee.md`](../governance/technical-committee.md)).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Governance, Risk, and Regulatory Working Group is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body bridging global AI policy developments, regulatory compliance mandates, and practical risk governance architectures for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11] The working group designs structured taxonomies, theme card specifications, and decoupled obligation schemas enabling deployers to evaluate AI systems against dynamic cross-jurisdictional legal requirements without embedding proprietary compliance databases directly in open-source repositories.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]

# Architecture / Specification
The working group's technical architecture decouples normative compliance row formats from deployment-specific legal data feeds, mirroring open-source ecosystem architectures like OpenSSF OSV and Open Policy Agent.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]

### Theme Card and Obligation Schema
Regulatory obligations are modeled through standardized "Theme Cards" structured with standard applicability fields:[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]
- **Jurisdiction**: Geographic and political authority where the duty attaches (e.g., EU, Colorado, Korea, Vietnam).
- **Instrument and Article**: Specific legal codification, article, and statutory revision identifier.
- **Bound Role**: Specific role in the AI lifecycle bound by the obligation (e.g., provider, deployer, user, controller, processor).
- **Duty and Scope**: Structured statement of legal obligation and applicable technical threshold.
- **Status and Revision Date**: Temporal tracking of amendments, effective dates, and repeals (e.g., tracking Colorado SB 24-205 transition to SB 26-189, and EU AI Act amendments under Regulation 2026/1744).[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]

### Runtime Decoupling Model
To prevent repositories from maintaining static, quickly outdated legal interpretations or violating licensing terms, the working group standardizes open data schemas (such as CC-BY-4.0 formatted CSV/JSON specifications) designed to ingest run-time feeds from pluggable external regulatory registers and compliance providers.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]

# Lifecycle History
- **Phase 1 Landscape**: Initial mapping of global AI statutes, governance frameworks, and high-level risk categories.
- **Phase 2 Technical Formalization**: Transitioning to standardized obligation theme cards, run-time pluggable requirement schemas, and longitudinal regulatory change tracking across 13+ binding AI legal instruments.[^evt-wg-governance-risk-and-regulatory-issue-11]

# Overview
The Public Agent Skills repository provides a collection of modular, procedural agent skills, orchestrator workflows, and deterministic execution scripts designed for community operations, issue triage, repository synchronization, and asset generation across the Agentic AI Foundation.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710][^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30] The skills enforce strict operational constraints, including privacy guardrails, identity matching, format-preserving document manipulation, and calibrated visual asset placement.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49][^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]

# Architecture / Specification

### Operational Community Skills
- **`aaif-announcement-post`**: Generates LinkedIn launch and announcement posts when event RSVPs open, integrating with Luma and Gradual.AI.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710] Enforces the *Public-Copy Rule*, forbidding agent outputs and conversational reasoning transcripts from echoing sensitive intake details (speaker emails, door codes, attendee contact information), and attaches mandatory LF Code of Conduct and Privacy Policy footers.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]
- **`aaif-event-status`**: Reads chapter and online series task health from `Event Tracker.docx` files using authenticated Google Workspace (`gws`) CLI integration.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30] Prohibits headless office suites (e.g., LibreOffice/`soffice`) to prevent font substitution and OOXML metadata corruption, preferring native Docs APIs and byte-level zip patching.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]
- **`aaif-audit-slack`**: Validates chapter Slack workspaces, checking channel existence, organizer rosters, and membership alignments.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb] Flags high-severity security anomalies such as publicly readable `-organizers` channels and supports `--planned-ok` flags during pre-provisioning lifecycle states.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
- **`aaif-create-chapter`**: Automates chapter asset generation using paragraph-level text transformation and a mathematical Gall Stereographic map projection (`lon2x` linear in longitude, `lat2y` linear in `(1 + √2/2)·tan(lat/2)`) fitted to Natural Earth coastlines for precise map marker placement.[^evt-community-events-file-0dc3d95afe1f-91fcca49]

### Operational and Privacy Guardrails
1. **Public-Copy Redaction**: Prohibits emitting private intake data in draft copy or agent transcripts; private fields must only be referenced by name.[^evt-community-events-file-133151709c55-f5700710]
2. **Deterministic Precedence**: Source of truth is reconciled against central registers (e.g., Chapters List, Intake Ops) with strict precedence rules over heuristic matches.[^evt-community-events-file-2ca2907cf349-5ea9efbb]
3. **Format Integrity**: Restricts editing of cloud documents to native Google Workspace APIs and deterministic Python tooling to avoid formatting degradation.[^evt-community-events-file-2a0ccd906b70-3a886c30]

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability and Execution Boundaries
proposed_concept.description: Standards for packaging portable agent plugins, resolving skill root paths, abstracting tool capabilities, and enforcing mutation authorization gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Foundation community events repository establishes an operational standard for portable Agent Plugins and skills across multiple execution environments including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. By separating portable manifest declarations from client-specific hooks and defining capabilities over proprietary tool names, agent skills achieve deterministic cross-client compatibility without duplication [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69].

# Architecture / Specification
## Manifest and Path Portability
Plugins maintain a canonical root `plugin.json` adhering to the Agent Plugins specification [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Client-specific metadata overlays (such as `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) provide backward compatibility without fragmenting identity. Within each `SKILL.md`, all file and script references are resolved relative to the skill directory using `<skill-root>` placeholders rather than hardcoded shell environment variables [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca][^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].

## Capability Abstraction Matrix
Skills declare operational requirements as abstract capabilities rather than client-specific tool bindings [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]:
- **Read bundled files**: Load workflows, references, or templates locally.
- **Run Python and subprocesses**: Execute deterministic Python automation and authorized CLIs (e.g., `gws`).
- **Read web pages**: Fetch public event links and external calendars.
- **Show local files**: Present generated artifacts (HTML, PNG, PPTX) for local inspection.
- **Request user approval**: Halt execution before crossing documented write or notification gates.

## Authorization and Boundary Controls
Loading or invoking a skill confers read-only access by default [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69]. Mutating external systems requires explicit runtime gates aligning with [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md) and [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md):
- **Deterministic Separation**: Agents invoke CLIs for transport while offloading document edits to deterministic local scripts [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].
- **Explicit Mutation Flags**: Modifying actions require flags like `--write`, `--apply`, or `--create`, permitted only after user review of proposed changes [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad].
- **Public-Copy and Privacy Safeguards**: Content generation skills strictly forbid echoing private PII (such as unpublished emails or access codes) in output drafts or agent reasoning responses [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-8c8b765e][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5].
- **Secret Elimination**: Credentials reside strictly in environment variables or system keychains, never passed in command-line arguments or prompt transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-57c4a0921db3-7bd7bd69][^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].

# References
- [../resources/public-agent-skills.md](../resources/public-agent-skills.md)
- [../patterns/human-approval-gate.md](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)

# Overview
Community Event Operations Skills comprise a suite of procedural agent skills and deterministic Python tooling designed to manage the end-to-end lifecycle of AAIF chapters and online event series [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca][^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93]. These skills standardize event tracking, presentation deck generation, social carousel copywriting, and design system compliance across Google Drive and local execution environments [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-8c8b765e][^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5][^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad].

# Architecture / Specification
## Skill Capabilities and Workflows
The event operations skill suite automates specific operational workflows:
- **Online Series and Chapter Provisioning (`aaif-create-online-series`)**: Clones standardized series structures in Google Drive, rebranding templates and configuring event runbooks for virtual platforms without physical venue requirements [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca].
- **Event Scheduling and Luma Sync (`aaif-create-event`)**: Clones example sections in `Event Tracker.docx`, computes phase due dates backward from event dates, and generates live Luma event pages upon explicit human approval [^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93].
- **Presentation Deck Assembly (`aaif-dayof-slides`)**: Extracts structured event metadata from trackers to populate "Day of Event" PowerPoint slide text while preserving immutable brand slides and host lockups [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-8c8b765e].
- **Social Marketing Copywriting (`aaif-carousel-copy`)**: Generates concise, technical LinkedIn carousels emphasizing practitioner practices and community signals according to AAIF voice guidelines [^evt-community-events-file-52894c310bd9-392b08f5].
- **Design System Enforcement (`restyle_design_system.py`)**: Executes deterministic sweeps over templates, auditing DrawingML and SpreadsheetML styles, verifying WCAG AA text legibility contrast, and enforcing non-destructive backups before applying changes [^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad].

## Deterministic Tooling and Tool Execution Boundary
The suite mandates a strict execution boundary separating transport from content mutation [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca][^evt-community-events-file-4c2672b57ca1-cb10dc93]:
- Agents interact with remote Google Drive storage exclusively via the `gws` CLI driven by Python [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca].
- Document modifications utilize native Google APIs or byte-level OOXML manipulation (OpenXML zip part editing) to preserve embedded fonts and complex features [^evt-community-events-file-2e96153bc720-02e706ca].
- Headless office suites (such as LibreOffice or `soffice`) are strictly prohibited to prevent font substitution and schema loss [^evt-community-events-file-4676d39ff431-8c8b765e][^evt-community-events-file-49f05aeb9187-979566ad].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill catalog provides modular, deterministic automation and conversational procedures for managing Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) chapters, event tracking, speaker lifecycle, presentation assets, and community audit reporting [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210]. Built in accordance with portable agent skill standards [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210] (see [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)), these skills enforce strict privacy boundaries, deterministic data-fetching contracts, and zero-drift estate backfill capabilities.

# Architecture / Specification

### 1. Speaker Lifecycle & Public Copywriting Rules
The skill bundle provides specialized copywriting workflows designed around a builder-to-builder house voice ("share the practice, never sell the product; signal over numbers") [^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b]:
- **Speaker Outreach (`aaif-speaker-invite`)**: Formulates concrete, low-friction speaker invitations (~90 words) specifying topic, length, date, venue, and audience profile [^evt-community-events-file-8035c6f18e40-cc3d7afd].
- **Speaker Bios (`aaif-speaker-bio`)**: Drafts dual-format biographies consisting of a 60–80 word third-person narrative and a concise single-line summary (maximum 18 words) [^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b].
- **Post-Event Recap (`aaif-recap-post`)**: Produces LinkedIn wrap-up posts (~110 words) within 48 hours of an event, thanking speakers/venues by name, sharing takeaways, and attaching standard [Code of Conduct](../policies/code-of-conduct.md) and privacy footers [^evt-community-events-file-6ceee5c2c51f-0a4ad5f7].

**Public-Copy Privacy Rule:** When synthesizing drafts from intake trackers via `fetch_tracker.py`, non-public PII (e.g., speaker email addresses, door codes, private venue contacts, unannounced attendee names) is systematically withheld from agent responses and generated copy [^evt-community-events-file-64b0f6914598-99abd07b] [^evt-community-events-file-6ceee5c2c51f-0a4ad5f7]. Agents are prohibited from echoing raw sensitive values in execution transcripts even when explaining omissions [^evt-community-events-file-8035c6f18e40-cc3d7afd].

### 2. Estate Backfills & OOXML Presentation Surgery
For bulk template synchronization across existing chapter decks, specialized scripts perform in-place OOXML modifications [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62]:
- **Map Marker Placement (`backfill_map_dots.py`)**: Re-positions chapter location markers and labels using Gall Stereographic projection formulas derived from authoritative geolocation sheets, with plan-first dry runs and tolerance gates [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].
- **Host Footer & Project Roster Backfills**: Synchronizes global sponsor footers and foundation project rosters across Google Drive slide templates without manual editing churn [^evt-community-events-file-799e4722911d-3d7dbf62].

### 3. Community Workspace Auditing & Cache Safety
The Slack audit pipeline (`aaif-audit-slack`) reconciles workspace rosters, chapter channel linkages, and organizer access permissions [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214]:
- **Cache Safety & Git Protection**: Raw API pulls are cached in local directories with `0600`/`0700` POSIX permissions; execution engines abort immediately if output paths risk accidental repository exposure via `git add -A` [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214].
- **Combined Audit Reports (`summarize_audits.py`)**: Consolidates separate audit fragments (Chapters, Organizers, Topics, Members) into a unified HTML dashboard without speculative extrapolation [^evt-community-events-file-8b30d97e0275-93d6c214].

### 4. Portability & Hygiene Enforcement
All skills and helper scripts are validated via pre-commit hooks that check portable `SKILL.md` frontmatter, prevent tooling banner drift between skill copies, verify secret elimination from command-line arguments, and enforce single-module redaction surfaces [^evt-community-events-file-63a9c44a44ac-37822210].

# Overview

The Community Event Operations skill toolkit provides standardized, procedural agent skills for administering Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) in-person meetups, chapter provisioning, estate synchronization, and community communications [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-eb4f6eb2]. Designed to comply with agent plugin portability standards [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-eb4f6eb2], the toolkit partitions capabilities into setup-free content generation skills and privileged operational automation workflows [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-eb4f6eb2].

All file mutations across Google Drive and local storage follow strict deterministic tooling rules: agents interact exclusively via Python and the `gws` CLI [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e]. Modifying native Google formats is performed directly through Docs/Sheets/Slides APIs, while local Office formats (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`) require direct OOXML zip-part manipulation to preserve embedded brand typography and schema integrity without relying on headless office suites like LibreOffice [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7].

# Architecture / Specification

### Content Skills

Content generation skills operate in an unprivileged, read-only mode to generate structured event communications while preventing accidental leaks of private organizer or attendee data [^evt-community-events-file-a4874490bd2a-eeb8e84e]:

- **`aaif-luma-description`**: Formats structured Luma event listings (approx. 180 words) covering key topics, target audience, schedule, and standard vendor-neutral positioning statements [^evt-community-events-file-a4874490bd2a-eeb8e84e]. Enforces a strict public-copy rule where private contact information (e.g., speaker email addresses, venue door codes) retrieved from local event trackers is withheld and never reflected in agent transcripts [^evt-community-events-file-a4874490bd2a-eeb8e84e].

### Operational & Estate Skills

Operational workflows require authenticated access to cloud storage and messaging backends to execute lifecycle changes [^evt-community-events-file-b33563055168-eb4f6eb2]:

- **`aaif-create-chapter`**: Provisions a new city chapter by cloning the canonical `TemplateCity` Google Drive hierarchy [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7]. Rebrands Office files and spreadsheet metadata while programmatically updating map coordinates for the chapter network visual on presentation title decks [^evt-community-events-file-d236c244f6dc-d6812bc7].
- **`aaif-audit-slack`**: Runs read-only inspections of community Slack workspaces to evaluate chapter channel coverage, organizer memberships, inactive discussion channels, and overall workspace health without performing destructive writes [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
- **`aaif-backup`**: Generates timestamped, immutable local snapshots of mission-critical operational sheets and Drive assets prior to bulk migrations or schema refactoring [^evt-community-events-file-91fd6707275c-30b3ce2e].

### Security & Validation Boundaries

To ensure untrusted input handling across all skill entrypoints [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65]:
1. External CRM cell text, Slack topics, and message bodies are strictly treated as data rather than prompt instructions [^evt-community-events-file-91886a9e0653-1a4c1c65].
2. CI workflows isolate automated pull-request validation into unprivileged read-only runners, preventing secret exfiltration from forks while restricting live skill executions to gated dispatch environments [^evt-community-events-file-a5c0f08bc43f-b99183b6].

# References

- [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)
- [Public Agent Skills](../resources/public-agent-skills.md)
- [Community Events Evaluation Suite](../resources/community-events-eval-suite.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agent Plugin Portability
proposed_concept.description: Standards for packaging portable agent plugins, resolving skill root paths, and structuring progressive disclosure between SKILL.md and WORKFLOW.md.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Agent Plugin Portability defines architectural standards for authoring, packaging, and distributing vendor-neutral AI agent skills across client runtimes such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. The standard mandates portable directory placeholders, explicit execution compatibility manifests, and token-bounded procedural documents to maximize runtime reliability and cross-client compatibility [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-fd49cca9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Plugin and Skill Directory Layout
A portable agent plugin encapsulates skills, manifests, and validation tools within a standardized repository structure [^evt-community-events-pr-54][^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-fd49cca9]:
- `plugin.json`: Shared root manifest declaring the plugin identifier, version, and exposed skills.
- `.claude-plugin/`: Client-specific manifests (`plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`) retained for backwards compatibility.
- `skills/<skill-name>/`: Individual capability directories containing:
  - `SKILL.md`: Core procedural spine bounded strictly under 500 lines (~5,000 tokens).
  - `WORKFLOW.md`: Extended procedural sequences linked progressively for complex workflows.
  - `scripts/`: Executable helper tools, each paired with unit tests (`test_*.py`).
  - `references/`: Detailed reference documentation loaded on demand with explicit trigger conditions.

## Path Resolution and Metadata Standards
- **Placeholder Resolution**: File references within skills must avoid client-specific environment variables (such as `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`) and use client-agnostic `<skill-root>` placeholders resolved dynamically from `SKILL.md` [^evt-community-events-pr-54][^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570].
- **Frontmatter Declarations**: Every `SKILL.md` must declare a descriptive `name`, activation criteria in `description` ("Use when asked to..."), and an explicit `compatibility` string listing runtime prerequisites [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-fd49cca9]. Client-specific extensions must be scoped under the `metadata` namespace [^evt-community-events-pr-54].

## References
- Operational reference skills are documented in [Community Event Operations](../skills/community-event-operations.md).

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Community Event Operations toolkit provides modular procedural agent skills for managing Foundation chapters, attendee communications, and recurring community reporting [^evt-community-events-pr-54]. Implemented as portable agent skills, these tools enforce strict data privacy boundaries, deterministic OOXML file operations, and progressive disclosure between procedural entrypoints and deep reference manuals [^evt-community-events-file-eca12c0a30e2-fd49cca9].

# Architecture / Specification

## Modular Skill Capabilities
The event operations toolkit encompasses distinct functional modules:
- **Community Pulse (`aaif-community-pulse`)**: Collects recent activity across Slack organizer channels, member forums, and Luma calendars to draft three separate audience-specific summaries (organizers, members, public social copy) without directly publishing to external APIs [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
- **Attendee Communications (`aaif-attendee-reminder`)**: Generates standardized, logistics-focused event reminders referencing cached event tracker entries while withholding sensitive contact information [^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-6a45ddf8].
- **Chapter Lifecycle Transformations (`aaif-create-chapter` / `rename_chapter.py`)**: Executes deterministic four-surface chapter migrations (folder naming, file paths, OOXML internal strings, and document metadata) with isolated slug decoupling and rollback safety [^evt-community-events-file-ec8a86dec4ad-08c3cbb3].

## Operational and Security Boundaries
Skills operate under mandatory execution rules:
- **Public-Copy Boundary**: Agent skills must never output non-public attendee emails, phone numbers, or venue door codes into transcripts or drafts [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570][^evt-community-events-file-ede28c6c866a-6a45ddf8].
- **Untrusted Input Isolation**: Channel messages, tracker spreadsheets, and calendar entries are treated strictly as untrusted data rather than operational instructions [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570][^evt-community-events-file-f1c760a76169-ceb51f5d].
- **Deterministic File Surgery**: Google Workspace Drive APIs handle cloud documents while byte-level ZIP part surgery is reserved for true OOXML packages (`.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`), strictly avoiding lossy local office converters [^evt-community-events-file-ed850506c872-63272570].

## References
- Agent plugin packaging standards are specified in [Agent Plugin Portability](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md).
