proposed_concept.title: Agentic Use Case Classification Schema and Inventory
proposed_concept.description: Taxonomy schema and empirical inventory categorizing production agentic workflows across triggers, HITL patterns, coordination, and execution topology.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agentic Use Case Classification Schema and Inventory provides a standardized, twelve-column analytical framework developed by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) Critical Use Cases Workstream to describe, classify, and compare real-world agentic workflows across industries[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. Rather than cataloging theoretical systems, the repository benchmarks verified production deployments spanning horizontal functions (sales, marketing, customer support, finance, HR, research) and vertical domains (engineering, IT/network ops, SDLC, platform engineering, healthcare, legal, supply chain, real estate, education)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae].

# Architecture / Specification

### Classification Dimensions

The framework isolates five structural classification dimensions that capture distinct design decisions rather than observational metrics[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]:

1. **Trigger**: The initial activation mechanism, classified into external system events, scheduled cron jobs, or explicit human interaction.
2. **HITL Pattern**: The placement and necessity of human intervention in the execution path, such as [human approval gates](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md), draft review, or exception escalation.
3. **Agent Count**: The structural division of reasoning agents, capturing architectural justifications for multi-agent splits such as distinct foundation models, isolated tool scopes, or decomposed cognitive complexity.
4. **Coordination**: The governing mechanism determining downstream actions—distinguishing deterministic code-based routing from dynamic runtime LLM reasoning.
5. **Workflow Pattern**: The execution topology, including linear pipelines, concurrent branching and merging, or [bounded convergence loops](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md) iterating against [deterministic acceptance gates](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md).

### Supporting Attributes and Duration

Seven supporting fields accompany each classified implementation[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]:
- **Duration**: Observed execution time strictly measuring active agent runtime, excluding asynchronous queue delays or downstream human processing waits.
- **Descriptive Metadata**: Identification via Use Case name, textual Description, and Tools & Systems utilized.
- **Failure and Context Records**: Documentation of Key Failure Modes, environmental Preconditions, and Notes containing architectural rationales.

### Evidentiary Standards

Entries in the inventory must satisfy strict sourcing standards to eliminate speculative or unverified claims[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41]:
- **Preferred Evidence**: Primary vendor announcements or product documentation verifying a named, production enterprise deployment.
- **Acceptable Evidence**: Vendor documentation confirming active production features operating at scale without a named reference.
- **Disallowed Sources**: Secondary analyst summaries, marketing projections, opinion blog posts, and unverified academic preprints.

proposed_concept.description: AAIF technical working group defining reference architectures, execution profiles, workflow orchestration schemas, and production use-case taxonomies.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Workflows and Process Integration Working Group (WG-WPI) is an Agentic AI Foundation technical body tasked with establishing vendor-neutral reference architectures, workflow orchestration patterns, execution profiles, and industry use-case classifications for autonomous and human-in-the-loop agent systems[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc]. The group coordinates cross-industry standards for connecting autonomous agent execution with enterprise business processes and human decision boundaries.

# Active Workstreams

### Critical Use Cases Workstream

The Critical Use Cases Workstream curates the [Agentic Use Case Classification Schema and Inventory](../resources/agentic-use-case-classification.md)[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-6cdd0fb97084-5ba45ebc][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-c10bbaa87c3e-880211ae]. This workstream evaluates production agent implementations across five primary structural dimensions (Trigger, HITL Pattern, Agent Count, Coordination, and Workflow Pattern) and enforces strict primary-source evidentiary criteria for production verifiability[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-41].

### Reference Architecture Workstream

Develops lower-level execution models, tool invocation protocols, context/state handoff mechanisms, and guardrail enforcement architectures, complementing operational patterns such as [approval checkpoints](../patterns/approval-checkpoint.md) and [workflow architecture principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md).

mutations.rationale: Spector is proposed to the Agentic AI Foundation as an open-source cognitive memory engine providing multi-tier episodic, working, semantic, and procedural state substrates over MCP and native bindings.

proposed_concept.title: Spector Memory Engine
proposed_concept.description: Open-source cognitive memory engine and MCP server providing multi-tier state retention, decay scoring, and namespace isolation for AI agents.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Spector is an open-source cognitive memory engine designed to provide autonomous AI agents and multi-agent systems with durable, stateful memory substrates beyond stateless vector databases.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48] It addresses context degradation and long-running session context loss by organizing memory traces across working, episodic, semantic, and procedural tiers with associative graph scoring and power-law decay.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]

# Architecture / Specification
Spector is implemented as a modular Java reactor utilizing Project Panama Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) and the Vector API to achieve SIMD-accelerated scoring off-heap with low garbage collection overhead.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48] It implements the open Memory Fundamentals (MF-001) memory model specification.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]

Key architectural components include:
- **Tiered Memory Model**: Segregates experiential data into working, episodic, semantic, and procedural stores with power-law decay and consolidation routines.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]
- **Namespace Isolation**: Enforces physical on-disk tenant and agent namespace isolation boundaries to prevent cross-tenant data leakage.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]
- **Interface Layer**: Exposes an embedded Model Context Protocol (`spector-mcp`) server providing cognitive memory tools (`memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_reinforce`, `memory_introspect`, `memory_why_not`, `memory_status`), alongside REST/gRPC gateways and language SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Java).[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]
- **Runtime Integration**: Interoperates with local execution harnesses such as [goose](../resources/goose.md) via stdio or HTTP MCP configurations.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]

# Lifecycle History
Spector was submitted to the AAIF Project Proposals intake for Sandbox stage incubation under Apache-2.0 licensing, targeting vendor-neutral standardization of agent memory infrastructure.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-48]

mutations.rationale: Prismor is proposed to the Agentic AI Foundation as an Apache-2.0 self-hosted control plane providing tool call interception and policy-as-code enforcement across agent frameworks and MCP gateways.

proposed_concept.title: Prismor
proposed_concept.description: Self-hosted runtime control plane and proxy intercepting agent tool calls to enforce policy-as-code and audit logging.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Prismor is an open-source, self-hosted control plane for AI agents that performs tool call interception and evaluates actions against versioned policy-as-code before execution.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51] It acts as a runtime governance layer that issues allow, block, transform, or human approval verdicts independently of model-context instructions.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]

# Architecture / Specification
Prismor provides runtime enforcement across multiple deployment touchpoints using a unified policy engine:[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]

- **MCP Gateway Proxy**: Intercepts downstream `tools/call` invocations across [mcp-gateway-registry](../resources/mcp-gateway-registry.md) routes, evaluating arguments before forwarding and scanning returned payloads before context re-entry.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]
- **In-Process SDK Adapters & Coding Hooks**: Integrates directly into agent runtimes and coding harnesses to intercept tool executions at the client boundary.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]
- **Evaluation Modes**: Supports *observe mode* for auditing and impact measurement without disruption, and *enforce mode* for deterministic intervention and blocking.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]
- **Policy-as-Code Engine**: Ingests declarative YAML policies scoped across organization, project, repository, or session levels, generating signed audit trails and attestation bundles.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]

# Lifecycle History
Originally created as `immunity-agent`, the project was rebranded to `prismor` in 2026 and submitted to the AAIF as a proposed Sandbox project to provide runtime policy enforcement complementing agent protocols and frameworks.[^evt-project-proposals-issue-51]

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic Use Case Classification and Inventory is an empirical catalog and schema curated by the [Workflows & Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to classify real-world production agentic deployments and identify recurring workflow shapes.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

# Architecture / Specification
The Critical Use Cases workstream establishes a systematic classification framework and inventory dataset to map deployment choices across industries:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

- **Schema Definitions (`schema-agentic-use-cases.md`)**: Standardizes column taxonomy, classification dimensions, autonomy tiers, and execution constraints.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]
- **Production Inventory (`use-case-inventory.md`)**: Catalogs named, deployed agentic workflows mapped across classification dimensions to discover structural workflow shapes and pattern frequencies.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

## Evidentiary Standard
To ensure the catalog reflects genuine production implementations rather than theoretical proposals, the workstream enforces strict citation criteria for inventory rows:[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

1. **Preferred Sources**: Vendor product pages or primary announcements documenting a confirmed, named customer deployment (e.g., enterprise production rollouts).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]
2. **Acceptable Sources**: Vendor product pages detailing verified feature availability operating in production at scale without a named customer.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]
3. **Unacceptable Sources**: Secondary blogs, analyst market projections, academic concept papers, unverified personal knowledge, or unreferenced individual write-ups.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303]

Every use case requires at least one verified citation, targeting three independent citations for mature entries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-5028db4c24a1-b054a303][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-46]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Technical guidance consolidating practical security controls across secrets elimination, MCP protocol hardening, and people, process, and technology capability matrices.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guideline consolidates technical controls, architectural guardrails, and operational standards developed by the [Security & Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md) to secure autonomous agent runtimes, tool invocation boundaries, and model-context interfaces.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

# Architecture / Specification
Security controls in agentic deployments are organized across three supporting implementation domains via a feature matrix:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

- **People**: Capabilities focusing on personnel skills, security awareness training, and role-based operational understanding for supervising autonomous agent actions.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]
- **Process**: Formal documented policies, operational playbooks, risk review workflows, and governance strategies defining how agent security controls are executed and validated.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]
- **Technology**: Physical and digital tools, software harnesses, hardware enforcement mechanisms, and automated systems executing controls such as [kill-switch](../patterns/kill-switch.md) capabilities, tool call proxies, and [attested-isolated-runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-pr-20]

Core technical baselines also govern static credential elimination, out-of-band human confirmation at sensitive state transitions, and context boundary sanitization.

proposed_concept.title: Community Event Operations
proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skills executing deterministic OOXML presentation templating, chapter lifecycle synchronization, and non-destructive roster drift audits.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations comprises automated procedural skills used across the Agentic AI Foundation to maintain chapter rosters, generate presentation assets, and audit operational consistency across community tracking records.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

# Architecture / Specification
Operational execution is structured across deterministic validation and state synchronization modules:[^evt-community-events-pr-55]

- **Non-Destructive Chapter Synchronization**: Roster synchronization routines never directly purge or clear chapter records from central sheets. Rows lacking qualifying active organizers are surfaced as retirement candidates for explicit human review.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Deprecation and Merge Lifecycle**: Inactive or consolidated chapters transition through explicit state updates (`Status=Deprecated` or `Status=Merged` with an associated target identifier) to preserve historical notes, summaries, and operational metadata.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Drift Reporting**: Ambiguous organizer associations or malformed city names trigger holding states on the run drift log rather than automated write mutations or exit-code failures.[^evt-community-events-pr-55]
- **Asset Templating**: Programmatic generation of standardized event collateral and presentation decks from authoritative meeting data.

proposed_concept.title: TRACE Specification
proposed_concept.description: Open standard and JSON Schema for signed agent execution records supporting verifiable software, hardware-attested, and transparency-anchored evidence.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The TRACE Specification (Trust, Runtime Attestation, and Compliance Evidence) is an open specification for generating signed records of AI agent runs that third parties can verify without trusting the producing operator [^evt-project-proposals-issue-42]. A TRACE Trust Record captures which model executed (`model.model_id`, `model.weights_digest`), the target execution environment (`runtime.platform`, `runtime.measurement`), policy bundles in force (`policy.bundle_hash`), data classifications, and tool transcript hashes [^evt-project-proposals-issue-42].

# Architecture / Specification

TRACE builds on existing IETF and open standards rather than defining novel cryptography [^evt-project-proposals-issue-42]:
- **RFC 9711 (EAT)**: Defines the structured claims envelope.
- **RFC 9334 (RATS)**: Defines architecture and roles for attesters, verifiers, and relying parties.
- **RFC 8785**: Canonical JSON format used prior to cryptographic signing.
- **SCITT**: Supply chain integrity transparency log anchoring.

### Conformance Levels

Records declare one of three conformance tiers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-42]:
- **Level 0 (Software-Signed)**: Cryptographically signed audit trail without hardware appraisal.
- **Level 1 (Hardware-Attested)**: Bound to hardware evidence (e.g., Intel TDX, AMD SEV-SNP, NVIDIA H100/Blackwell, AWS Nitro, Arm CCA, TPM 2.0) requiring hardware appraisal and verifier binding (see [../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)).
- **Level 2 (Transparency-Anchored)**: Incorporates transparency log inclusion proofs based on `registry-anchor-v1` specifications.

# Lifecycle History

TRACE was initially previewed at the Confidential Computing Summit on 23 June 2026 and announced under LF Projects on 25 August 2026 before being submitted as an AAIF project proposal [^evt-project-proposals-issue-42].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Skills
proposed_concept.description: Open file-based packaging format and progressive disclosure standard for extending AI agents with procedural knowledge, scripts, and domain workflows.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Agent Skills is an open specification and folder structure format for packaging specialized procedural knowledge, scripts, and workflows for AI agents [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]. Rooted in a self-contained directory with a `SKILL.md` file containing metadata and operational instructions, skills allow portable contextual capabilities to be authored once and executed across conforming agent runtimes [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

# Architecture / Specification

Agent Skills standardizes execution through progressive disclosure to minimize context consumption [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47]:
1. **Discovery**: At runtime startup, an agent inspects only top-level metadata (`name` and `description`) across configured skill repositories.
2. **Activation**: When an incoming prompt matches a skill description, the agent loads the complete `SKILL.md` instructions into active context.
3. **Execution**: The agent follows procedural instructions, invoking bundled scripts, referenced templates, or external Model Context Protocol tools as necessary [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

It complements repository-level instruction files such as AGENTS.md by isolating portable, on-demand domain tasks from project-specific workspace guidelines (see [../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md](../guidelines/agent-plugin-portability.md)) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

# Lifecycle History

Originally developed by Anthropic and published as an open standard in December 2025, the format was proposed for neutral ownership under the Agentic AI Foundation in September 2026 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-47].

proposed_concept.title: Agent Network Protocol
proposed_concept.description: Open communication protocol stack utilizing Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) for cross-platform agent identity, secure messaging, and semantic discovery.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Agent Network Protocol (ANP) is an open communication protocol stack designed to interconnect autonomous agents across heterogeneous platforms, administrative domains, and infrastructure [^evt-project-proposals-issue-46]. ANP defines mechanisms for decentralized agent identity, end-to-end encrypted messaging, and semantic discovery over standard Internet protocols (DNS, HTTPS) without requiring proprietary silos or blockchain dependencies [^evt-project-proposals-issue-46].

# Architecture / Specification

ANP comprises three primary functional layers [^evt-project-proposals-issue-46]:
- **Agent Identity**: Employs W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs), introducing the `did:wba` (Web-Based Agent) method and supporting `did:web` to bind cryptographic key material to web-accessible agent identities (see [../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md)).
- **Agent Messaging**: A DID-anchored messaging protocol facilitating direct peer-to-peer dialogues, multi-agent group communication, attachment sharing, and end-to-end encrypted interactions with verifiable origin proofs.
- **Agent Discovery and Description**: Semantic Linked Data representations referencing agent capabilities and interfaces (such as OpenAPI schemas), allowing external agents to dynamically discover available service endpoints [^evt-project-proposals-issue-46].

# Lifecycle History

Initiated in 2024 and launched as an open-source community effort in April 2025, ANP was submitted as a project proposal to the Agentic AI Foundation [^evt-project-proposals-issue-46].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Process with Human Approval
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate between an agent proposal and a protected effect.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The single-agent process with human approval is a reference architecture for human-approved operations where an agent investigates, calculates, and constructs an action proposal, an authorized human explicitly reviews and decides on the proposal, and a dedicated workflow-controlled executor applies the protected effect [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

The architecture addresses scenarios where an agent's output alters real systems (such as financial refunds, configuration updates, or outbound communications) where effects are irreversible, costly, or subject to strict audit obligations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]. By establishing a structural break between proposal generation and execution, it distinguishes end-to-end business tasks from constituent workflow activities [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-50].

# Architecture / Specification
The reference architecture is composed of core workflow patterns [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb]:
- [Proposal/Execution Split](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md): Separates proposal generation capabilities from the capability to trigger the protected effect.
- [Human Approval Gate](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md): Mandates that a named person approves or rejects an immutable proposal payload.
- [Durable Wait](../patterns/durable-wait.md): Ensures workflow execution state persists across extended approval latency without losing context or duplicating effects upon resume.

Key architectural guarantees include:
- No protected effect occurs without verified human approval, ensuring the exact approved payload executes without revision [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- Resiliency against process interruptions and restarts during extended approval waits [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].
- Complete provenance recording across proposer, approver, and executor identities in the audit log [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-file-a4fea1b2d544-d6bb99fb].

# References
- [Proposal/Execution Split Pattern](../patterns/proposal-execution-split.md)
- [Human Approval Gate Pattern](../patterns/human-approval-gate.md)
- [Durable Wait Pattern](../patterns/durable-wait.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

mutations.rationale: Update bounded autonomous remediation architecture with minimum evidence requirements for deterministic acceptance gates.

proposed_concept.title: Bounded Autonomous Remediation
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for autonomously resolving bounded tasks using deterministic acceptance gates.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Bounded autonomous remediation is a reference architecture for closed-loop, agent-driven resolution of scoped system failures, errors, or anomalies within strictly bounded domains using deterministic acceptance gates rather than manual human sign-off for routine steps.

# Architecture / Specification
The architecture governs autonomous remediation by iterating through bounded convergence loops and enforcing explicit validation criteria before applying state modifications:

- **Deterministic Acceptance Invariants**: Requires automated, reproducible validation criteria to verify remediation correctness prior to state commit.
- **Minimum Evidence Scaling**: Minimum evidence requirements for deterministic gates scale directly with permitted effects based on two primary dimensions: blast radius and reversal cost [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
- **Core Acceptance Record Guarantees**: Every acceptance record preserves three invariant properties regardless of gate strength:
  1. *Determinism of verdict*: The evaluation logic and test assertions yield identical outcomes for identical inputs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
  2. *Binding to candidate*: The verdict is immutably bound to the specific candidate patch or payload [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].
  3. *Execution evidence preservation*: The verdict and underlying evaluation telemetry are retained in persistent execution logs [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-43].

# References
- [Deterministic Acceptance Gate Pattern](../patterns/deterministic-acceptance-gate.md)
- [Bounded Convergence Loop Pattern](../patterns/bounded-convergence-loop.md)
- [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md)

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The AAIF Blog Guidelines establish editorial standards, content scopes, and submission processes for publications on the Agentic AI Foundation official blog.

# Architecture / Specification
Guidelines define review standards and stylistic rules for contributors:
- **Tone and Voice**: Educational, neutral, and technical content focusing on open standards and agentic AI advancements.
- **Editorial Conventions**: Content must adhere to sentence case for headings and titles, standard US English spelling, and official project naming conventions [^evt-foundation-pr-7].
- **Factual Substantiation and Sourcing**: Requires primary-source linking for technical assertions and restricts unsupported categorical claims [^evt-foundation-pr-7].
- **Eligibility**: Open to working group participants, maintainers, and community members writing on Foundation projects, architectures, and research.

# References

- [Brand Guidelines](./brand-guidelines.md)

proposed_concept.description: Modular agent skills executing deterministic presentation templating, intake data normalization, and chapter operations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
Community Event Operations provides standardized agent skills and operational workflows for managing Agentic AI Foundation community chapters, presentation assets, and intake data pipelines [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].

# Architecture / Specification
The skill suite enforces strict boundaries and tooling constraints for chapter and attendee data management:

## Data Normalization and Intake Ops
The `aaif-clean-data` operational skill normalizes intake forms and tracking sheets:
- **Canonicalization and Extraction**: Normalizes LinkedIn profile URLs, rectifies casing/whitespace in attendee names and cities, extracts structured city records from free-text inputs, and flags email anomalies or duplicate entries [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].
- **Read-Only Scans by Default**: Operates in scan mode to generate non-destructive diffs and proposals; data mutations require explicit human approval prior to applying writes [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].
- **Untrusted Input Boundaries**: Form responses and sheet cells are treated as untrusted data; instruction-like prompt injections within sheet cells cannot alter status flags, grants, or chapter authorizations [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].

## Tooling and Document Manipulation Rules
- **Google Workspace API Integration**: Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides files are manipulated exclusively through Python driving the `gws` CLI [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].
- **Office Document Surgery**: Raw OOXML zip part manipulation is restricted to stored `.docx`, `.pptx`, and `.xlsx` files without round-tripping through third-party desktop suites like LibreOffice to prevent font substitutions or XML corruption [^evt-community-events-file-1caae192c2a4-183bf153].

# References
- [Agent Skills Standard](../standards/agent-skills.md)

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Technical guidance consolidating practical security controls across secrets elimination, in-loop policy hooks, MCP protocol boundaries, and approval fatigue mitigations.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes actionable defensive patterns and architectural controls for securing autonomous agents, tool interfaces, and runtime environments across enterprise deployments. Developed by the Security and Privacy Working Group, the guide addresses threats spanning secret exposure, unauthorized tool execution, memory-based privilege retention, and human approval fatigue.

# Architecture / Specification

## Secret Auditing and Context Hygiene
Securing agent deployments requires auditing both static configuration files and dynamic context streams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33]:
- **Configuration and Skill Audits**: Secret scanners must inspect MCP client configuration files (such as `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, and `claude_desktop_config.json`) and packaged skill bundles for hardcoded API keys or environment blocks [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Context Redaction**: Tool outputs containing tokens, environment variables, or sensitive files must be redacted prior to re-entering agent context, traces, and log streams [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].
- **Host Credential Protection**: Runtime hooks must enforce deny rules against host credentials (such as SSH keys, cloud tokens, and browser session files) and mandate short-lived credential issuance to mitigate sandbox escapes [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33].

## Policy Enforcement: In-Loop Hooks vs. Gateways
While centralized MCP gateways provide authentication, payload logging, and routing for remote servers, complete policy enforcement requires execution within the agent loop [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30]:
- **In-Loop Policy Hooks**: In-loop hooks intercept all tool invocations—including `stdio` transports, local shell commands, SDK calls, and framework connectors—with full visibility into prompt context and intention [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].
- **Gateway Boundary Checkpoints**: Remote gateways act as network checkpoints and central audit logging points that feed into in-loop policy engines [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30].

## Approval Fatigue Mitigations
Human-in-the-loop authorization gates degrade in efficacy under repetitive prompts, where high baseline approval rates lead human reviewers to rubber-stamp requests [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35]. Automated policy checks and tiered approval gates mitigate reviewer fatigue and prevent critical bypasses [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

# Lifecycle History
- Initial draft deliverables and threat models established under the Security and Privacy Working Group.
- Open issue proposals expanded secret audit scope, in-loop hook architectural placement, and fatigue empirical metrics [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-30] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-33] [^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-35].

proposed_concept.title: Single-Agent Human Approval Architecture
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture establishing an enforceable human approval gate between an agent proposal and downstream execution.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Single-Agent Human Approval architecture defines an execution pattern wherein an autonomous agent produces an immutable proposal that must receive verified human authorization prior to triggering side-effecting operations.

# Architecture / Specification

## Boundary Isolation and Executor Decoupling
The architecture enforces authorization boundaries by separating proposal generation from action execution:
- **Proposal-Execution Split**: Decoupling the proposal engine from the execution handler guarantees that sensitive tools cannot execute without passing an explicit approval checkpoint [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].
- **Durable Waits and Context Cache**: When approval involves extended delay ([../patterns/durable-wait.md](../patterns/durable-wait.md)), spawning a clean executor process avoids stale cache states while requiring minimal context reconstruction [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].
- **Critique Separation**: Multi-session separation allows independent verification or critique workflows prior to human sign-off [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

# Lifecycle History
- Draft reference architecture established within the Workflows and Process Integration Working Group.
- Open issue feedback highlighted execution decoupling tradeoffs and context rebuilding considerations [^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-issue-45].

proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agent Behavior Trace Model defines telemetry conventions, turn boundaries, and causal trace schemas for agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]

Rather than introducing a distinct competing trace protocol, recent working group alignment reframes the initiative around identifying semantic inconsistencies across agent SDK implementations and standardizing upstream conformance profiles for [OpenTelemetry](../resources/opentelemetry.md).[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]

# Architecture / Specification
## Telemetry and Conformance Focus
Agent frameworks frequently implement OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes inconsistently across multi-turn reasoning loops, tool dispatches, and subagent invocations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]

The behavior trace effort focuses on:
- **Semantic Gap Identification**: Cataloging variances in how disparate agent SDKs capture turn boundaries, prompts, completions, and error states.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]
- **Upstream OpenTelemetry Contributions**: Driving semantic attribute harmonizations directly into OpenTelemetry semantic conventions rather than establishing a divergent format.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]
- **Conformance Framework**: Providing a vendor-neutral test suite to validate that runtime SDKs produce coherent, semantically uniform distributed traces.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-09-30: [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) reframed the behavior trace model deliverable to focus on resolving OpenTelemetry semantic gaps and publishing an upstream conformance framework.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-fc392a405330-7a0995cd]

proposed_concept.title: Identity and Trust Working Group
proposed_concept.description: AAIF working group advancing vendor-neutral standards, reference architectures, and trust models for agent identity, delegation, and attestation.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Identity and Trust Working Group establishes open specifications, reference architectures, and interoperable trust frameworks for agent identification, credential delegation, and cryptographic execution attestation.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]

# Architecture / Specification
## Attestation Component Decomposition
Technical discussions in the working group decompose runtime attestation into three distinct reference architecture components to accommodate multi-platform confidential execution nuances:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]

1. **Platform Evidence**: Signed hardware or firmware reports and endorsement chains (e.g., AMD SEV-SNP via `/dev/sev-guest`, Azure confidential VM paravisor claims, NVIDIA H100 GPU reports) proving the exact physical environment and launch measurements.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]
2. **Identity Binding**: Signed statements binding an agent's cryptographic identity document or key to platform measurements through platform-specific fields such as `REPORT_DATA`, paravisor runtime claims `user-data`, or TPM quote `qualifyingData`.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]
3. **Appraisal**: The relying party verification logic producing an authoritative trust verdict by evaluating received evidence and bindings against organizational policy rules.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]

This separation interfaces with isolation patterns defined by the [Security and Privacy Working Group](../working-groups/security-and-privacy.md), such as the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md).[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-09: Architecture proposal submitted to subdivide the unified attestation component into explicit platform evidence, identity binding, and appraisal stages across SEV-SNP, TDX, and GPU environments.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-12]

proposed_concept.title: Agentic AI Security Best Practices
proposed_concept.description: Technical guidance consolidating practical security controls across secrets elimination, in-loop policy enforcement, and execution sandbox boundaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
The Agentic AI Security Best Practices guide establishes defensive patterns, operational constraints, and risk management strategies for running autonomous agents across developer tools, enterprise workflows, and cloud environments.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]

# Architecture / Specification
## Sandbox Scope and Containment Boundaries
While sandbox execution modes restrict an agent's local filesystem modifications to designated working directories, security analysis highlights critical containment boundaries that sandboxing alone does not resolve:[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]

- **Egress and Data Exfiltration**: Blocking local shell utilities (such as `curl`) does not prevent exfiltration if the agent runtime retains unrestricted network access via language standard libraries (such as Python `urllib`) to complete tasks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]
- **Host Tool Trust Handoffs**: Artifacts written by a sandboxed agent into working directories can trigger execution escapes if subsequent host-level, unsandboxed developer tools or pipelines automatically execute them without secondary acceptance checks.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]
- **Layered Defense Mandate**: Sandboxing filesystem access must be coupled with strict outbound network controls and runtime enforcement patterns like the [Attested Isolated Runtime](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md) rather than treated as an absolute containment barrier.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]

# Lifecycle History
- 2026-09: Security reviews clarified blast-radius limitations of client-side sandbox modes regarding network egress and host execution handoffs.[^evt-wg-security-and-privacy-issue-34]

proposed_concept.title: Cross-Boundary Observability Model
proposed_concept.description: Three-layer coordination model analyzing telemetry propagation, context hand-offs, and observability gaps across LLM primitives, protocols, and infrastructure.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

The Cross-Boundary Observability Model is a coordination framework developed by the [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) to systematically identify and analyze telemetry gaps across execution boundaries in agentic systems.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a] Rather than acting as a standalone telemetry wire protocol, the model serves as an analytical map for evaluating how existing specifications and runtimes handle identity propagation, delegation chains, context preservation, and lifecycle tracking across heterogeneous boundaries.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25]

Current observability tooling frequently isolates insights to single execution layers, creating operational blind spots during inter-agent hand-offs, protocol negotiation failures, and cross-runtime delegations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]

# Architecture / Specification

The model organizes observability gap analysis across three distinct structural layers:[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]

1. **LLM Primitive Layer**: Encompasses core cognitive and execution primitives including agents, skills, tools, models, and memory stores.
2. **Protocol Boundary Layer**: Captures interaction patterns and transport-level transactions across discovery, negotiation, request/response cycles, delegation hand-offs, streaming channels, cancellation signals, and structured error handling, as seen in interfaces such as [Agent-to-MCP boundaries](../resources/agent-mcp-server-boundary.md) and [Agent-to-CLI boundaries](../resources/agent-tool-cli-boundary.md).
3. **Infrastructure Boundary Layer**: Governs underlying platform execution substrates, API gateways, execution runtimes, containerized microservices, and network topologies.

By categorizing system interactions across these layers, working groups evaluate whether distributed context tokens, provenance data, and authorization metadata successfully transit boundaries without truncation or loss of causal linkage.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-566afac466bc-889ed18a]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-25**: First draft of the cross-boundary observability model merged as a working document to guide WG gap analysis and upstream recommendations.[^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-pr-25]

mutations.rationale: Introduces the two-axis evidence-strength appraisal vocabulary for agent identity, authorization, and consent claims proposed in the Identity & Trust WG.

proposed_concept.title: Evidence-Strength Labels
proposed_concept.description: Two-axis appraisal vocabulary categorizing identity, delegation, and consent claims by assertion source, chain composition, and verification depth.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Evidence-Strength Labels are a vendor-neutral appraisal vocabulary developed within the [Identity and Trust Working Group](../working-groups/identity-and-trust.md) to characterize how independently claims regarding agent identity, provenance, delegation, and consent have been verified.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5] The taxonomy replaces binary present/absent checks with a multi-dimensional grading model generated by a relying party verifier during appraisal, distinguishing self-asserted statements from independently corroborated and cryptographically anchored claims.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]

Under this model, evidence labels are an appraisal finding produced by the verifier reflecting the actual verification depth executed, rather than self-graded assertions embedded directly within credentials.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]

# Architecture / Specification

The vocabulary decouples appraisal into two distinct structural axes and an orthogonal freshness dimension:[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]

### Axis A: Assertion Origin (Who Asserts)
- **Declared**: The agent or its operator asserts the claim directly without independent validation.
- **Platform-attested**: The claim is vouched for by the underlying runtime, hosting platform, or execution service (e.g., [attested isolated runtimes](../patterns/attested-isolated-runtime.md)).
- **Corroborated**: An external, independent entity (such as an identity provider, merchant, or counterparty) independently validates the claim.

### Axis B: Chain Structure (How the Chain is Built)
- **Composed**: Multiple discrete attestations are bound together into a single verifiable claim (e.g., identity coupled with delegation hops and human consent). Chains are subject to the weakest-hop rule, reflecting the lowest verified hop in the sequence.
- **Anchored**: The verification chain terminates in an immutable root of trust directly verifiable by the relying party (such as a DID document, signed mandate, or hardware/CA root).

### Freshness and Revocation Dimension
Freshness, revocation status, and credential expiry are evaluated as an orthogonal dimension separate from chain depth. Verifiers evaluate real-time revocation stores and fail closed when status information is unreachable, rather than rounding up appraisal scores.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08-28**: Proposal introduced in Issue #5 of the Identity & Trust WG establishing the two-axis model aligned with RFC 9334 (RATS) and NIST SP 800-63 principles.[^evt-wg-identity-and-trust-issue-5]

proposed_concept.title: Workflow Primitives
proposed_concept.description: Standardized vocabulary of modular workflow building blocks, boundary contracts, and handoff specifications for single- and multi-agent reference architectures.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview

Workflow Primitives are the standardized, modular building blocks defined by the [Workflows and Process Integration Working Group](../working-groups/workflows-and-process-integration.md) to compose reliable single-agent and multi-agent systems.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29] Designated across catalog series (P1 through P19), these primitives define discrete functional roles such as Triggers, AgentSteps, Budgets, and Handoffs, enabling formal composition according to foundational [workflow architecture principles](../guidelines/workflow-architecture-principles.md).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54]

Each primitive crossing is governed by rigorous interface contracts to enforce predictable execution, state continuity, and policy compliance across system boundaries.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]

# Architecture / Specification

The primitive framework standardizes workflow mechanics across reference architectures, including [single-agent human approval architectures](../architectures/single-agent-human-approval.md) and multi-agent topology patterns (T1–T6):[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54]

- **Primitive Vocabulary (P1–P19)**: Identifies atomic workflow components including invocation triggers, autonomous agent steps, constraint evaluators, budget limits, human intervention gates, and delegation handoffs.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]
- **AgentStep Boundary Contracts**: Defines deterministic input/output schemas and execution invariants required whenever an agent step is executed.
- **Handoff Contracts**: Specifies state transfer, context propagation, and authorization invariants required when transferring execution responsibility between autonomous agents or between agents and human operators.[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29]

# Lifecycle History

- **2026-08**: Workflows & Process Integration WG introduced the primitive-based architecture drafts and supporting contracts (PR #29, PR #54).[^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-29][^evt-wg-workflows-and-process-integration-pr-54]

mutations.rationale: Score-P MPI/OpenMP tracing reference architecture merged in wg-observability-and-traceability.

proposed_concept.title: MPI and OpenMP Unified Tracing
proposed_concept.description: Reference architecture for unified HPC tracing of MPI inter-process communication and OpenMP threading via PMPI, OMPT, and Score-P OTF2 binaries.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
MPI/OpenMP tracing provides standardized performance profiling across distributed high-performance computing (HPC) nodes and multi-threaded shared memory processes [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0335a90fd535-bebc1711]. By combining PMPI interposition for message passing and OMPT callbacks for shared-memory parallelism, tools like Score-P unify instrumentation into Open Trace Format 2 (OTF2) binary streams and CUBE profile summaries [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0335a90fd535-bebc1711].

# Architecture / Specification
The tracing architecture spans multiple layers of the parallel execution stack [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0335a90fd535-bebc1711]:
- **PMPI Interposition**: Intercepts MPI calls (`MPI_Send`, `MPI_Recv`, `MPI_Allreduce`, `MPI_Barrier`) via link-time symbol wrapping to measure inter-process communication latencies and transfer volumes.
- **OMPT Callbacks**: Hooks into OpenMP runtime thread events (`ompt_callback_parallel_begin`, `ompt_callback_task_create`, `ompt_callback_work`) without requiring compiler source modifications.
- **Score-P Measurement Core**: Unifies PMPI and OMPT events into process-local lock-free memory buffers, correlating distributed timestamps across nodes.
- **OTF2 & CUBE Formats**: Persists event traces to disk in binary OTF2 format or aggregates performance metrics into CUBE hierarchy files for analysis in Scalasca and Vampir [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0335a90fd535-bebc1711].

This architecture integrates into agentic infrastructure alongside GPU profiling systems such as [AMD ROCprofiler](../resources/amd-rocprofiler.md) and [NVIDIA Nsight](../resources/nvidia-nsight.md) as part of the broader [Observability and Traceability Working Group](../working-groups/observability-and-traceability.md) landscape [^evt-wg-observability-and-traceability-file-0335a90fd535-bebc1711].

proposed_concept.title: OpenEnv
proposed_concept.description: Unified execution environment framework for agentic reinforcement learning exposing Gymnasium-style APIs and MCP tool interfaces.
proposed_concept.body:
# Overview
OpenEnv is an open-source framework for creating, containerizing, and orchestrating isolated execution environments for agentic reinforcement learning (RL) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]. It provides Gymnasium-style lifecycle primitives (`reset`, `step`, `state`) while exposing environment tools to agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].

# Architecture / Specification
OpenEnv resolves tooling fragmentation across RL post-training stacks by standardizing the interface between models, environments, and harnesses [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50]:
- **Gymnasium-Style API**: Exposes standard episode lifecycle controls for trainers, handling environment resets, step transitions, observation state capture, and reward calculation [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **MCP Tool Interface**: Uses MCP as the model-to-environment interaction layer, ensuring agent tools used in training mirror those available in production deployment [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **Containerized Packaging**: Encapsulates environments within OCI containers distributed via Hugging Face Hub, enabling portable execution across local runtimes, cloud sandboxes (such as Modal, Daytona, and Azure Container Apps), and distributed RL training harnesses [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
- **Agent Harness Integration**: Provides adapter patterns (such as RFC 005) enabling coding agents like [Goose](../resources/goose.md) to undergo RL training within isolated environments while retaining their internal control loops [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].

# Lifecycle History
OpenEnv was initially developed in October 2025 as a joint initiative between Hugging Face and Meta-PyTorch, transitioning to multi-vendor Technical Committee stewardship under Hugging Face in June 2026 before being proposed for AAIF hosting in 2026 [^evt-project-proposals-issue-50].
